The Power Authority may not charge residential customers any penalty fee on overdue accounts. Under the Power Authority's rules a bill is delinquent if not paid by its due date, and after notice the Authority may cut off electricity or water; a water customer 180 or more days in arrears may have the water facilities removed, and service is not reconnected until arrears and reconnection fees are paid. On your side, never cut off or interrupt service yourself to pressure a tenant; possession comes back only through the courts (`edu-utility-interruption-submeter-as`).

title: Shifting Upkeep Duties to the Tenant in American Samoa
bodyText: American Samoa has no minimum-standards or landlord-tenant statute listing your maintenance duties or saying which may be moved to a tenant; we found none, so most allocations are left to the lease (`edu-no-tenant-repair-agreement-rule-as`). One rule does let you shift a named duty, on a condition. Under the solid-waste rules, when a dwelling is rented, the owner who must prepare and put out solid waste for collection is the person to whom the rent is payable, that is, you. The occupant may be made responsible instead only if you and the tenant agree and the licensed collector is notified in writing, with the notice signed by both of you. Use the American Samoa clause (`garbage-setout-as`) and send the signed notice. Duties the law puts on every owner, lessee or occupant, such as the rodent and garbage-accumulation duties, bind both of you whatever the lease says. Where several dwelling units are licensed to provide lodging for hire, the solid-waste rules treat the property as a business that must arrange for collection of all its solid waste.

title: Smoke and Carbon Monoxide Alarms in American Samoa
bodyText: No American Samoa statute or regulation we searched requires a residential landlord to install or maintain smoke or carbon monoxide alarms, or gives the tenant a duty to test them, and we found no fire code for dwellings. The territory adopted the 1964 Uniform Building Code (Short Form) for buildings, but the code book itself was not in the sources we searched, so we could not check what, if anything, it requires for alarms. The cautious course is to install working smoke alarms outside sleeping areas and on each level, add a carbon monoxide alarm where there is a fuel-burning appliance such as a gas stove, test them at move-in, and have the lease ask the tenant to test them and report problems. Whether failing to do so could make you liable after a fire rests on the common law (case law not searched).

title: Alternate Housing During Repairs
bodyText: No American Samoa statute, regulation or court rule requires you to provide or pay for alternate housing while a rental is repaired or after a cyclone, fire or other casualty, whether or not the tenant asks; we found none. If the home cannot be lived in because of your breach, a tenant sued for unpaid rent can raise that breach as a defence, and the court deducts the rent it finds excused, so don't charge rent for a period the home is unusable through your fault. Two government programs touch displaced tenants. When the government acquires a dwelling for a federally assisted public project, it may pay relocation assistance to a tenant who lawfully lived there at least 90 days. In a declared disaster emergency the Governor may arrange temporary emergency housing and may commandeer private property, with compensation only where its use was ordered. Say in the lease what happens to rent if the home is damaged and can't be lived in.

title: Appliances You Leave but Will Not Maintain
bodyText: No American Samoa statute, regulation or court rule presumes that appliances left in a rental are yours to maintain, or lists appliances you may not exclude; we found none. So you may use the optional clause listing items you leave but will not repair (`appliances-excluded-la`), and you should, because without a lease term the question turns on the common law (case law not searched). Keep its limit: never exclude something whose failure could seriously affect health or safety, such as a gas appliance or water heater. The water utility may refuse or cut off water or wastewater service to premises where water-using appliances or equipment are dangerous, unsafe or not in conformity with laws or regulations, and pumps, tanks, filters and other connections between the water meter and the outlets are the utility customer's sole responsibility, so an excluded item can still cost you service.

title: Appliances You Supply
bodyText: No American Samoa statute, regulation or court rule lists appliances a landlord must furnish, such as a stove, refrigerator or air conditioner, or sets how you must maintain the ones you do; we found none. The shared clause listing the appliances you supply (`appliances-included`) works as written, and listing them matters: what the lease promises is what you must keep up, and a breach of the lease that excuses rent can be raised as a defence in a repossession case for nonpayment and deducted from the rent. Water-using equipment that is dangerous, unsafe or not in conformity with laws or regulations can lead the utility to refuse or cut off water to the premises.

title: Common-Area Lighting in American Samoa
bodyText: No American Samoa statute or regulation we searched requires lighting in the halls, stairs or other common areas of a rental building, or says whether a tenant may be made to pay for common-area lights wired to the tenant's own electric service; we found none. The 1964 Uniform Building Code the territory adopted was not in the sources we searched, so any lighting rule in it was not checked. In a building with several tenants the electric rules give each tenant its own meter, so wire common-area lights to a house meter in your name rather than to a tenant's service. Keep halls, stairs and entrances lit at night; your exposure if someone is hurt in a dark common area rests on the common law (case law not searched).

title: Rent After a Closing or Unsafe-Building Order
bodyText: No American Samoa statute, regulation or court rule expressly bars you from collecting rent after a building is ordered closed, evacuated or torn down; we found none. But several government orders can end the tenant's use of the home. If a building is so dilapidated as to be unsafe and dangerous, the owner must tear it down within 30 days after the Governor's written notice. The Department of Health may order a property that is a nuisance closed and evacuated, and in a declared public health emergency may close and compel evacuation of a facility. A quarantine placard bars anyone from entering or leaving the premises except as authorized, and in a disaster emergency the Governor may compel evacuation and control the occupancy of premises. Don't charge rent for a period when the tenant can't lawfully use the home because of a condition you are responsible for: a breach that excuses rent is a defence to a repossession case for nonpayment, and the court deducts the excused rent.

title: Habitability: What American Samoa Has and Lacks
bodyText: How American Samoa compares on habitability features found elsewhere. Absent (we found no statute, regulation or court rule): a housing code or statutory warranty of habitability for private rentals; a list of required conditions such as heat, hot water, alarms or lighting; a non-waiver rule; repair deadlines; repair-and-deduct; rent withholding, abatement or escrow; and statutory tenant damages or attorney's fees. Present: in a repossession case for unpaid rent, your breach of the lease that excuses rent is a defence, and the court deducts the excused rent; either side may join claims for breach of the lease; a termination intended primarily as retribution for the tenant's lawful act is a defence; every owner, lessee or occupant has rodent and sanitation duties; the Department of Health may order a nuisance (anything that endangers life or health) abated at the owner's expense; and an unsafe, dilapidated building must be torn down on the Governor's notice. The territory adopted the 1964 Uniform Building Code, which we did not read. Beyond these, your repair duties come from the lease and the common law (case law not searched).

title: How Serious a Defect Must Be
bodyText: No American Samoa statute sets a materiality threshold for a tenant's habitability claim or lists which defects count, because the territory has no habitability statute; we found none. The tests that do exist are general. In a repossession case for unpaid rent, the question is whether you committed a breach of the lease that excuses the payment of rent, and the court deducts the portion it finds excused, so what the lease promises sets the yardstick. Public-law yardsticks: a public health nuisance is anything that endangers life or health, which the Department of Health can order you to correct; and a building so dilapidated as to be unsafe and dangerous must be torn down on the Governor's notice. How serious a breach must be to excuse rent is a common-law question (case law not searched), so treat any defect that affects health, safety or the basic use of the home as serious and fix it promptly.

title: Can a Lease Change Repair Duties?
bodyText: No American Samoa statute says whether a lease may waive or modify a landlord's repair or habitability duties, because there is no statutory habitability duty to waive; we found none. Three limits apply anyway. Public-law duties, such as the rodent and sanitation duties on every owner, lessee or occupant, nuisance orders issued to the owner and the unsafe-building rule, bind you whatever the lease says. The tenant's defences in a repossession case, including that your breach excused the rent and that the termination was retaliation, come from statute, and no statute allows the lease to waive them, so don't try. And if the Consumer Protection Act reaches residential leases, which is unsettled, a court could strike or limit an unconscionable clause, for example one that is excessively one-sided. The one duty the rules expressly let you shift is putting garbage out for collection (`garbage-setout-as`).

title: No Presumption of Repair Breach
bodyText: No American Samoa statute or court rule presumes that a landlord breached a repair or habitability duty, or took too long to repair, from a health order, a government notice or the passage of time, and none sets a repair deadline running from a tenant's request; we found none. In a repossession case the tenant who claims your breach excused the rent must establish it, and so must a tenant claiming retaliation. The only fixed periods are in public enforcement: a Department of Health nuisance order sets a reasonable time to abate, the Director may abate a nuisance at the owner's expense 10 days after written notice, and an unsafe building must come down within 30 days after the Governor's notice. Keep dated records of repair requests and what you did.

title: No Required Habitability Statement
bodyText: No American Samoa statute requires a residential lease to state that the home will be delivered or kept fit for habitation; we found none. What the lease does say matters, though: with no habitability statute, your repair promises in the lease are the main measure of your duty, and a breach of them that excuses rent is a defence to a repossession case for unpaid rent, with the excused rent deducted. The shared maintenance clause (`landlord-maintenance`) states those promises; use it as written and keep it realistic. Public-law duties apply whatever the lease says (`edu-landlord-maintenance-as`).

title: Tenant Remedies When You Breach
bodyText: American Samoa gives a residential tenant no statutory right to end the lease after notice, to repair and deduct, to withhold or escrow rent, or to recover statutory damages or attorney's fees when you breach; we found none. What the statutes do give the tenant is defensive. If you sue for possession for unpaid rent, your breach of the lease that excuses the payment of rent is a defence, and in any judgment the court deducts the rent it finds excused; a termination intended primarily as retribution for the tenant's lawful act, or an attempt to raise the tenant's obligations as a penalty for one, also defeats possession. Either side may join money claims for breach of the lease in the possession case. Beyond that, a tenant's remedies (damages or ending the lease for a serious breach) rest on the lease and the common law (case law not searched). These defences apply to every tenancy, and no statute lets a lease waive them, so treat them as beyond the lease's reach (case law not searched).

title: Your Upkeep Duties in American Samoa
bodyText: No American Samoa statute or regulation sets a general repair or habitability duty for private residential landlords; we found none, so the shared Maintenance & Repairs clause (`landlord-maintenance`) is what defines your repair duty, and the tenant can hold you to it as a defence and counterclaim in a repossession case (`edu-landlord-breach-remedy-as`). Use it as written. Several public-law duties fall on you as owner whatever the lease says: the rodent, garbage and weed duties on every owner, lessee or occupant of an occupied building, and keeping an unoccupied building and its grounds clean; Department of Health orders to correct a nuisance at the owner's expense, with the cost chargeable as a lien or collectible from rents if unpaid; tearing down a building that is unsafe and dangerous on the Governor's notice; installing plumbing or drainage equipment ordered to abate a plumbing nuisance; and inspecting any check valves or other backflow devices on the premises at least every three months. Water pipes, fixtures and equipment beyond the meter are the utility customer's responsibility, so they are yours if the water account is in your name. Putting garbage out for collection is also your duty unless shifted (`garbage-setout-as`).

title: Who Makes Repairs
bodyText: No American Samoa statute lets a tenant make repairs at your expense, deduct repair costs from rent or withhold rent, so there is no statutory procedure for designating who does that work; we found none. A lease may name your repair contact and say the tenant will not make, or hire anyone to make, repairs at your expense without your written consent; the optional American Samoa clause does that (`designated-repairer-as`). One rule governs who may do paid work: anyone who for pay undertakes to build, alter, repair or improve a building must hold a contractor's license, except maintenance staff regularly employed to do casual, isolated or incidental repairs. Use licensed contractors for anything beyond small repairs. A consent clause doesn't remove the tenant's defence that your breach of the lease excused the rent.

title: Disability Accommodations in American Samoa Rentals
bodyText: American Samoa has no general territorial law on disability in housing; its one territorial rule is that a person who tests HIV positive may not be denied housing because of it (`edu-fair-housing-as`). The federal Fair Housing Act reaches the territory and sets the rules. You may not refuse to rent to, or set different terms for, a person because of a disability of that person, anyone who will live with them, or anyone associated with them. You must allow reasonable modifications of the home, at the tenant's expense, that are necessary for full enjoyment of it; in a rental you may, where reasonable, require the tenant to agree to restore the interior at the end, reasonable wear and tear excepted. You must make reasonable accommodations in your rules, policies, practices and services when they are necessary to give a disabled person equal opportunity to use and enjoy the home, for example allowing an assistance animal despite a no-pets rule. Multifamily buildings first occupied after March 1991 must meet the Act's accessible design rules. A narrow exemption covers some owners renting a single-family house without a broker or rooms in an owner-occupied building of four units or fewer, but never the advertising ban.

title: Renting the Same Home or Room Twice
bodyText: No American Samoa statute forbids letting part of a room to more than one household, or says what happens if the same home is leased to two tenants for the same period; we found none. Between competing tenants, the answer turns on the common law and on registration (case law not searched): a written lease is an instrument that does not pass an interest in the land until registered with the Territorial Registrar, and due registration gives notice of it to everyone who deals with the land afterwards. Register your written leases, never sign a second lease for a period already let, and if it happens, expect to answer to the tenant who loses for breach of the lease.

title: Screening Staff Who Enter Units
bodyText: No American Samoa statute or regulation requires you to run background checks on employees, managers or contractors who have access to tenants' homes, or sets standards for doing so; we found none, and we found no real estate broker or property-manager licensing law. Related rules: anyone who for pay undertakes to repair or alter a building must hold a contractor's license (regular maintenance staff doing casual or incidental repairs excepted), and a business, including property management, needs a business license. The territory keeps a public sex offender registry website you can check. Screen staff with keys carefully, keep keys controlled, and give tenants notice before entry as your lease provides.

title: Public Health Rules for American Samoa Rentals
bodyText: American Samoa has no health districts or local boards of health, and no statute or regulation requires you to give tenants health regulations on request or to refer them to a health office; we found none. Health oversight is territory-wide through the Department of Health. The Director may inspect public and private buildings at reasonable hours and order a public health nuisance (anything that endangers life or health) abated; department staff may enter a property with the owner's, custodian's or occupant's consent, or with an administrative search warrant if refused. Unabated nuisance costs can be charged to the owner as a lien or collected from rents (`edu-municipal-utility-lien-as`). Cooperate with inspections and keep records of the repairs you make.

title: Heating: Not Applicable in American Samoa
bodyText: Not applicable in American Samoa. The territory's tropical climate has no heating season, and no American Samoa statute, regulation or court rule requires a landlord to supply heat or hot water, sets a minimum or maximum indoor temperature, or makes air conditioning an essential service; we found none. So the heating rules found elsewhere, including rules on shifting heat costs to a tenant, do not apply. If you supply air conditioning or a water heater, list it in the lease (`appliances-included`) and keep it working as the lease promises, since a breach that excuses rent is a defence in a repossession case for nonpayment.

title: Facilities You Must Provide in American Samoa
bodyText: We found no American Samoa statute, regulation or court rule that lists the facilities a landlord must supply in a rental home, such as a kitchen, toilet, hot water, screens, a stove or a refrigerator, so the lease sets what you provide; list every facility and appliance in it. A few territorial rules still reach you as owner. Pumps, tanks, filters and other connections on the water line between the utility's meter and the outlets are the utility customer's responsibility to install and maintain, not the utility's, so say in the lease who keeps them up if the tenant holds the account; and the owner of premises with check valves or other backflow devices must inspect them at least every three months. Every owner, lessee or occupant of an occupied building must keep it and its surroundings free of garbage and rodent harborage, and setting out household garbage for collection is the duty of the person to whom rent is paid unless you and the tenant shift it by a signed notice to the collector (`garbage-setout-as`). New buildings are built under the 1964 Uniform Building Code and inspected for safety on completion; that code's text is not published with the territorial Code and we did not review it, so ask the Department of Public Works what it requires before you build or convert a dwelling.

title: Promises to Repair in American Samoa
bodyText: We found no American Samoa statute, regulation or court rule requiring a landlord's promise to clean, repair or improve a rental to be in writing, to carry a completion date, or to be made before the lease is signed. Whether an oral or pre-lease promise binds you is a question for the common law of contracts the territory's courts apply (case law not searched). Put every such promise in the lease or a signed addendum with a completion date anyway. If a promise that is part of the lease goes unperformed and the breach excuses rent, the tenant can defeat a possession case for nonpayment, and the court deducts the excused rent from the amount it finds owing. The territory's Consumer Protection Act also treats a false promise, or a false claim that something was supplied as promised, as deceptive; whether that Act reaches a residential lease is unsettled, so promise only work you will do.

title: Quiet Possession in American Samoa
bodyText: We found no American Samoa statute that writes a covenant of quiet possession or quiet enjoyment into a lease. The territory applies the common law of England so far as it suits local conditions, and the common law generally implies that covenant in a lease (case law not searched), so assume your tenant has it. The statutes protect the tenant's possession in other ways: no one may enter premises unless the entry is permitted by law, and even then only peaceably, never by force, and you recover possession only through a court case (normally the summary procedure). If your breach of the lease excuses rent, the tenant can raise it against a nonpayment case. Keep your own entries, and those of your workers and agents, to what the lease's access terms allow.

title: Rent Collection and Repair Duties in American Samoa
bodyText: Some states say that whoever collects the rent keeps the landlord's repair duties, whatever a lease, assignment, deed or mortgage says. We found no American Samoa statute, regulation or court rule like that, and no statutory habitability duty for it to protect. Two territorial rules do follow the rent. Under the solid-waste rules, when a dwelling is rented, the owner responsible for setting out its garbage is the person to whom the rent is payable. And if the Department of Health abates a public health nuisance on a property and the person responsible will not repay the cost, the department may collect it from rents paid on the property under a court order, or as a lien on the property. If you hand rent collection to a manager or assign rents to a lender, say in that agreement who handles repairs, garbage and health orders.

title: Government Inspections of Rentals in American Samoa
bodyText: American Samoa has no rental licensing, registration or periodic inspection program; we found none. Government inspectors can still come. The Department of Health may enter a property, with the consent of the owner, custodian or occupant, to check compliance with the health laws, and if refused may seek an administrative search warrant; the Director of Health may inspect public and private buildings at reasonable hours; the village pulenuu inspects his village for sanitation; and the Power Authority may enter a customer's premises at all reasonable times for purposes connected with its water, wastewater or electric service. No statute says whether a lease can give the tenant's consent to an inspector in advance, and the Revised Constitution protects houses against unreasonable searches, so do not rely on a lease clause to make a tenant admit an inspector: ask the tenant's consent each time, or leave it to the inspector to get a warrant. You can still agree in the lease that the tenant will cooperate with lawful inspections and let you in on notice to fix what an inspector finds.

title: No Repair Escrow or Exemption Notice in American Samoa
bodyText: Some states let tenants pay rent into an escrow account while repairs are outstanding, and exempt certain landlords who give a notice. We found no American Samoa statute, regulation or court rule creating a rent escrow for repairs, so there is no exemption and no exemption notice for you to give. A tenant's repair complaint reaches you instead as a defence in a possession case: rent that your breach of the lease excuses is deducted from what the court finds owing (`edu-tenant-repair-remedies-as`).

title: Repair Requests in American Samoa
bodyText: We found no American Samoa statute, regulation or court rule on how a tenant must ask for repairs or how fast you must respond, so the lease sets the method. You may ask for repair requests in writing, but no statute says that a verbal request waives written notice, or that a written-notice term limits the tenant's defences. The tenant's main defence in a nonpayment case, that your breach of the lease excuses rent, turns on the breach rather than on how the tenant told you, and whether a written-notice term could defeat it is unsettled (case law not searched). Cautious course: name the method you prefer, but act on and keep a record of every repair request however it arrives. Going the other way, if a tenant causes a serious and continuing health hazard or extensive and continuing damage, your written demand must state its reasons and the time to put things right, and the tenant then has 7 days to restore or repair before you can sue for possession.

title: Locks and Security Devices in American Samoa
bodyText: We found no American Samoa statute, regulation or court rule requiring a landlord to install locks, deadbolts, door viewers or other security devices, or to rekey or change locks between tenants. The lease decides what you provide, so say in it which locks and keys the tenant gets. Changing or rekeying locks between tenants is still sensible practice. If you keep a key, enter only as the lease allows, and never use a lock change to keep a tenant out: entry must be permitted by law and peaceable, and you recover possession only through a court case (normally the summary procedure).

title: Staff Screening in Housing for Older Persons
bodyText: We found no American Samoa statute, regulation or court rule requiring staff of housing for older persons to hold work cards or pass background checks. If you run housing reserved for older persons, the federal Fair Housing Act, which applies in American Samoa, sets the conditions for exemption from its familial-status rules: for housing for persons 55 and older, at least 80 percent of occupied units must have at least one occupant 55 or older, and you must publish and follow policies showing that intent and verify occupancy. Meet those conditions before you turn away families with children.

title: Services and Utilities You Provide in American Samoa
bodyText: No American Samoa statute requires a landlord to provide any particular service or utility, so your lease decides, and the shared Services and Utilities clause (`services-utilities-provided-ks-oh`) works as written. When it says you provide what applicable law requires, the territorial rules that matter are few: equipment on the water line beyond the meter is the utility customer's, not the utility's, to install and maintain, setting out garbage is the duty of the person to whom rent is paid unless you shift it (`garbage-setout-as`), and in a building with several tenants the electric rules give each tenant its own meter as a customer of the Power Authority (`edu-utilities-responsibility-as`). Name every service you will provide, and how often, in the lease. Never stop a service you provide to pressure a tenant; possession comes back only through a court case (normally the summary procedure).

title: Stoves and Refrigerators in American Samoa
bodyText: We found no American Samoa statute, regulation or court rule requiring a landlord to supply a stove, refrigerator or other appliance, or setting who must repair one you supply. The lease decides, so list the appliances you provide and say who maintains and replaces them. One criminal rule matters when you replace an appliance: leaving a discarded refrigerator or icebox with a latching door where children can reach it, on premises you control, is a misdemeanor unless you first remove the door, hinges or latch.

title: Health and Safety Orders on Rental Property in American Samoa
bodyText: American Samoa has no rental receivership and no housing code-enforcement program; we found none. Two government powers can still reach a run-down rental. The Department of Health may order you to correct or remove a public health nuisance within a set time, including by closing or evacuating a building; if you do not, it may do the work at the owner's or occupant's expense and recover the cost as a lien on the property, from rents paid on the property under a court order, or like a tax, and keeping a nuisance after 10 days' written notice is a misdemeanor. Separately, the Governor may order the owner of a building so dilapidated that it is unsafe and dangerous to tear it down within 30 days. A tenant or other occupant who caused or permitted a nuisance is liable to you for what you pay. Act on any health notice at once, and tell your tenants if an order affects their occupancy.

title: Cable, Satellite and Internet Access in American Samoa
bodyText: We found no American Samoa statute, regulation or court rule giving tenants a right to cable, satellite or internet service, requiring you to let a provider wire your building, or barring different rent for subscribers. The territory's telecommunications rules bind carriers, not landlords. The lease decides whether a tenant may install a dish, antenna or new wiring; say what is allowed, where, and who restores the property at move-out. Federal rules on tenant antennas were not reviewed for this library.

title: Tenant Remedies for Unmade Repairs in American Samoa
bodyText: We found no American Samoa statute, regulation or court rule letting a tenant withhold rent, pay rent into escrow, or repair and deduct the cost from rent, and no statutory repair duty on landlords. A tenant's remedies come from the lease and the common law of contracts (case law not searched), and from the possession statute. If you sue for possession for nonpayment, the tenant can defeat the claim by showing you breached the lease in a way that excuses rent, and the court deducts the excused rent from the amount it finds owing; the tenant may also counterclaim for damages for your breach of the lease. Ending a tenancy mainly to punish a tenant for a lawful act, such as complaining about repairs, is also a defence. Make the repairs you promise, keep records, and do not file for unpaid rent while a real repair dispute is open without considering how much the court might excuse.

title: Paying Utilities for Your Tenant in American Samoa
bodyText: No American Samoa statute stops you from paying a tenant's utilities and including them in the rent, so the shared Utilities Paid by Landlord clause (`utilities-paid-by-landlord`) works as written. If you do, you are the utility's customer and answer to it for the bill. For water, several units under one management may share one connection with the Power Authority's permission, and the applicant then pays for all water supplied. For electricity, when a building is occupied by several customers each becomes a customer of the Power Authority with its own meter, and a customer may not supply another person or premises through its service without the Authority's approval, so check with the Authority before promising to pay electricity in a multi-unit building. Reselling electricity is unlawful; including it in a fixed rent is the cautious way to provide it, while charging tenants separately by meter or share may be treated as resale (unsettled, case law not searched). The current water rules have no resale ban. If your account falls behind, the utility treats it as a default on all your services and may cut off service to your tenants at all your locations at once.

title: Utility Allowances and Overage Charges in American Samoa
bodyText: We found no American Samoa statute, regulation or court rule on utility allowances, or on charging a tenant for usage above an allowance. The utility rules do matter: reselling electricity received from the utility is unlawful, a customer may not supply another person or premises through its service without the Power Authority's approval, and in a building with several tenants each tenant is to have its own electric meter as a customer of the Power Authority. Whether billing a tenant for the cost of electricity above an allowance counts as resale is unsettled (case law not searched). The current water rules have no resale ban, and we found no rule limiting a water allowance, so it rests on the lease. The cautious course for electricity is either to include it in a fixed rent, or to have the tenant open its own account with the utility, rather than reselling or recharging metered usage.

title: Sharing Utility Costs Among Tenants in American Samoa
bodyText: We found no American Samoa statute, regulation or court rule that sets how a landlord may divide a shared utility bill among tenants, or that makes a term charging tenants for utilities not separately metered unenforceable. The utility rules shape what you can do. Electricity in a building occupied by several customers is metered separately, and each occupant becomes the utility's customer. Water for several units under one management may come through separate meters or one shared connection, and with one connection you, as applicant, pay for all of it; a building with several units is on one water meter unless you ask, at your expense, for a meter per unit. Reselling electricity is unlawful, and whether dividing a shared electric bill among tenants is resale is unsettled (case law not searched). The current water rules have no resale ban, so dividing a shared water bill rests on the lease. Cautious course: install separate electric meters in the tenants' names, and either include shared water in the rent or state in the lease exactly how the water bill is divided.

title: Getting Notice of a Tenant's Utility Shutoff in American Samoa
bodyText: We found no American Samoa statute, regulation or court rule letting an owner arrange for the utility to tell it when a tenant's service is about to be disconnected, or letting a tenant name the landlord to receive copies of shutoff notices. Before cutting off a delinquent account, a public utility must give the consumer notice by first-class mail or by posting it in a conspicuous place on the structure where the account is metered, and service ends 10 working days after the postmark or posting. This matters to you, because the Power Authority's rules make a landlord co-sign the tenant's application or account transfer and hold the co-signer responsible for the tenant's past-due bills. You may still ask your tenant in the lease to tell you promptly of any disconnection notice, and you may see a posted notice on the building. You can also ask the Power Authority whether it will copy you, as co-signer, with the tenant's written consent.

title: When the Utility Account Is in Your Name
bodyText: If you keep the electric or water account for a rental in your name, the utility deals with you, not your tenant. We found no American Samoa statute giving tenants rights when a landlord's account falls behind: no right to pay and deduct, no receiver, and no notice to each unit before a building-wide shutoff. The termination statute protects the consumer who uses and is billed for the service: no cutoff of an account that is not delinquent without consent, and notice by mail or posting on the metered structure, with 10 working days before cutoff. Your own delinquency can reach your tenants hard: an account is delinquent if not paid by the bill's due date, default on any amount counts as a default on all your services, and after notice the utility may cut off electricity and water at all your locations and will not reconnect until arrears and reconnection fees are paid. A lapse in a service the lease says you provide may also be a breach that excuses rent in a nonpayment case. Keep landlord-held accounts current, and if one falls behind, tell your tenants at once. Accounts you co-signed for tenants also make you answerable for their past-due bills, so watch those too.

title: Utility Shutoff Rules in American Samoa
bodyText: American Samoa has a utility termination statute. A public utility may not cut off power, water or telephone service to a consumer whose account is not delinquent without consent; before cutting off a delinquent account it must send notice by first-class mail or post it on the structure where the account is metered, naming a contact person and stating in bold that service will end 10 working days later. A utility that cuts off service in violation must credit the consumer $25 plus $10 for each full day without service. The Power Authority may not charge residential customers penalty fees on overdue accounts. We found no seasonal, storm, emergency or medical limit on disconnection. These rules bind utilities, not you: never shut off, disconnect or interfere with a tenant's service yourself to force payment or possession; possession comes back only through a court case (normally the summary procedure), and tampering with another's property to cause inconvenience, or with a utility's property, is a crime (`edu-utility-service-continuity-as`).

title: Submetering and Utility Billing by Landlords in American Samoa
bodyText: We found no American Samoa statute, regulation or court rule setting disclosures, billing limits or other rules for a landlord who submeters or bills tenants for utilities. That is not permission for electricity: reselling electricity received from the utility is unlawful, a customer may not supply another person or premises through its service without the Power Authority's approval, and in a building with several tenants each tenant is to have its own electric meter as a customer of the Power Authority. Whether billing tenants for electricity by submeter or by share is resale is unsettled (case law not searched), so the cautious course is separate utility meters in the tenants' names, or electricity included in the rent. The current water rules have no resale ban; if one water connection serves several units, you as applicant pay for all of it, and the lease should state how tenants share the cost (`edu-utility-interruption-submeter-as`).

title: Transferring Utilities to the Tenant in American Samoa
bodyText: We found no American Samoa statute, regulation or court rule on moving utility accounts into a tenant's name, or letting a landlord cut off service the tenant fails to transfer. The Power Authority's rules do involve you: a landlord must co-sign the tenant's initial application or the transfer of an account, and as co-signer answers for the tenant's past-due bills. The customer on an electric account pays for all power through its meter until it ends service in writing and the utility finally terminates it. A water customer must give 30 days' notice to discontinue water and pays until that date (or, without notice, for 30 days after the utility learns it has vacated), and wastewater service cannot be voluntarily discontinued. So require in the lease that the tenant open accounts in its own name by a set date, and close or transfer your own accounts in writing, with notice, at the start and end of each tenancy. Do not close an account in your name to cut off an occupied unit to force the tenant's hand; that risks being treated as an unlawful lockout by other means (case law not searched); instead, claim what you paid as damages for the tenant's breach of the lease's transfer term rather than reselling metered usage (`edu-utility-submetering-as`).

title: Lock Changes for Domestic Violence Victims in American Samoa
bodyText: We found no American Samoa statute, regulation or court rule giving a tenant who is a victim of domestic or family violence a right to have the locks changed, or requiring you to change them. The territory's protection-order law does reach your property: a court may order the abuser removed and excluded from the victim's residence regardless of who owns it, ordered to stay away from it, and the police may be directed to restore the victim to possession. If a tenant shows you such an order, honour it: do not let the excluded person in or give him a key, even if he is on the lease. The cautious course is to change or rekey the locks promptly at the victim's request, keep a key yourself, and agree in writing who pays. Federal VAWA rules add protections in federally assisted housing (`edu-dv-eviction-protection-as`).

title: Inspecting the Rental in American Samoa
bodyText: No American Samoa statute gives a landlord a right to inspect a rented home during the tenancy or sets notice for an inspection, so your right comes from the lease; use the shared Inspection Rights clause (`inspection-rights`) as written, with the shared entry clause. The law that does apply limits how you enter: no one may enter premises unless the entry is permitted by law, and then only peaceably, never by force, and entering a home a tenant occupies without the tenant's consent or another legal right can be criminal trespass. So inspect only on the notice the lease gives, at reasonable times, and if the tenant refuses, do not force your way in: rely on the lease's remedies or the court.

title: Key Control in American Samoa
bodyText: We found no American Samoa statute, regulation or court rule requiring a landlord or management company to keep a key-control policy, or to screen employees who hold keys, at any size of complex. Keeping keys secure is still part of protecting your tenants and yourself: log who holds keys, rekey when keys are lost or staff leave, and let staff enter only as the lease allows. Entering an occupied unit without the tenant's consent or another legal right can be criminal trespass, and under the common law the territory applies you may be answerable for what an employee does with a key (case law not searched).

title: Entering the Rental in American Samoa
bodyText: American Samoa has no landlord-tenant act setting an entry notice period, entry hours, emergency entry, or remedies for refused or abusive entry; the lease sets your access, and the shared Landlord's Right of Entry clause (`landlords-access`) gives 24 hours' notice except in an emergency. Two statutes still govern every entry. No one may enter premises unless the entry is permitted by law, and then only peaceably, never with force. And entering a home a tenant occupies without the tenant's consent or another legal right, or staying after being told to leave, can be criminal trespass. So enter only as the lease allows, give the notice it promises, and never force entry or change locks to get in; if a tenant refuses access the lease allows, treat it as a breach to be handled through a written demand and, if needed, the court. A tenant's complaint about entry is not a ground for retaliation: a possession case brought mainly to punish a lawful act fails.

title: Entry for Scheduled Services in American Samoa
bodyText: We found no American Samoa statute, regulation or court rule on entry for regularly scheduled services such as pest treatment or filter changes, so the lease decides. If you want to enter on a schedule with shorter notice than your general entry term gives, write the services, schedule, hours and notice into the lease; the optional shared clause (`scheduled-services-entry-la`) does that. Every entry must still be permitted by the lease and made peaceably, never by force.

title: Showing the Rental in American Samoa
bodyText: We found no American Samoa statute, regulation or court rule on entry to show a rental to prospective tenants or buyers, on the notice for showings, or on whether a tenant may waive that notice. The lease decides, and a tenant may agree in it to shorter notice for showings near the end of the term; the optional shared clause (`showing-notice-la`) does that. Keep showings within the hours and notice the lease gives, accompany visitors, and never enter by force.

title: Smart Locks and App-Based Entry in American Samoa
bodyText: We found no American Samoa statute, regulation or court rule on smart locks, keypad or app-based entry systems in rentals. You may use them, but an entry code is a key: an entry through it must still be permitted by the lease and made peaceably, and you must never disable or change a tenant's code to keep the tenant out, since possession comes back only through a court case (normally the summary procedure). If the system logs entries or collects data, tell tenants what it records, and give them a physical key or another way in if it fails.

title: Property Left Behind in American Samoa
bodyText: We found no American Samoa statute, regulation or court rule on what a landlord may or must do with belongings a tenant leaves behind, whether after moving out or after the court's writ is carried out. The writ directs the marshal or police to remove the tenant and those claiming under the tenant and restore possession to you; it says nothing about belongings. Under the common law the territory applies (case law not searched), selling or throwing away someone else's property without consent can make you liable for its value, and removing belongings while the tenant is still in possession is self-help the law does not allow. The cautious course is a written procedure the tenant agrees to in the lease: notice, safe storage for a stated time, then sale or disposal (`abandoned-property-procedure-as`). If the tenant has died, the belongings belong to the estate: deal with the personal representative, or, where the personal property left is worth $10,000 or less in all, known debts are less than that, and those entitled to it cannot readily obtain it, the persons entitled to administer the estate (the surviving spouse or the spouse's designee, then next of kin, then a competent creditor living in American Samoa; and, if none of them petitions within 90 days of the death, any creditor) can petition the High Court's Trial Division for an order transferring the property to the petitioner.

title: Abandonment and Re-Renting in American Samoa
bodyText: We found no American Samoa statute defining when a tenant has abandoned a rental, or requiring a landlord to re-rent and credit the tenant when a tenant leaves early. Both questions fall to the common law the territory applies (case law not searched); the cautious course is to make reasonable efforts to re-rent and to credit what you receive against what the departed tenant owes. Two statutory points matter. A written demand for nonpayment may claim only rent actually due, not future rent accelerated because of the breach; your claim for the rest of the term is a damages claim, which you can join to a possession case or bring separately. And if you think a tenant has abandoned the home but are not sure, do not simply retake it: entry must be permitted by law and peaceable, and the safe route is to recover possession through the court's summary procedure.

title: Attorney Fees and Court Costs in American Samoa
bodyText: No American Samoa statute governs attorney-fee terms in a residential lease: none requires them to be mutual, caps them, or bars them. Court costs are different: in a civil case the court allows costs to the winning party as a matter of course unless it directs otherwise, a possession judgment may include costs, and a tenant who wins the possession case gets judgment for costs. Whether a court will also award attorney's fees under a lease term rests on the lease and the common law (case law not searched). If you include a fee term, make it run both ways, as the shared Default by Tenant clause does, and keep the fees reasonable; a one-sided term risks attack under the Consumer Protection Act, whose reach to leases is unsettled, and that Act separately lets a court award fees against a supplier who violates it. To stop a nonpayment writ, a tenant pays the judgment amount plus taxed costs.

title: Federal 30-Day Notice to Vacate in American Samoa
bodyText: The federal CARES Act notice rule (`edu-cares-act-notice`) applies to rentals in American Samoa on the same terms as anywhere else: if the property has a federally backed mortgage loan, or takes part in a covered federal housing program or the rural housing voucher program, you may not require the tenant to vacate until 30 days after you give a notice to vacate. American Samoa's own nonpayment demand gives only 7 days, so on a covered property give a written notice to vacate of at least 30 days as well, and do not file for possession before it runs out. Check the loan and any program participation for each property before you serve a demand.

title: Fire and Casualty Damage in American Samoa
bodyText: We found no American Samoa statute, regulation or court rule giving a tenant the right to end the lease, or to pay less rent, after a fire, storm or other casualty damages the home, and none giving you a right to end it. What happens rests on the lease and the common law (case law not searched), so put it in the lease: the optional casualty clause (`casualty-termination-as`) lets either party end the lease after serious damage, stops or reduces rent for the part that cannot be used unless the tenant's side caused the damage, and keeps the tenant liable for damage it caused (`tenant-caused-damage-nm`). If a tenant willfully or negligently causes extensive and continuing damage, you may serve a written demand and recover possession if it is not substantially restored or repaired within 7 days, and you can claim damages for waste or malicious destruction in the possession case. After a declared disaster, see also `edu-disaster-duties-as`.

title: Converting a Rental in American Samoa
bodyText: We found no American Samoa statute, regulation or court rule on converting rental housing to condominiums, cooperatives, hotel rooms or other uses: the territory has no condominium act, and there is no conversion notice, first-refusal right or relocation duty for private landlords. Ending tenancies for a conversion follows the ordinary rules: a fixed term runs to its end, and a periodic tenancy ends on the notice the lease or the common law requires (case law not searched). Land status still matters: selling units that carry an interest in the land is an alienation of land: communal (native) family land may be alienated only with the Governor's written approval and, to a buyer with any non-Samoan blood, only on the strict conditions the land laws set, and no land except freehold land may be sold to a buyer of less than one-half Samoan blood (`edu-communal-land-lease-approval-as`). If you convert to short-term lodging, ask about the territorial business licence and hotel occupancy tax first.

title: Criminal Activity at a Rental in American Samoa
bodyText: We found no American Samoa statute making a lease void for criminal use, creating a fast-track eviction for crime or drug activity, or making it a crime for a landlord to allow drug use on the property. To remove a tenant for criminal activity you need a lease term that lets you end the lease for it, such as the optional shared Criminal Activity clause (`criminal-activity-ky`), then a written demand stating the reason and the time allowed, and a possession case if the tenant does not leave; a tenant who is causing a serious and continuing health hazard can be given a 7-day demand. One territorial rule binds owners directly: a room or building regularly used for prostitution is a public nuisance, and if the court finds the owner knew or had reason to believe it, it may order the premises closed for up to a year; owners and lessees who aid the nuisance may be enjoined. In federally assisted housing, VAWA bars evicting a victim because of crime committed against the victim (`edu-dv-eviction-protection-as`).

title: Grounds for Possession and the Chance to Cure in American Samoa
bodyText: American Samoa's possession statute lists the grounds on which you may recover possession in the court's summary procedure, and each starts with a written demand. Nonpayment: the tenant has 7 days after service of a written demand stating the amount due; paying in that time ends the ground, and the demand may not claim future rent accelerated because of the breach. Serious and continuing health hazard, or extensive and continuing damage, caused willfully or negligently: 7 days after the demand to leave or substantially restore or repair. Other breaches: there is no statutory cure period; you need a power in the lease to end it for the breach, and your demand must state the reasons and the time you allow to put things right, so give a reasonable time and say it in the demand. Holding over after the term ends, and forcible entry or trespass, are separate grounds. Even after a nonpayment judgment, the tenant can stop the writ by paying the judgment amount and taxed costs within 10 days after the judgment (`edu-eviction-process-as`).

title: Tenant Default in American Samoa
bodyText: The shared Default by Tenant clause (`default-by-tenant`) works in American Samoa as written, read with the possession statute. For unpaid rent, the time to cure after written notice is the 7 days the statute gives after service of your written demand, and the demand must state the amount due and may not include future rent accelerated because of the breach. For other breaches, the clause's termination right is the lease power to terminate that the statute relies on; your written demand must state the reasons and the time to put things right. Serve demands only by personal delivery, delivery on the premises to a household member or employee of suitable age and discretion, or registered mail with a return receipt signed by the tenant, and keep a copy, since it and the lease must be attached to your complaint. Recover possession only through the court; a tenant can defeat the case by proving retaliation or, in a nonpayment case, a breach by you that excuses the rent, and can stop a nonpayment writ by paying the judgment amount and costs. Attorney's fees depend on the lease and the court (`edu-attorney-fees-as`).

title: After a Declared Disaster in American Samoa
bodyText: No American Samoa statute ends a tenancy, or suspends rent, when a declared disaster makes a home inaccessible or unusable; the lease and the common law decide (case law not searched), so use the optional casualty clause (`casualty-termination-as`). Two sets of rules apply during a disaster. First, the Governor may declare a disaster emergency, for up to 30 days unless renewed, and may then order evacuations, control who enters and occupies premises in the disaster area, commandeer private property subject to compensation, and provide temporary emergency housing; follow those orders even where the lease says otherwise. Second, the price-gouging law: once a state of emergency is declared, and for 30 days after, you may not rent or offer month-to-month housing for more than 10 percent above what you charged just before the declaration, unless you can prove the increase comes from added costs, and the Governor may extend the period by 30 days at a time. Violations carry civil penalties and are misdemeanors, enforced by the Attorney General. Disaster emergencies were declared in 2023, 2024 and 2025, so before raising a month-to-month rent, check whether one was declared or extended in the last 30 days.

title: Drug-Free Housing Terms in American Samoa
bodyText: We found no American Samoa statute, regulation or court rule requiring, prescribing or limiting a drug-free or crime-free lease addendum. You may include one as a lease term; the optional shared Criminal Activity clause (`criminal-activity-ky`) covers drug activity on the property. Enforcing it follows the ordinary route: the lease's termination power, a written demand stating the reason and the time allowed, and a possession case if needed (`edu-criminal-activity-as`). Federal program rules for assisted housing were not reviewed for this library; if your property is in a federal housing program, use the addendum the program requires.

title: Domestic Violence and Eviction in American Samoa
bodyText: We found no American Samoa statute that protects a tenant from eviction because the tenant is a victim of domestic or family violence, or that limits evicting a household because of an abuser's conduct. Two other sources apply. If your rental is assisted under a covered federal housing program (for example Section 8 assistance, the low-income housing tax credit, or federal rural housing assistance), the federal Violence Against Women Act bars denying, terminating or evicting a tenant because the tenant is a victim, says an incident of violence against the victim is not a serious lease violation or good cause to end the victim's tenancy, and lets you split the lease to remove the abuser alone; this federal law applies in American Samoa by its own terms. And in any rental, a territorial protection order may remove and exclude the abuser from the victim's home regardless of ownership: honour it, and do not treat it as a breach by the victim. Retaliation is also a defence to possession, but only where you end the tenancy mainly to punish a lawful act arising out of the tenancy; whether seeking a protection order is such an act is unsettled (case law not searched), so never end a tenancy because a tenant sought one.

title: Ending a Lease Early Because of Domestic Violence in American Samoa
bodyText: We found no American Samoa statute letting a tenant who is a victim of domestic or family violence, sexual assault or stalking end a lease early, and none letting you end the tenancy of an abuser who is the only remaining tenant on a short notice. The lease and the common law decide (case law not searched), so consider agreeing in writing to release a victim who needs to move for safety. In federally assisted housing, VAWA lets you split the lease to evict or remove the abuser alone without penalizing the victim, and if the abuser was the only tenant eligible for assistance, you must give the remaining household a chance to establish eligibility and, if they cannot, a reasonable time, set by the program agency, to find new housing or qualify under another covered program (`edu-dv-eviction-protection-as`). A territorial protection order may also exclude the abuser from the home regardless of whose name is on the lease.

title: Proof of Domestic Violence Status in American Samoa
bodyText: No American Samoa statute says what documents a tenant must give to claim protection as a victim of domestic violence, because the territory gives no such housing protection. In federally assisted housing, VAWA sets the rule: you may ask in writing for documentation, and the tenant then has 14 business days (which you may extend) to give one of: the federal certification form; a statement signed by a victim service provider, attorney, or medical or mental health professional and by the tenant, under penalty of perjury; a police, court or administrative record; or, at your discretion, the tenant's own statement or other evidence. You need not ask for any documentation, and whatever you receive must be kept confidential and not disclosed except with the tenant's written consent, for an eviction case, or as law requires. A territorial protection order or a court record of one is a record a court issued.

title: Ending a Lease Early in American Samoa
bodyText: No American Samoa statute gives a tenant a right to end a lease early or limits an early-termination fee, so the lease decides; the shared Early Termination clause (`early-termination-ks`) works as written and keeps its fee to fixed-term leases. Whether a court would enforce a large fee as agreed damages or strike it as a penalty is a common-law question (case law not searched), and a grossly one-sided fee may also draw the Consumer Protection Act, whose reach to leases is unsettled, so keep the fee proportionate to your likely loss. One federal right overrides the lease: under the Servicemembers Civil Relief Act, which applies in American Samoa, a tenant who enters military service, or who receives orders for a permanent change of station or a deployment of at least 90 days, may end the lease by written notice with a copy of the orders; for a monthly lease the end comes 30 days after the next rent due date, you may not charge an early-termination fee, and you must refund rent paid in advance within 30 days.

title: Government Taking of a Rental in American Samoa
bodyText: The American Samoa Government may take land or any interest in it for public purposes, paying just compensation through a court proceeding; once the declaration of taking is filed and the estimated compensation deposited, title vests in the Government. If the Government takes possession immediately, the damage the occupant, lessee, lessor or owner suffers from that early occupancy is included in the compensation. Under the territory's relocation rules, a tenant lawfully living in a taken home for at least 90 days before negotiations began may receive a replacement-housing payment, and the Government is to give people living on acquired property at least 90 days' written notice before they must move, to the extent practicable. No statute says whether rent stops or the lease ends when the property is taken, so say so in the lease: for example, that the lease ends on the date the Government takes possession, rent is prorated to that date, and each party may claim its own compensation from the Government.

title: Who May Represent a Company Landlord in Court in American Samoa
bodyText: No American Samoa statute or court rule says expressly whether a corporation, partnership or other entity landlord may appear in a possession case through an officer or employee who is not a lawyer. The territory makes it a crime for any person, association, firm or corporation to practise law unless licensed by the Chief Justice, and the Bar's case notes describe representing another in court as the practice of law. An individual owner may bring a case personally, but a property manager or relative who is not a lawyer should not sign or argue a case for the owner, and the cautious course for an entity landlord is to file and appear through a licensed attorney (case law not searched). Legal practitioners, the non-attorney practitioners still on the Bar's roll, may practise only in the Land and Titles Division, the village courts and certain other matters, not in a Trial Division possession case. A demand for possession may still be signed by an agent.

title: Environmental Events and Ending a Lease in American Samoa
bodyText: We found no American Samoa statute, regulation or court rule letting a landlord or tenant end a lease because of an environmental event such as contamination, a volcanic or seismic hazard, flooding or a tsunami. The lease and the common law decide (case law not searched); the optional casualty clause (`casualty-termination-as`) covers physical damage, and you may add a similar term for a property made unusable by an environmental hazard. Government orders can force the issue: the Department of Health may order a building closed, evacuated or decontaminated to abate a public health nuisance, and the Governor may order evacuations and control occupancy of premises in a declared disaster area (`edu-disaster-duties-as`). Follow any such order, tell your tenants at once, and agree in writing how rent is handled while they cannot live there.

title: Delays and Stays in a Possession Case in American Samoa
bodyText: We found no American Samoa statute, regulation or court rule letting a court stay or postpone a possession judgment because of the tenant's hardship. The timing rules are fixed: the court may continue a summary case, or the parties may agree in writing to continue it, but for no more than 7 days at a time, and it may require security; except in cases of forcible entry, trespass, or a serious health hazard or continuing damage, the writ cannot issue until 10 days after judgment; and if the tenant files an appeal or a motion for a new trial and a bond to stay proceedings, the writ waits until that is decided. In a nonpayment case the tenant can stop the writ altogether by paying the judgment amount and costs in time. Federal law adds one stay: if the tenant is a servicemember, or a servicemember's dependent, whose ability to pay is materially affected by military service, and the rent is under the federal limit, the court must on request stay the case for 90 days or adjust the lease.

title: The Possession Process in American Samoa
bodyText: You recover possession of a rental in American Samoa only through a court case, normally the summary procedure under Title 43, chapter 14 (which is in addition to, not instead of, your other court remedies), never by lockout, utility shutoff or removing belongings. The steps: (1) a written demand, dated and signed, addressed to the person in possession, describing the premises, stating the reasons and the time to put things right and, for unpaid rent, the amount due; (2) service by personal delivery, delivery on the premises to a household member or employee of suitable age and discretion, or registered mail with a return receipt signed by the tenant (mailed demands count from the date of receipt); (3) after the demand period (7 days for rent and for a serious health hazard or continuing damage), a complaint in the Trial Division with the demand and any written lease attached; (4) a summons for trial within 10 days, served at least 3 days before trial, with continuances of no more than 7 days; (5) judgment, in which the court deducts rent excused by your breach and may award costs; and (6) a writ, not before 10 days after judgment except in force, trespass or health-hazard cases, carried out by the marshal or police. The tenant may defend on retaliation and, in a nonpayment case, on a breach by you that excuses the rent, and in a nonpayment case may stop the writ by paying the judgment amount and costs; assume that right applies even if your lease is unregistered or you rely on a termination clause. Disputes over communal land itself go to the Land and Titles Division.

title: Eviction Court Records in American Samoa
bodyText: We found no American Samoa statute, regulation or court rule sealing, expunging or removing eviction case records, automatically or on request. Under the High Court's rules, court files are public records that may be examined at the courthouse unless the court has ordered a particular file sealed. Assume a possession case you file, and its outcome, will be public. If you screen applicants using court records, judge each record on what it shows, including whether the case was dismissed or settled.

title: Serving Possession Papers in American Samoa
bodyText: The possession statute sets how your written demand is served: personally on the person in possession; on the premises to a member of that person's family or household, or an employee, of suitable age and discretion, asking that it be passed on; or by registered mail with a return receipt signed by the person in possession or that person's authorized agent. We found no rule letting a lease name a person to accept the demand or court papers, so do not rely on one: serve by a statutory method even if the lease names an agent. The court's summons is served by an officer or other person authorized to serve the court's process. We found no address-confidentiality program changing how a protected tenant is served.

title: Faster Possession for Force, Trespass or Serious Hazard in American Samoa
bodyText: American Samoa has no separate fast-track eviction for drug or other criminal activity. Every summary possession case already moves quickly: trial is set within 10 days. The statute then lets the court issue the writ immediately on judgment, instead of after the usual 10 days, where it is pleaded and proved, with notice, that the person entered by force, holds possession by force after a peaceable entry, came in as a trespasser without color of title, or is willfully or negligently causing a serious and continuing health hazard or extensive and continuing damage and will neither leave after demand nor restore or repair. Criminal conduct that fits none of these needs a lease term letting you end the lease for it (`edu-criminal-activity-as`) and the ordinary process.

title: No Just-Cause Rule for Ending a Tenancy in American Samoa
bodyText: We found no American Samoa statute, regulation or court rule that requires you to have a reason (just cause or good cause) to end a residential tenancy or to decline to renew it. A fixed-term lease may end at the end of its term, and a month-to-month or week-to-week tenancy may end by the notice your lease sets (`periodic-tenancy-notice-as`); either way you recover possession only through the court, after a written demand (`edu-self-help-eviction-as`). There are limits on why you end it: the court will not give you possession if the termination was mainly retribution for a lawful act arising out of the tenancy, such as a complaint to the authorities (`edu-retaliation-as`), and the federal Fair Housing Act, which reaches American Samoa, bars ending a tenancy because of race, color, religion, sex, disability, familial status or national origin. In federally assisted housing, federal program rules (including the Violence Against Women Act) can require cause and protect victims of domestic violence. For 30 days after a state of emergency is declared, and for any further 30-day periods the Governor adds, you may not rent month-to-month housing for more than 10% above the rent charged just before the declaration, unless you can prove a larger increase comes directly from added costs, within the statute's cost-plus-markup limit, and just before and while a declaration is in effect an increase above the territory's consumer price index may be an unconscionable price (`edu-disaster-duties-as`), so ending a tenancy to re-let at a higher rent in that window can break the price-gouging law. If the home is on communal (native) land, a matai's authority and Samoan custom may affect who may stay; a court case note says a matai's eviction orders to family members need good cause (case law not searched), so take advice before ending a tenancy there.

title: Foreclosure and Tenants in American Samoa
bodyText: We found no American Samoa statute, regulation or court rule that requires you to tell a tenant or applicant the property is in foreclosure, keeps a lease in force after a foreclosure sale, or gives the tenant a set time to leave after one. A mortgage in American Samoa is only a lien; the owner keeps use and possession until default, and the lender forecloses either by a High Court action or under a power of sale in the mortgage, which needs published notice and a copy posted on the premises at least 21 days before the sale, so your tenants may see it before you tell them. Whether the buyer at a foreclosure sale takes subject to your lease depends on recording and priority under common law (case law not searched), so register a written lease with the Territorial Registrar (`edu-lease-registration-as`). Federal law may apply where the mortgage is federally backed or the home is in a federal housing program: the CARES Act's 30-day notice to vacate covers such dwellings, and the federal Protecting Tenants at Foreclosure Act was not reviewed for this library. If a foreclosure notice is published or posted on your rental, tell your tenants in writing and don't take rent more than a month in advance until it is resolved.

title: Paying to Keep the Tenancy in American Samoa
bodyText: A tenant who is behind on rent has two chances under American Samoa law to keep the home. Before any case, the nonpayment ground needs rent still unpaid 7 days after your written demand is served, so if the tenant pays the amount stated in the demand within that time you have no nonpayment case. After a nonpayment judgment, the tenant can stop the writ by paying the judgment amount and taxed costs within the time the law allows (`edu-redemption-after-judgment-as`). We found no American Samoa statute, regulation or court rule that lets a tenant undo a termination for some other breach by curing it later, or that sets a general right to relief from forfeiture of a lease; whether a court would relieve a forfeiture in equity rests on common law (case law not searched). Don't write a lease term that waives or shortens either payment chance, and if a tenant tenders the full amount due before you file, accept it or take advice before refusing.

title: Lease Guarantors in American Samoa
bodyText: We found no American Samoa statute, regulation or court rule on lease guarantors: nothing limits a guarantor to the original term, requires a guaranty to state a maximum amount or end date, or limits what you may ask a guarantor to deposit. The territory also has no general guaranty statute, so a guaranty is a contract governed by common law (case law not searched). Under the general common-law rule a guarantor can be released if the lease is changed or extended without the guarantor's agreement, so get the guaranty in writing, signed by the guarantor, and say plainly whether it covers renewals, extensions and any month-to-month continuation, and any maximum amount. Use the optional clause `guaranty-as` if a guarantor signs. Because the Consumer Protection Act may reach a residential lease, explain the guaranty to the guarantor and don't misstate what it covers.

title: Tenants Who Stay After the Lease Ends in American Samoa
bodyText: If a tenant stays after a fixed term ends, or after you end the tenancy under a power in the lease or by notice, American Samoa's possession statute treats that as holding over and lets you recover the home in a summary repossession case in the Trial Division, after a written demand that meets the statute (`edu-self-help-eviction-as`). We found no American Samoa statute, regulation or court rule that sets holdover damages for a private rental, such as double rent or a daily multiple of rent; the "fair market value rent" rule for holdovers applies only to government housing. You may join a claim for your actual damages from the holdover (usually the rental value of the days held and any provable loss) in the same case, or bring it separately. If you accept rent after the term ends, a court may treat the tenancy as continuing from period to period under common law (case law not searched), so say in writing whether a payment is accepted as rent for a new period or only as use and occupancy. An agreed daily holdover charge is optional (`holdover-rate-as`).

title: No Exemption-Waiver Rule in American Samoa
bodyText: American Samoa has no homestead exemption and we found no American Samoa statute, regulation or court rule that lets a lease waive a tenant's protections from collection, or that sets waiver wording; the library offers no waiver clause. The protections that do exist are set by statute: a Samoan's real property cannot be sold under a writ to pay a judgment (other than a mortgage foreclosure), a court setting a payment order must let the debtor keep what the debtor and dependents reasonably need to live, including Samoan family obligations, and workers' compensation benefits are exempt and the exemption cannot be waived. Collect a rent judgment through the court's ordinary process (`edu-landlord-remedies-termination-as`), and don't put a waiver of any of these protections in your lease.

title: No Health or Care-Facility Termination Right in American Samoa
bodyText: We found no American Samoa statute, regulation or court rule that lets a tenant end a fixed-term lease early because of age, illness, disability or a move to a nursing home, assisted living or a relative's care. A tenant in that position stays bound by the lease unless you agree otherwise or the lease has an early-termination term (`edu-statutory-early-termination-as`). Two federal rules can still apply: a servicemember who suffers a catastrophic injury or illness in service may, within one year, end a residential lease covered by the Servicemembers Civil Relief Act (`edu-servicemember-rights-as`), and a request from a tenant with a disability to end the lease early may be a reasonable-accommodation request under the federal Fair Housing Act, which you should consider in good faith. If a tenant does leave early, try to re-let the unit before claiming the rest of the rent, because whether a court will expect you to reduce your loss rests on common law (case law not searched).

title: No Landlord's Lien on a Tenant's Belongings in American Samoa
bodyText: American Samoa gives a residential landlord no lien on a tenant's furniture or other belongings for unpaid rent, and no right to seize or hold them (distress); we found no American Samoa statute, regulation or court rule creating one. Don't take, lock up or sell a tenant's property to collect rent: entry onto premises must be permitted by law and peaceable, and possession is recovered only through the court (`edu-self-help-eviction-as`). A lease clause granting you a security interest in a tenant's household goods would not bind third parties unless it is signed, witnessed, describes the goods and is filed with the Territorial Registrar within 10 days, so the library offers no such clause. To secure a rent claim, use the court: in a suit on the lease you may ask for a writ of attachment of the tenant's non-exempt property, but you must first post a bond of at least double your claim. Federal law also bars distress, except by court order, during a servicemember's military service against a home rented to the servicemember or dependents whose monthly rent is within the federal cap (adjusted yearly for inflation).

title: Landlord's Remedies When a Tenant Defaults in American Samoa
bodyText: When a tenant defaults, your remedies in American Samoa are possession and money, and possession goes through the High Court. For possession you serve a written demand and bring a summary repossession case in the Trial Division (`edu-self-help-eviction-as`); in that case you may also claim unpaid rent and damages for breach of the lease, for wrongful holding over, or for waste, and the judgment states the arrears. The summary remedy is in addition to your other remedies, so a possession judgment does not stop a later suit for damages, which may be heard in the Trial Division or the Land and Titles Division. A money claim of $15,000 or less that is not an action involving land may instead go to the District Court, and one under $7,500 may use its simplified small-claims procedure; whether a claim for rent counts as an action involving land is a point only case law could settle (case law not searched), so ask the court clerk which court takes your claim.
