The Revised Constitution bars jail for an unpaid debt except in cases of fraud, so unpaid rent is collected through a judgment, not a criminal complaint. Accelerated future rent cannot be counted as rent due for the nonpayment ground, and we found no American Samoa statute that lets you accelerate all remaining rent or that requires you to re-let to reduce your loss; both rest on common law (case law not searched), so claim future rent only as it falls due or as damages after you have tried to re-let. Sue on a written lease within 10 years (3 years on an oral one), and expect the court to set a payment schedule that leaves the tenant enough to live on.

title: No Statutory Right to Fix a Tenant's Breach and Bill It in American Samoa
bodyText: We found no American Samoa statute, regulation or court rule that lets you fix a tenant's breach (cleaning, repairs the tenant must make, garbage, damage) and bill the cost as rent. A right to do so comes only from the lease (`landlord-self-cure-as`), and two rules limit how you use it: you may enter only where the law permits and only peaceably, never by force, and an unpaid repair bill is not "rent due" for a nonpayment case, so recover it as a sum due under the lease, from the deposit as your lease allows, or as damages joined in a possession case. If the Department of Health makes you abate a nuisance the tenant caused, the tenant is liable to you by statute for what you pay (`edu-nuisance-as`). Give written notice and a fair time to fix the problem first, and charge only the reasonable cost.

title: Agreed Damages for a Tenant's Breach in American Samoa
bodyText: We found no American Samoa statute, regulation or court rule that permits, sets, caps or bars an agreed (liquidated) damages amount for a residential tenant's breach, such as an early-termination fee or a fixed charge for leaving early. Whether such a figure is enforceable or an unenforceable penalty rests on common law (case law not searched), and the Consumer Protection Act may reach a residential lease and lets a court strike or limit grossly one-sided terms. If you use an agreed amount, make it a reasonable estimate of the loss you would actually suffer, say it replaces rather than adds to your other damages for the same loss, and don't stack it with late fees or interest on the same default. Never raise a tenant's charges to punish a complaint or other lawful act: the court will refuse you possession where the tenant's failure to pay the added charge is the main reason you are ending the tenancy.

title: No Lockouts for Unpaid Rent in American Samoa
bodyText: We found no American Samoa statute, regulation or court rule that lets a residential landlord lock out a tenant for unpaid rent, with or without a lease clause, and the library offers none. The possession statute allows entry onto premises only where the law permits it, and never by force; you recover possession of a rented home only by a court judgment and a writ served by a court officer, normally no sooner than 10 days after judgment, and a nonpayment judgment can still be paid off in that time (`edu-redemption-after-judgment-as`). Changing the locks, removing doors or belongings, or cutting off utilities to press for rent puts you at risk of a damages claim for wrongful entry or possession, and entering a tenant's home without a right to be there can be criminal trespass. Serve a written demand for the rent and, if it isn't paid within 7 days, file a summary repossession case (`edu-nonpayment-notice-as`).

title: Minors as Tenants and in Repossession Cases in American Samoa
bodyText: In American Samoa a person becomes an adult at 18. We found no American Samoa statute, regulation or court rule on leasing to someone under 18 or barring you from naming a minor in a repossession case, so whether a minor's lease can be cancelled by the minor rests on common law (case law not searched). Have only adults sign the lease as tenants; list children as occupants, and if a 16- or 17-year-old must be a tenant, have a parent or guardian sign as tenant or guarantor (`guaranty-as`). If a minor is a party to a court case, the court rules require service on the minor's parent or guardian (and on the minor if 12 or older) and let the court appoint a guardian ad litem, so name the adult tenants as defendants; the writ of restitution covers everyone on the premises claiming under them.

title: Written Demand Before a Nonpayment Case in American Samoa
bodyText: Before you can bring a summary repossession case for unpaid rent in American Samoa, you must serve a written demand and wait 7 days after service. The demand must be in writing, addressed to the tenant in possession, describe the premises (address or brief description), state clearly the reason and the time the tenant has to pay, state the amount due on the date of the demand, and be dated and signed by you or your attorney or agent. Serve it by handing it to the tenant, by leaving it at the home with a household member or employee of suitable age and discretion who is asked to pass it on, or by registered mail, return receipt requested, signed by the tenant or the tenant's agent (service is then the date of receipt); email or text alone is not one of the listed methods. Don't count the day of service; weekends count, but if the 7th day falls on a weekend or legal holiday, wait until the next business day. No wording is prescribed and we found no rule letting the lease itself serve as, or waive, the demand, so serve a separate demand every time and keep proof of service: a copy must be attached to your complaint, with a copy of the written lease. If the property has a federally backed mortgage or is in a federal housing program, the CARES Act may also require 30 days' notice to vacate.

title: No Waiving the Demand Before a Repossession Case in American Samoa
bodyText: We found no American Samoa statute, regulation or court rule that lets a lease waive or shorten the written demand you must serve before a summary repossession case, and American Samoa has no statutory notice to quit for periodic tenancies that a lease could vary (`periodic-tenancy-notice-as`). The demand is built into the case itself: the nonpayment ground runs 7 days from service of the demand, and a complaint filed without a copy of a demand meeting the statute can be dismissed. A court case note suggests a tenant may waive the demand rules, but it is only a lead (case law not searched) and does not deal with a waiver signed in advance in a lease. Don't put a waiver of the demand, or a shorter period than the statute's 7 days, in your lease; serve a full demand every time (`edu-nonpayment-notice-as`).

title: Nuisance Law and Your Rental in American Samoa
bodyText: American Samoa's nuisance rules are general health and criminal rules, not landlord-tenant rules, but they reach your rental. It is unlawful to create or allow a public health nuisance (anything that endangers life or health or contaminates the environment); the Department of Health can order it removed at the owner's or occupant's expense, and if costs go unpaid it can make them a lien on the property or collect them from the rents under a court order. A tenant who caused or allowed the nuisance must repay you what you paid or what was assessed against the property. Keeping a nuisance after 10 days' written notice to abate is a misdemeanor for whoever owns or occupies the property. If you know or have reason to believe a unit is used regularly for prostitution, a court can bar anyone from using the premises for up to a year, and property used for a drug felony, including a tenant's leasehold, can be forfeited. If a tenant willfully or negligently causes a serious and continuing health hazard, serve a written demand to stop or repair it; after 7 days you may bring a repossession case and ask for an immediate writ (`edu-nonpayment-notice-as` explains the demand). Village council rules on noise, animals or conduct may also apply (not published; flagged only).

title: Ending a Lease Early to Move In
bodyText: We found no American Samoa statute, regulation or court rule that gives you a right to end a lease early so you or a relative can move in, or that limits such a right if your lease reserves it. During a fixed term the right comes only from the lease: use the library's optional owner-occupancy clause (`owner-occupancy-termination-ar`) if you may need the home back, and give the notice it states. A month-to-month or week-to-week tenancy can be ended without a reason by the notice your lease sets (`periodic-tenancy-notice-as`). Either way, if the tenant does not leave you must serve a written demand and recover possession through the court, and the court will refuse possession if the real reason is retaliation. If the home is on communal (native) land, the matai's authority over family land may affect who may occupy it (flagged only; take advice).

title: No Possession Bond in American Samoa
bodyText: We found no American Samoa statute, regulation or court rule that lets you require a tenant to post a bond, or sign a confessed judgment, to secure giving up possession when the lease ends, and the library offers none. The bonds the law knows arise inside a repossession case: the court may require security as a condition of a continuance (which may not exceed 7 days), and a tenant who appeals or moves for a new trial may be required to file a bond to stay the writ. A lease term in which the tenant agrees in advance to a judgment for possession would sidestep the written demand, the court's judgment and the tenant's statutory defences and post-judgment payment right, and the Consumer Protection Act may let a court strike it, so don't use one. Secure the end of the term with the security deposit your lease sets and, if the tenant stays, the court process (`edu-holdover-as`).

title: Delay in Delivering Possession in American Samoa
bodyText: We found no American Samoa statute, regulation or court rule on what happens if you can't deliver possession on the lease's start date, and none requiring a private landlord to provide alternate housing; the relocation rules in the Code cover only people displaced when the government acquires property. The lease governs, with the common law behind it (case law not searched), so use the library's possession-delay clause (`possession-delay`): no rent until you deliver, and the tenant may cancel and get everything back if you can't deliver within 30 days. If a previous occupant won't leave, you, as the person entitled to the premises, can bring a summary repossession case against that occupant after a written demand. Don't advertise or rent a unit you know won't be ready, since the Consumer Protection Act may reach a residential lease.

title: A Tenant's Belongings After a Repossession in American Samoa
bodyText: After you win a repossession judgment, the High Court marshal or a police officer carries out the writ: within 10 days of receiving it the officer removes, or supervises removal of, the tenant and everyone claiming under the tenant and restores possession to you. We found no American Samoa statute, regulation or court rule on what happens to belongings or animals left behind, how long you must store them, what notice you must give, or whether you may sell or discard them; the general escheat rule (unclaimed property passes to the Territory after 14 years) is no practical guide. Because the law is silent, your handling rests on common law (case law not searched), so take the cautious course: photograph and list what is left, store it safely, give the former tenant written notice by the methods the demand statute uses (`edu-nonpayment-notice-as`) with a reasonable time (for example, at least 30 days) to collect it, release it free of storage charges you can't justify, and arrange care for any animal at once. A former tenant who returns after removal without permission may be trespassing.

title: Leases and Unlawful Use of the Premises in American Samoa
bodyText: We found no American Samoa statute, regulation or court rule that makes a residential lease void, or ends it automatically, because the tenant uses the premises for an unlawful or different purpose. The lease continues until you end it under its own terms (the residential-use and lawful-use terms) and recover possession through the court after a written demand that states the reason and the time to remedy it (`edu-nuisance-as`). Unlawful use matters in other ways: a home used regularly for prostitution is a public nuisance that the Attorney General can sue to enjoin, and if the court finds the owner knew or had reason to believe of the regular use it may bar occupancy for up to a year, and owners and lessees who aid it can be made defendants, and property used for a drug felony, including a tenant's leasehold, can be forfeited. If you lease communal (native) land, the approved lease may not be used for mining or cutting timber.

title: Paying a Nonpayment Judgment to Keep the Home in American Samoa
bodyText: In American Samoa a tenant who loses a repossession case for unpaid rent can still keep the home by paying, after judgment, the amount the judgment states plus the court's taxed costs. The statute says the writ may not issue if that amount is paid within the time provided, and the writ cannot issue until 10 days after the judgment; the court rules give the same 10 days. The judgment amount is the arrears at trial, less any rent the court finds excused by your own breach of the lease. The court rules say this payment right does not apply where you are exercising a termination clause in the lease (unless the tenant pleads and proves the termination was influenced by retaliation or by your breach of the lease excusing rent) or where no written lease is registered with the Territorial Registrar, but the statute has no such exceptions and the rules themselves say the statute prevails where they contradict it. Assume the statutory right applies in every nonpayment judgment: accept full payment of the judgment amount and costs within 10 days, from the tenant or anyone paying for the tenant, and don't ask for the writ if it is paid. No lease term may waive or shorten this right. We found no American Samoa rule on accepting partial payments or on wording to reserve your rights; if you take part payment after a demand or judgment, say in writing that it is applied to the amount due and does not waive the demand or judgment (`edu-waiver-by-acceptance-as`).

title: No Rent-into-Court Rule in American Samoa
bodyText: We found no American Samoa statute, regulation or court rule that requires a tenant to pay rent into court, or into escrow, to defend a repossession case or to raise a counterclaim, and none makes the tenant's counterclaim mandatory in the possession case. A tenant may join a damages counterclaim (for example, for your breach of the lease), and the court may decide possession separately and leave the money claims for later, in the Trial Division or the Land and Titles Division. In a nonpayment case the tenant may defend by showing your breach of the lease excuses some or all of the rent, and the court deducts the excused rent from the judgment. If the court grants a continuance (at most 7 days), it may require security, which you can ask for, and either party may ask leave to deposit a disputed sum with the court. If the Consumer Protection Act reaches your lease, a tenant you sue may counterclaim under it.

title: False Information in a Rental Application
bodyText: We found no American Samoa statute, regulation or court rule on false statements in a rental application, so the lease and the common law govern (case law not searched). The library's American Samoa application-accuracy clause (`rental-application-accuracy-as`) makes a material false or misleading statement a breach of the lease, which you can act on by ending the tenancy under the lease and, if the tenant stays, serving a written demand and bringing a repossession case. One territorial rule matters: when a juvenile court record is sealed, the case is treated as never having happened and the person may properly answer that no record exists, so that answer is not a misstatement. Ask only questions you may lawfully consider: the federal Fair Housing Act, which reaches American Samoa, bars questions or screening that indicate a preference based on race, color, religion, sex, disability, familial status or national origin.

title: No Notice-Fee Rule in American Samoa
bodyText: We found no American Samoa statute, regulation or court rule that authorizes, caps or bans a fee for preparing or serving a notice on a tenant, such as the written demand for unpaid rent, and the library offers no such fee. The demand is your own legal step before a repossession case, and once you sue, the court decides what costs the tenant pays; those taxed costs are part of what the tenant may pay after a nonpayment judgment to keep the home, and adding your own notice fee to that amount or to the demand could make the demand overstate what is due. If you want to recover the cost of late payment, use a modest late fee stated in the lease (`edu-late-fee-as`), and don't stack fees and interest on the same late payment.

title: No Termination Because Repairs Cost Too Much
bodyText: We found no American Samoa statute, regulation or court rule that lets you end a lease, or refuse a repair, because the repair would cost too much compared with the rent or the property's value, and none that gives the tenant such a right. American Samoa has no residential repair or habitability statute, so your repair duties come from the lease and the common law (case law not searched) (`edu-landlord-maintenance-as`). If you leave a needed repair undone in breach of the lease, a court may excuse rent and refuse you possession for nonpayment. If a building becomes so dilapidated that it is unsafe, the Governor can order the owner to tear it down within 30 days; if the premises are destroyed or become unusable, whether the lease ends rests on common law and your lease's casualty terms. If you may want a way out, put an early-termination term for major damage in the lease rather than relying on cost alone.

title: Retaliation Against Tenants in American Samoa
bodyText: American Samoa's possession statute protects tenants from retaliation: the court may not give you a judgment for possession if the tenant shows that ending the tenancy was mainly retribution for a lawful act arising out of the tenancy (such as complaining to you or to the Department of Health, or asking for repairs), or that you tried to add to the tenant's obligations, such as a higher rent or new charges, as a penalty for a lawful act and the tenant's refusal to pay them was the main reason for ending the tenancy. The law sets no presumption or time window and no separate damages claim, but the defence applies to every tenancy, and no statute lets a lease waive it, so treat it as beyond the lease's reach (case law not searched). The federal Fair Housing Act, which reaches American Samoa, also bars threatening or interfering with anyone for exercising fair housing rights. Keep a written record of the real reason for any termination, rent increase or new charge, and avoid acting against a tenant soon after a complaint unless you have a documented, independent reason.

title: Seasonal and Short-Stay Rentals in American Samoa
bodyText: We found no American Samoa statute, regulation or court rule that sets special rules for seasonal or vacation residential tenancies. A lease for a season is an ordinary lease with an agreed term: state exact start and end dates, because a fixed term ends on its last day and an occupant who stays after it is holding over, whom you can remove only through the court after a written demand (`edu-holdover-as`). If you rent rooms or units by the night or week, or without a written lease for a term of at least one month, the 5% hotel occupancy tax may apply (`edu-rent-tax-as`), and zoning treats buildings rented to transient guests as hotels, so check the zone before offering short stays. Whether a short-stay guest is a tenant or a lodger rests on common law (case law not searched); if you treat a stay as a tenancy, use the court process to end it.

title: Court-Only Repossession: No Self-Help Eviction in American Samoa
bodyText: In American Samoa you may recover possession of a rented home only through the High Court. The possession statute allows entry onto premises only where the law permits it, and then only peaceably, never by force; the only process for removing a tenant is a written demand, a summary repossession case in the Trial Division, a judgment, and a writ carried out by the court marshal or a police officer (normally no sooner than 10 days after judgment). Don't change the locks, remove doors, windows or belongings, or cut off water or power to force a tenant out or to collect rent, whatever the lease says (`edu-no-lockout-for-rent-as`): the tenant may recover damages for wrongful entry or possession in the same or a separate case, may use the summary procedure against you if you took possession by force, and entering a home you have no right to enter can be criminal trespass. Disconnecting water or power for nonpayment is for the utility (ASPA) to do under its own rules, not for you (`edu-utility-service-continuity-as`). Federal law also makes it a crime to evict a servicemember or the servicemember's family from a covered home without a court order.

title: Servicemember Tenants in American Samoa
bodyText: Servicemember protections in American Samoa come from the federal Servicemembers Civil Relief Act, which applies in the territory by its own terms; we found no American Samoa law adding to it, and the territory has no National Guard of its own. Under the Act, you may not evict a servicemember or the servicemember's dependents from their home during military service without a court order if the rent is at or below a ceiling adjusted each year, and the court must, on request, stay the case for 90 days (or adjust the lease) where military service materially affects the ability to pay. A tenant who enters military service after signing, or who receives permanent change-of-station or deployment orders of at least 90 days, may end the lease by written notice with a copy of the orders; for monthly rent it ends 30 days after the next rent due date, you may charge no early-termination fee, and you must not hold back the tenant's deposit or belongings unlawfully. Within one year, the spouse or dependent of a servicemember who dies in service, and a servicemember with a catastrophic service injury or illness (or the spouse or dependent, if the servicemember lacks capacity), may also end such a lease. Before asking for a default judgment, check whether the tenant is in military service (the Act's affidavit rule was not reviewed for this library).

title: Late Benefit or Voucher Payments in American Samoa
bodyText: We found no American Samoa statute, regulation or court rule that requires a court to postpone a nonpayment case, gives the tenant a defence, or reinstates a tenancy because a Social Security payment, other government benefit or housing-voucher payment arrived late. The ordinary rules apply: a written demand and 7 days before you file, a trial within about 10 days, continuances only at the court's discretion and for no more than 7 days, and the tenant's right to pay the judgment amount and costs after judgment to keep the home (`edu-redemption-after-judgment-as`). If the tenancy is in a federal housing program, that program's rules may limit when and how you can end it (not reviewed for this library). If you know a payment is simply delayed, accepting it when it arrives is usually cheaper than a case, and agree any payment plan in writing.

title: When a Tenant May End a Lease Early Under American Samoa Law
bodyText: American Samoa law gives a tenant no territorial right to end a fixed-term lease early: we found no American Samoa statute, regulation or court rule releasing a tenant because of domestic violence, illness or age (`edu-no-infirmity-termination-as`), a job move, or your misrepresentation. Federal law adds two rules that reach the territory: the Servicemembers Civil Relief Act lets a servicemember end a residential lease on entering service or on qualifying orders, without an early-termination fee (`edu-servicemember-rights-as`), and in federally assisted housing the Violence Against Women Act bars evicting or ending assistance because a tenant is a victim of domestic violence, sexual assault or stalking. A domestic violence protection order can also remove an abuser from the home whatever the lease says. A tenant who signed because of your false statements may have common-law or consumer-law remedies (case law not searched). Otherwise a tenant who leaves early stays liable under the lease, subject to whatever early-termination term the lease contains and to your efforts to re-let.

title: Moving Out at the End of an American Samoa Lease
bodyText: A fixed-term American Samoa lease ends on its last day: we found no statute, regulation or court rule that requires good cause to end or not renew it, so the shared surrender clause, which asks the tenant to leave and return the keys at the end of the term "unless applicable law entitles Tenant to remain", fits. If the tenant stays, you recover possession only through the court after a written demand (`edu-holdover-as`), and for a home with a federally backed mortgage or in a federal housing program the CARES Act may require 30 days' notice to vacate. We also found no American Samoa rule on belongings left behind at move-out, so treat them cautiously: list and store them and give written notice before disposing of anything (`edu-post-eviction-property-as`).

title: Tenancies Without a Fixed Term in American Samoa
bodyText: We found no American Samoa statute, regulation or court rule that defines a tenancy at will or by sufferance or sets the notice needed to end one; the 30-day rule in the Code covers only government housing. Someone living in your property by permission with no agreed term or rent period is still covered by the possession statute, which treats a written or verbal lease or licence as a lease, so if the occupant won't leave you must end the permission, serve a written demand, and recover possession through the court. How much notice the common law requires is not settled in what we searched (case law not searched), so give clear written notice of at least one full rent period (and at least 30 days where there is no rent period) before serving the demand. Better still, put the arrangement in a written lease that states the term or the rent period and the notice either side must give (`periodic-tenancy-notice-as`).

title: When a Tenant Files for Bankruptcy
bodyText: We found no American Samoa statute, regulation or court rule on a tenant's bankruptcy: nothing makes bankruptcy a ground for ending a tenancy, sets a procedure when a tenant files, or limits a lease clause that treats bankruptcy as a default, and the territory has no bankruptcy or insolvency law of its own. Federal bankruptcy law (not reviewed for this library) may still matter: a court case note says that a filing in a federal bankruptcy court automatically stays related cases in the High Court. If a tenant tells you they have filed for bankruptcy anywhere, stop collection and repossession steps and get legal advice before going further. Otherwise, collect unpaid rent through the ordinary process, where the court sets a payment schedule that leaves the tenant enough to live on (`edu-landlord-remedies-termination-as`).

title: Damage Caused by a Tenant in American Samoa
bodyText: American Samoa law gives you three tools when a tenant damages the home. If the tenant willfully or negligently causes extensive and continuing physical injury to the premises and doesn't stop or repair it within 7 days after you serve a written demand, you may bring a repossession case and ask the court to issue the writ immediately rather than after 10 days. In that case, or separately, you may claim damages for waste or malicious destruction of the premises. And if the Department of Health makes you pay to abate a nuisance the tenant caused or allowed, the tenant must repay you. We found no American Samoa statute on fire or casualty damage, on rent while a damaged home is repaired, or setting a measure of the tenant's liability, so those rest on the lease and the common law (case law not searched); the library's optional tenant-caused damage clause (`tenant-caused-damage-nm`) makes the tenant liable for repair costs and lost rent when the tenant, a household member or someone on the premises with the tenant's consent causes the damage deliberately or negligently. Knowingly damaging another's property is also a crime.

title: When a Tenant Dies in American Samoa
bodyText: We found no American Samoa statute, regulation or court rule on what happens to a residential lease, the deposit or the tenant's belongings when a tenant dies: no rule ending the lease at a sole tenant's death, no affidavit or contact-person procedure, and no rule letting the lease name someone to remove property or receive the deposit. Under the common law (case law not searched) a fixed-term lease generally does not end on the tenant's death, so the tenant's estate may remain responsible. Deal with the person the High Court authorises: the administrator or executor, or, for a small estate (personal property worth up to $10,000), the person granted a transfer order on a sworn petition; if no family member petitions within 90 days, you as a creditor may petition yourself. Don't hand over belongings or the deposit to anyone without that authority. An optional emergency contact in the lease helps you reach family quickly but gives that person no right to the property (`tenant-death-contact-nh`). On communal land, family and matai arrangements may affect who stays (flagged only). If the tenant was a servicemember who died in service, the spouse or dependent may end the lease within a year.

title: Ending a Periodic Tenancy in American Samoa
bodyText: We found no American Samoa statute, regulation or court rule that sets the notice needed to end a month-to-month, week-to-week or other periodic residential tenancy, or that requires notice before a fixed term ends; the 30-day rule in the Code applies only to government housing. The common-law default is not settled in what we searched (case law not searched), so set the notice in the lease (`periodic-tenancy-notice-as`): a full rental period, and at least 30 days for a month-to-month tenancy, is the cautious minimum. A notice ending the tenancy does not by itself let you recover the home: if the tenant stays, serve the written demand for possession the possession statute requires, stating the reason and the time to leave, and then bring a repossession case (`edu-nonpayment-notice-as`). A fixed-term lease ends on its last day, when the surrender clause (`surrender-end-of-term`) has the tenant leave; you may still remind the tenant of the end date in writing. Before raising rent on a month-to-month tenancy instead, check whether the Governor or the President declared a state of emergency in the last 30 days, whether the Governor has extended the price-gouging period, and whether a declaration is still in effect (`edu-disaster-duties-as`).

title: Removing Unauthorized Occupants in American Samoa
bodyText: American Samoa has no fast-track way to remove squatters or other unauthorized occupants outside the courts: we found no rule letting police or the marshal remove someone on your sworn complaint, and no special squatting crime. What the law gives you: a summary repossession case against anyone who took possession by forcible entry, holds it by force, or came in by trespass without any claim of right, and in those cases the court may issue the writ immediately after judgment. Someone who knowingly enters or stays in a building without permission commits criminal trespass, so if a stranger has just broken in you can call the police; but a former tenant, a tenant's guest the tenant still welcomes, or anyone who claims a right to be there should be removed only through the court after a written demand. Don't use force or change the locks on someone in possession. On communal (native) land, disputes over who may occupy the land go to the Land and Titles Division and usually need a certificate from the Secretary of Samoan Affairs first (flagged; take advice).

title: Accepting Rent After a Breach or Demand in American Samoa
bodyText: We found no American Samoa statute, regulation or court rule that says whether accepting rent after a tenant's breach, after your written demand, or during a repossession case waives the breach, the demand or the case, and none prescribes wording to reserve your rights. The question rests on common law (case law not searched), and courts applying it have often treated accepting rent for a period after a demand or termination date as forgiving the breach or creating a new tenancy. So if you accept a payment after a breach or demand, give a written receipt saying what it is applied to and that you are not waiving the breach, the demand or the case (`rent-acceptance-nonwaiver-as`), and don't accept rent for a period after the date the tenancy is to end unless you mean to continue it. One payment you must accept: after a nonpayment judgment, the judgment amount plus taxed costs paid within the time allowed stops the writ (`edu-redemption-after-judgment-as`).

title: Agreed Ways of Giving Notice in American Samoa
bodyText: We found no American Samoa statute, regulation or court rule that defines when a landlord or tenant has actual notice, or that lets the parties agree on an extra way of giving notice (such as text message or e-mail) that then counts as a notice the law requires. For routine notices that no law prescribes (repair requests, reminders, notice of entry under the lease), you and the tenant may agree in the lease to use e-mail or text in addition to paper. For the written demand before a repossession case, use only the statute's methods: hand it to the tenant, leave it at the home with a household member or employee of suitable age and discretion, or send it by registered mail with a return receipt the tenant or the tenant's agent signs. Federal electronic-signature law, which reaches American Samoa, does not validate electronic delivery of eviction or default notices for a residential lease, so an e-mailed or texted demand alone is not enough.

title: Which Document Controls in an American Samoa Lease
bodyText: We found no American Samoa statute, regulation or court rule that requires a separate addendum that must control over a residential lease, or that says which document wins when the lease and an addendum conflict, so the shared Addendum Precedence clause (`addendum-precedence`) fits: the lease controls, except for any disclosure or addendum the law requires or says controls. Two territorial rules make the full set of documents matter. If the home is on communal (native) land, the Governor approves the lease on its full stated terms, so an addendum that changes those terms should go through the same approval (`edu-communal-land-lease-approval-as`). And a written lease is registered with the Territorial Registrar as an instrument, so register the lease with its addenda attached (`edu-lease-registration-as`).

title: Proceedings Against the Property: No Notice Statute in American Samoa
bodyText: We found no American Samoa statute, regulation or court rule that requires you to tell a tenant or applicant that the property faces foreclosure, condemnation, a lawsuit, a lien or another proceeding that could affect the tenancy, and none requires notice to tenants when the property is sold. Two rules mean tenants may learn of it anyway: a lender foreclosing under a power of sale must post a copy of the sale notice on the premises at least 21 days before the sale (`edu-foreclosure-tenants-as`), and when the Government takes land for public use its acquisition rules aim to give lawful occupants at least 90 days' written notice before they must move. Because the Consumer Protection Act may reach a residential lease, don't sign a new lease or take advance rent while concealing a scheduled sale or taking that will end the tenancy; tell applicants and tenants in writing. Whether a tenant must forward legal papers to you depends on the lease (`edu-no-tenant-forward-proceedings-as`).

title: Automatic Lease Renewal in American Samoa
bodyText: We found no American Samoa statute, regulation or court rule that regulates automatic-renewal terms in residential leases: there is no consumer auto-renewal law requiring bold type, an opt-in or a reminder before a lease renews. A lease may renew itself, or turn into a month-to-month tenancy at the end of the term, if it says so clearly. Because the Consumer Protection Act may reach a residential lease, make the renewal term and any notice the tenant must give to avoid it plain, and send a written reminder before the deadline. If the home is on communal (native) land, a renewal extends a lease that needed the Governor's approval and cannot take the total term past 55 years, so get approval for the renewal rather than relying on an automatic clause (`edu-communal-land-lease-approval-as`). If a renewal turns the tenancy into month-to-month, the price-gouging limit on rent increases applies from the declaration of a state of emergency until 30 days after the declaration (longer if the Governor extends it in further 30-day periods).

title: Arbitration Clauses in American Samoa Leases
bodyText: We found no American Samoa statute, regulation or court rule that authorizes or regulates arbitration clauses in residential leases, and the territory has no general arbitration act; the only arbitration statutes cover government land takings and a few special disputes. Possession cases belong in the Trial Division's summary repossession procedure, which is already fast (trial within about 10 days), and a clause sending possession or rent disputes to private arbitration could be struck as one-sided under the Consumer Protection Act if it reaches your lease. There is no civil jury in American Samoa, so a jury-waiver clause has nothing to do either. If you want a way to settle smaller disputes, offer voluntary mediation after a dispute arises instead. Federal law also matters here: the Federal Arbitration Act overrides state rules that block arbitration directly or indirectly (for example, a rule against giving up a jury), and the U.S. Supreme Court has held that renting out real estate is activity it reaches. On that basis the library now offers an optional clause, `arbitration-agreement`: money claims only, with possession, small claims, security-deposit, injury, emergency and government-agency matters kept out, every remedy and the right to a lawyer kept, the arbitration fees above a court filing fee paid by you, a 30-day opt-out for the tenant, and separate initials from both of you. Because state law points the other way, a court here could still refuse to enforce it; if one did, the dispute would simply go to court.

title: Other Rules American Samoa Does Not Have
bodyText: American Samoa has no residential landlord-tenant act: the word "landlord" appears only once in territorial law (in the hotel tax), and the only landlord-tenant statute is the summary repossession chapter. Many rules common elsewhere therefore do not exist here; each absence was searched across the whole corpus and is explained, with what the territory does have nearby, in its own section: no just-cause rule (`edu-for-cause-eviction-as`), no landlord's lien or distress (`edu-no-landlord-lien-as`), no lockout procedure (`edu-no-lockout-for-rent-as`), no possession bond (`edu-no-possession-bond-as`), no rent-into-court rule (`edu-no-rent-into-court-as`), no notice-fee rule (`edu-no-notice-service-fee-as`), no liquidated-damages rule (`edu-no-liquidated-damages-rule-as`), no self-cure statute (`edu-no-landlord-self-cure-as`), no repair-cost termination (`edu-no-repair-cost-termination-as`), no illness or care-facility termination (`edu-no-infirmity-termination-as`), no tenant-death statute (`edu-tenant-death-as`), no tenant-bankruptcy rule (`edu-no-tenant-bankruptcy-rule-as`), no seasonal-tenancy rules (`edu-no-seasonal-tenancy-rule-as`), no lease-arbitration statute (`edu-no-lease-arbitration-statute-as`), no auto-renewal rule (`edu-no-automatic-renewal-rule-as`) and no duty to disclose proceedings against the property (`edu-no-adverse-proceeding-notice-as`). Where the law is silent the lease governs, read with the common law (case law not searched), so write the point into the lease and take the cautious course each section describes.

title: Checked Across All of American Samoa Law
bodyText: Three things landlords ask about, checked across all of American Samoa's statutes, regulations and court rules, not only the possession chapter. (1) Squatters: there is no fast removal outside the courts; use a summary repossession case, which allows an immediate writ against trespassers, or report criminal trespass (`edu-unauthorized-occupants-as`). (2) Rent receipts: see `edu-rent-receipts-as`. (3) Registration: there is no landlord or rental-unit registration, and no rule makes registration a condition of a possession judgment. Two related rules matter, though: renting property regularly for gain is likely a business that needs a territorial business licence (a court case note suggests the court may refuse to enforce gains from unlicensed business, so whether an unlicensed landlord can win a possession case is unsettled; case law not searched), and registering a written lease with the Territorial Registrar protects your position and affects the court rules on post-judgment payment (`edu-lease-registration-as`). Get the business licence and register the lease. American Samoa's limited liability company law (A.S.C.A. ch. 30.06) was not available from an official source when this was written, so whether an unregistered or out-of-territory LLC may bring a possession case is not covered here; if you own through an LLC, confirm with the Department of Commerce that it is properly registered before you file.

title: Domestic Violence Law Citations Current in American Samoa
bodyText: American Samoa has no landlord-tenant statute that points to its domestic violence law, so no cross-reference has gone stale. The protection-order law is current and sits in Title 47 of the Code (enacted in 2004): a court may order an abuser out of the victim's home whatever the ownership, keep the abuser away, and, after a hearing, order the abuser to pay rent on the victim's home where the abuser owes support. If a tenant shows you a protection order excluding a household member, respect it: don't let the excluded person back in, and change the locks at the tenant's request if the order gives the tenant possession. American Samoa has no territorial lease-release right for victims (`edu-statutory-early-termination-as`); in federally assisted housing, the Violence Against Women Act applies.

title: Signing an American Samoa Lease Electronically
bodyText: American Samoa has no electronic-transactions act of its own, but the federal E-SIGN Act reaches the territory, so a lease signed electronically by you and the tenant may not be denied effect just because it is electronic, and the shared Electronic Signatures clause (`electronic-signatures`) records the parties' consent. If a law requires you to give the tenant information in writing, an electronic copy counts only if the tenant has first consented to electronic records after the disclosures E-SIGN requires; give the tenant a copy they can print or keep. E-SIGN does not cover notices of default, repossession or eviction for a home, and the possession statute lists only personal, household and registered-mail service for the demand, so serve those on paper (`edu-no-agreed-notice-method-rule-as`). If the lease will be registered with the Territorial Registrar, or the home is on communal (native) land where the lease must be a properly drawn and attested instrument confirmed by the Governor, sign a paper original as well.

title: Emergency Contacts for American Samoa Tenants
bodyText: We found no American Samoa statute, regulation or court rule that requires you to give tenants an emergency or 24-hour contact number, or to collect an emergency contact from each tenant, and none that says what a named contact may do. You may ask for one: the library's optional shared clause (`tenant-death-contact-nh`) lets the tenant name a contact, and naming a contact gives that person no right to occupy the home or take belongings; if the tenant dies, the person the High Court authorizes deals with the estate (`edu-tenant-death-as`). Because the territory is exposed to cyclones, tsunamis and other declared emergencies, give tenants a working number for urgent repairs and keep a current contact for each household, so you can reach them before and after a storm.

title: No Energy-Data Release Rule in American Samoa
bodyText: We found no American Samoa statute, regulation or court rule that requires energy benchmarking of residential buildings or governs a lease term letting the power utility release a tenant's usage data to you; the territory's energy-efficiency rules are building-design standards, and the library offers no data-release clause. If the tenant holds the ASPA account and you need usage information, ask the tenant to share the bills or the meter-reading notices ASPA leaves at the home, or to authorize ASPA in writing. If you hold the account and pass charges on to the tenant, show the readings you rely on (`edu-utilities-responsibility-as`).

title: Entire Agreement and Lease Changes in American Samoa
bodyText: The library's Entire Agreement section works in American Samoa as written. We found no American Samoa statute, regulation or court rule that lets you change an existing lease by written notice, whether to comply with a new law or for any other reason, and none that regulates entire-agreement clauses, so the clause's exception for changes the law lets you make by notice has nothing to operate on here. A change during the term therefore needs the tenant's agreement: put it in a writing both of you sign. American Samoa applies the common law of contracts where no statute speaks (case law not searched), and that is the cautious course. Two writing rules make a signed amendment matter: any agreement to pay interest above 6% a year must be in a writing the tenant signs, and if you registered the lease with the Territorial Registrar, register a signed amendment that changes the term, the rent or the property too, so the public record matches the lease you will attach to any eviction complaint.

title: American Samoa Law Governs an American Samoa Lease
bodyText: An American Samoa lease names the law of the Territory of American Samoa, not a state, county or city; the library's American Samoa version of the Governing Law section (`governing-law-as`) does this. By statute the law in force is the territory's Revised Constitution, the parts of the U.S. Constitution and federal laws that apply by their own force (for example the federal Fair Housing Act), the American Samoa Code Annotated and the rules issued under it, and so much of the common law of England as suits local conditions. There are no county or city ordinances, but village councils may adopt village regulations on strictly local matters (cleanliness, planting, roads), approved by the Department of Samoan Affairs, posted by the pulenuu and enforced in the village courts; they may not conflict with territorial or federal law. Samoan custom is preserved where it does not conflict with the law, and it can matter on communal land (who may grant a lease, and village rules on conduct). Ask about any village regulations where the property is, and follow them as rules of the property. We found no American Samoa statute that limits a lease's choice of law; an action to recover possession under the summary repossession chapter is brought in the Trial Division of the High Court.

title: Settling Disputes Before Court in American Samoa
bodyText: We found no American Samoa statute, regulation or court rule that requires, regulates or forbids a lease term asking you and the tenant to try to settle a dispute informally before going to court, so the library's informal dispute resolution clause (`informal-dispute-resolution-or`), which leaves possession actions and legal deadlines untouched, works here as a contract term. Keep it non-binding: an action to recover possession under the summary repossession chapter starts with the written demand and goes to the Trial Division on the statute's own timetable, and no lease term should delay it. One settlement step is required by law: before a lawsuit over communal (native) land or a matai title can be filed in the Land and Titles Division, the parties must appear twice before the Secretary of Samoan Affairs (or a deputy) and two persons the Secretary designates, without lawyers, to try to resolve it, and the complaint must carry the Secretary's certificate of irreconcilable dispute. Since 2023 a matter not completed there within six months is sent on to the Land and Titles Division. If your rental is on communal land and the dispute is really about the land (for example the family's or matai's right to lease it), expect that process; ask your lawyer which Division and procedure fit your case.

title: Business Licences and Guest-Worker Hosts in American Samoa
bodyText: American Samoa has no landlord registry, rental licence or rental-unit registration, and no real estate broker or property-manager licensing law. The general business licensing law can still reach you: no person may engage in business in American Samoa without a business licence, "business" means any regular activity carried on for gain (even part-time), and violating the law is a class B misdemeanor. Renting homes is not a named class; the fee for "all other business" is $150 a year, a separate licence is needed for each location, and the Territorial Planning Commission decides any classification question. Whether renting out one home is "carrying on a business" is not settled (case law not searched), so the cautious course is to apply to the Treasurer for a business licence if you rent regularly, and always if you rent several units or through a company. An owner who is not an American Samoan or a permanent resident (or a company majority-owned by such persons) is referred to the Commission for a hearing before a licence issues. A corporation formed outside American Samoa also needs a permit from the Governor before it transacts any business here (A.S.C.A. § 30.0305; `edu-nonresident-owner-agent-as`). If you house a cannery or call-center guest worker for rent, the law makes you a "host": your affidavit supporting the guest worker permit application must include a copy of your business licence and a written rent agreement stating the term, the monthly rent and the facilities, you may host no more than 5 guest workers at a time, and taking wages beyond the agreed rent by coercion is a felony.

title: No Blank-Spaces Rule in American Samoa
bodyText: We found no American Samoa statute, regulation or court rule that requires every blank in a written lease to be filled in, or that treats an incomplete lease as a breach by you. Fill in every blank anyway (write "none" or "N/A" where a blank does not apply) before the tenant signs. In a summary repossession case you must attach a copy of the lease to your complaint, and a blank where the rent, the term or the property should be invites a dispute about what was agreed that the court will resolve on the evidence. If the property is communal (native) land, the provisional lease agreement you submit for the Governor's approval must state all its terms and conditions in full (`edu-communal-land-lease-approval-as`). The Consumer Protection Act may reach a residential lease (unsettled), so do not leave terms open to be filled in later in a way that could mislead the tenant.

title: What an American Samoa Lease Needs to Say
bodyText: No American Samoa statute lists everything a residential lease must contain, and none prescribes a lease form, but several rules work only if the lease (or another signed writing) says something. Put these in the lease when they apply: (1) a power to end the lease for breach, because the summary repossession chapter lets you recover possession after termination "pursuant to a power to terminate provided in the lease or implied by law" (the library's default sections supply it); (2) any interest on late rent above 6% a year, which is enforceable only in a writing the tenant signs and may never exceed 15%; (3) if the rental is a cannery or call-center guest worker's housing, a written rent agreement stating the term, the monthly rent and the facilities provided. Acceleration does not help a nonpayment case: "rent due" for the 7-day nonpayment demand excludes rent accelerated because of a breach. On communal (native) land, the provisional lease agreement must state all its terms in full and has no validity until the Governor approves it in writing (`edu-communal-land-lease-approval-as`); a lease of government land for more than 4 years must contain an inflation-adjustment clause. Register a written lease with the Territorial Registrar (`edu-lease-registration-as`).

title: Giving the Tenant a Copy of the Lease
bodyText: We found no American Samoa statute, regulation or court rule that requires a landlord, or a broker or manager acting for one, to give the tenant a copy of the signed lease, and none that makes a missing copy a defence to enforcing the lease; American Samoa does not license real estate brokers or property managers. Give each tenant a complete signed copy anyway, at signing, and keep your own original. In a summary repossession case your complaint must attach a copy of the lease (if there is one) and of your written demand, and the tenant will compare them with the copy they hold. If you register the lease with the Territorial Registrar, the registered copy becomes a public record anyone may inspect. The optional receipt clause (`lease-copy-receipt-hi`) records that the tenant got a copy and any rules attached.

title: No Lease Initials Requirement
bodyText: We found no American Samoa statute, regulation or court rule that requires a tenant to initial particular lease clauses, or that makes a clause enforceable only if it is initialed, separately signed or printed conspicuously. The tenant's signature on the lease is what binds the tenant, and the summary repossession chapter even reaches oral leases. One term needs the tenant's signature on the writing itself: any interest above 6% a year on overdue rent, which is enforceable only if it is in a writing signed by the tenant. Asking for initials beside terms that matter most (the rent, the term, any late fee or interest, any fee for an extra occupant or pet) is still good practice, because a court applying the common law or the Consumer Protection Act (whose reach to leases is unsettled) may ask whether the tenant knew of a one-sided term (case law not searched).

title: Lease Length Limits in American Samoa
bodyText: How long a lease may run depends on the land. Communal (native) land: a lease needs the Governor's written approval and may not exceed 55 years, and a lease of native land for a school may not exceed 30 years per term; within 2 months after approval the lessee must deposit a properly drawn, legally attested lease for confirmation under the Governor's hand and seal (`edu-communal-land-lease-approval-as`). Government land: a lease longer than 4 years must contain an inflation-adjustment clause, and one longer than 6 years also a rent-renegotiation clause. Individually owned and freehold land: we found no American Samoa statute, regulation or court rule setting a minimum or maximum term, or requiring a seal, notarization or other special formality for a long lease. American Samoa's land statute of frauds covers agreements for the "sale" of real property or any interest in it; whether it reaches a lease is unsettled (`edu-statute-of-frauds-lease-as`), so put every lease, and certainly any lease longer than a year, in a writing both parties sign. A written lease is not effectual to pass an interest in the land until it is registered with the Territorial Registrar, and registration gives notice of it to later buyers and lenders; whether an unregistered lease still binds you and the tenant is unsettled (case law not searched) (`edu-lease-registration-as`).

title: When an American Samoa Lease Must Be in Writing
bodyText: American Samoa's statute of frauds for land says no agreement for the sale of real property "or of any interest therein" is valid unless it, or a note or memorandum of it, is in writing and signed by the party to be charged (or an agent authorized in writing), though a court may still order specific performance after part performance. It does not mention leases, and no other statute sets a writing rule for leases by length; the summary repossession chapter expressly covers verbal leases, so a month-to-month oral tenancy can still be enforced through it. Whether a lease is a "sale" of an interest in land under the statute of frauds is unsettled (case law not searched). The cautious course: put every lease in writing signed by you and every adult tenant, and have anyone signing for you hold written authority. Writing matters for other reasons too: a lease of communal (native) land has no validity until the Governor approves it in writing (`edu-communal-land-lease-approval-as`); only a written instrument can be registered with the Territorial Registrar (`edu-lease-registration-as`); and any interest above 6% a year on overdue rent is enforceable only in a writing the tenant signs.

title: No Lease Type-Size Rule
bodyText: We found no American Samoa statute, regulation or court rule that sets a minimum type size or typeface for a residential lease or a landlord notice, or that makes small print inadmissible or unenforceable. American Samoa sets type sizes only for other documents (insurance policies, notary fee schedules, some court papers and orders). Print the lease in a readable size (10-point or larger is a sensible floor), and make the written demand for possession easy to read, because the summary repossession chapter requires its reasons and the time to cure to be "clearly stated". Many tenants read Samoan more easily than English; see `edu-translation-duty-as`.

title: Lease and Notice Language in American Samoa
bodyText: Samoan and English are both official languages of American Samoa (since 2022), but we found no American Samoa statute, regulation or court rule that requires you to write a lease in Samoan, translate it, or give a landlord notice in a particular language, even when the tenancy was negotiated in Samoan. The law uses both languages where it wants them: the court's summons in a summary repossession case is issued in Samoan and English, and if you ask the court for a default judgment you must serve the tenant written notice of the application, in English and in Samoan, at least 10 days before the hearing. Because the written demand for possession must state its reasons and the time to cure clearly, and a tenant who did not understand the lease may dispute what was agreed (case law not searched), the cautious course is to give a Samoan translation of the lease and of every demand to a tenant who reads Samoan more easily than English, state which version controls, and keep a signed copy of both.

title: Statutory Forms and Prescribed Text in American Samoa
bodyText: American Samoa supplies no statutory lease form and prescribes no verbatim text that a residential lease must contain. The one landlord document with set contents is the written demand for possession or payment that starts a summary repossession case: it must be in writing, addressed to the person in possession, identify the premises, state clearly the reasons and the time to take remedial action, state the amount due if you claim unpaid rent or other sums, and be dated and signed by you or your lawyer or agent; the law prescribes those contents, not its words, and a copy must be attached to your complaint. The court rules prescribe the form of the writ of repossession the court issues after judgment, and the Territorial Registrar uses a prescribed bilingual notice when an agreement separating a house from communal land is offered for recording. For a lease of communal (native) land, follow the Land Commission's and Governor's approval process (`edu-communal-land-lease-approval-as`).

title: Owners Living Off-Island
bodyText: We found no American Samoa statute, regulation or court rule that requires an owner who lives off-island to name a local agent in the lease, to file an agent designation before suing a tenant, or to hire a licensed broker or manager (American Samoa does not license them). Other rules still reach you. If you own through a limited liability company it must keep a registered agent with a place of business in the territory, and a foreign corporation may not transact any business in American Samoa without first getting a permit from the Governor; its application must name a resident agent for service of process, and if that agent can't be found, process may be served through the Treasurer. A foreign corporation doing business without a permit forfeits $100 for each day, and an agent, officer or employee who knowingly transacts business for it commits a class C misdemeanor. We found no rule barring an unpermitted corporation from suing, and whether renting out property is transacting business is not settled (case law not searched) (A.S.C.A. §§ 30.0302(6), 30.0305, 30.0310, 30.0314). American Samoa's limited liability company law (A.S.C.A. ch. 30.06) was not available from an official source when this was written, so whether an unregistered or out-of-territory LLC may bring a possession case is not covered here; if you own through an LLC, confirm with the Department of Commerce that it is properly registered before you file. If you need a business licence to rent (`edu-landlord-registration-as`) and you are not an American Samoan or a permanent resident, your application is referred to the Territorial Planning Commission for a hearing. American Samoa's income tax adopts the federal chapter on withholding tax from payments to nonresident aliens and foreign corporations, so a tenant or manager paying rent to such an owner may have to withhold; get tax advice before collecting rent from off-island. Practically, name a local manager or agent in the lease who can sign and serve the written demand for possession (the law lets your agent sign it), receive notices and appear for you.

title: How Notices Must Be Delivered in American Samoa
bodyText: American Samoa law sets delivery methods for one landlord notice: the written demand for possession or payment that starts a summary repossession case. Serve it in one of three ways: hand it to the tenant; leave it at the premises with a member of the tenant's family or household, or an employee, of suitable age and discretion, asking that it be given to the tenant; or send it by registered mail, return receipt requested, signed by the tenant or the tenant's authorized agent. A mailed demand is served only on the date the tenant (or agent) actually receives it, so the 7-day period runs from that date; if the tenant will not sign for the letter, deliver the demand by hand. Posting on the door and e-mail are not listed methods. American Samoa has no electronic-transactions act; the federal E-SIGN Act applies here but does not cover notices of default, eviction or the right to cure under a lease of a tenant's primary residence, so deliver those on paper. For other notices the lease decides: the shared optional e-mail clause (`electronic-notice-ma`) works for routine notices because it excludes default and eviction notices. A tenant who is a servicemember may deliver a lease termination notice by hand, private carrier, return-receipt mail or electronic means.

title: The Notices Clause in American Samoa
bodyText: The library's Notices section (`notices`) works in American Samoa as written: it sends notices to the addresses in the lease and lets any method American Samoa law requires control. Only one notice has a required method: the written demand for possession or payment, which must be delivered by hand, left at the premises with a household member or employee of suitable age and discretion, or sent by registered mail with a return receipt signed by the tenant or the tenant's agent (`edu-notice-delivery-methods-as`). Fill in for each party both a place for hand delivery (for the premises without a street address, the village and a brief description, which the demand must also include) and a mailing address for registered mail, and tell the tenant in writing of any change. The demand may be signed by you, your lawyer or your agent; name in the lease who may sign notices for you if you use a manager. Electronic notice is suitable only for routine matters (`electronic-notice-ma`).

title: Which American Samoa Notices Must Be in Writing
bodyText: American Samoa law requires one landlord notice to be in writing: the demand for possession or payment that must precede every summary repossession case, whether for unpaid rent (7 days after service), a serious and continuing health hazard or extensive damage (7 days after service), holding over after the lease ends or is terminated, or another breach. It must be written, addressed to the person in possession, identify the premises, state the reasons and the time to take remedial action, state any amount claimed, and be dated and signed by you, your lawyer or your agent. We found no American Samoa statute, regulation or court rule that requires other lease notices (ending a month-to-month tenancy, entry, rent changes, rules) to be in writing, so the lease does that work; the library's lease requires written notice for them and you should follow it. Two federal rules also call for writing: a tenant who enters military service or gets qualifying orders ends the lease by written notice with a copy of the orders, and if the property has a federally backed mortgage or is in a covered federal housing program you may not require a tenant to vacate until 30 days after you give a notice to vacate (give it in writing so you can prove the date).

title: No Rule on Move-Out Notice Forms or Work During a Notice Period
bodyText: We found no American Samoa statute, regulation or court rule on a move-out or notice-to-vacate form you ask a tenant to sign: no required warning when such a form adds terms the lease does not contain, and no rule on what happens to added terms. We also found no rule barring renovation or other work that makes the unit hard to live in while a notice to vacate is pending. Keep any such form to the facts (the address, the date the tenant will leave, how keys will be returned); do not use it to add charges or waive rights, because the tenant may argue the added terms were never agreed, and the Consumer Protection Act may reach a lease (unsettled). The tenancy and your obligations continue until the tenant actually leaves or a court orders possession: do not cut services or start disruptive work to push the tenant out, which could support a retaliation defence (if it follows a lawful act by the tenant) and amounts to the self-help the law does not permit; possession is recovered only through the court.

title: Changing Rent or Terms in American Samoa
bodyText: We found no American Samoa statute, regulation or court rule that sets a notice period or form for changing the rent or any other term of a residential tenancy, or that treats a rent change differently from a change to a fee or a rule. During a fixed term you may change terms only as the lease itself allows or with the tenant's signed agreement. For a month-to-month or other periodic tenancy, the usual common-law route is notice ending the current tenancy and offering a new one on the changed terms, but the notice needed rests on common law (case law not searched): give written notice at least one full rental period ahead, ending on the last day of a period, and state the new terms. Two limits apply: from a declared state of emergency until 30 days after the declaration (longer if the Governor extends it in further 30-day periods), you may not raise a month-to-month rent more than 10% above the rent charged just before it (unless the increase is directly attributable to added costs, within the statute's limits); and a court will refuse possession if you raised the tenant's obligations as a penalty for a lawful act and the tenant's refusal to meet them was the main reason you ended the tenancy.

title: Where American Samoa Law Lets Your Lease Decide
bodyText: Because American Samoa has no residential landlord-tenant act, most terms are for the lease to decide under the common law (case law not searched), and only a few statutes turn on what the lease says. (1) Termination for breach: the summary repossession chapter lets you recover possession after the lease is ended "pursuant to a power to terminate provided in the lease or implied by law", so keep the library's default and termination sections, which supply that power. (2) Interest on late rent: with no written agreement, 6% a year applies to overdue debts; a higher rate (never above 15%) needs a writing the tenant signs (see the late fee and interest rows). (3) Registration: the court rules withdraw the post-judgment chance to pay and keep the home where you exercise a lease termination clause or no written lease is registered, but the statute gives a tenant evicted for nonpayment that chance without exception, so assume it applies whatever the lease says; register a written lease anyway (`edu-lease-registration-as`). (4) Communal (native) land: the lease needs the Governor's written approval (`edu-communal-land-lease-approval-as`). Write the rent due date, place and method, the term and renewal, and any fees into the lease, because no statute fills those gaps.

title: Landlord Size Thresholds in American Samoa
bodyText: American Samoa has no small-landlord exemption and no duties that start at a portfolio size: the summary repossession chapter, the retaliation defence and the other territorial rules apply the same way to a landlord with one room or many units. A few rules turn on counts. (1) Federal Fair Housing Act (it applies in American Samoa): a private owner of no more than three single-family houses who rents one without a broker, and an owner who lives in a building of up to four units, are exempt from most of the Act's discrimination rules, but never from its ban on discriminatory advertising; the Act's accessible-design rules apply to newer buildings of 4 or more units. (2) Guest-worker hosts may house no more than 5 cannery or call-center guest workers at a time. (3) Solid waste: an apartment establishment of 2 or more dwelling units licensed to provide lodging for hire is a "business" that must arrange collection of all its solid waste, and for rented units the "owner" responsible is the person to whom the rent is paid. (4) Business licence: one licence is needed for each business location (`edu-landlord-registration-as`). The zoning chapter calls a building of 3 or more dwelling units a "multiple dwelling".

title: No Renter's-Insurance Statute in American Samoa
bodyText: We found no American Samoa statute, regulation or court rule on renter's insurance in a residential lease: none bars you from requiring it, lets the tenant choose the carrier by statute, governs coverage you buy and charge back if the tenant fails to show proof, or requires a written notice that your insurance does not cover the tenant's belongings. You may require renter's insurance with a liability minimum you choose as a lease term; the library uses the shared clause without a liability disclaimer (`tenants-property-insurance-ks-oh-ca`) for American Samoa. If you want to buy coverage for a tenant who does not show proof and charge for it, say so in the lease with the amount or how it is calculated, and charge only the actual premium, since the Consumer Protection Act may reach a lease (unsettled). Do not use the insurance requirement to shift to the tenant losses the lease or the law makes yours.

title: Renter's Insurance Clause in American Samoa
bodyText: American Samoa uses the library's renter's-insurance clause without a liability disclaimer (`tenants-property-insurance-ks-oh-ca`): it says your insurance does not cover the tenant's belongings and requires the tenant to carry renter's insurance with a liability minimum you choose. We found no American Samoa statute that voids a "Landlord is not liable" term, but whether a residential lease may excuse a landlord from its own negligence rests on the common law and possibly the Consumer Protection Act's rule against unconscionable terms (case law not searched), so the library does not use the shared clauses that add a disclaimer. No American Samoa statute forbids, or expressly allows, requiring the tenant's insurance to pay for repairs that are yours under the lease; keep the clause to the tenant's own belongings and liability.

title: Selling the Property or Changing Managers
bodyText: We found no American Samoa statute, regulation or court rule that governs a residential lease when you sell the property or change managers: no required notice to tenants, no statutory release of the selling landlord, no rule moving the security deposit to the buyer, and no seller disclosure tied to the tenancy. Registration matters: a lease registered with the Territorial Registrar is notice of its contents to everyone who later deals with the land, so a buyer takes subject to it; whether a buyer is bound by an unregistered lease rests on common law (case law not searched), another reason to register (`edu-lease-registration-as`). Sales themselves are restricted: land other than freehold land may not be alienated to a person of less than one-half Samoan blood, communal land needs the Governor's written approval, and a corporation may not acquire any interest in land unless the Governor approves in writing and the Registrar records it. Good practice on a sale: tell tenants in writing who the new landlord is and where to pay rent, transfer or account for every deposit in writing, and have the buyer confirm in the sale contract that it takes subject to the leases. On a change of manager, tell tenants in writing who may now sign and receive notices.

title: Which American Samoa Laws Govern a Residential Lease
bodyText: American Samoa has no residential landlord-tenant act, no mobile-home park act and no separate rules for farm or student leases; long-term limits exist only for communal and government land (`edu-lease-term-limits-as`). What governs a residential lease is: the lease itself, read with the common law of contracts (case law not searched); the summary repossession chapter (Title 43, chapter 14) and its court rules, which apply to every "premises" (houses, apartments, condominiums, rooms, mobile trailer homes, vessels and vehicles used as dwellings, and commercial space) and every written or oral lease or licence to occupy; scattered statutes on interest, consumer protection, price gouging, health and building safety; and federal laws that apply by their own terms, such as the Fair Housing Act, the Servicemembers Civil Relief Act, the CARES Act notice rule and E-SIGN. Land status changes the rules: a lease of communal (native) land needs the Governor's written approval and is limited to 55 years (`edu-communal-land-lease-approval-as`), land controversies (including evictions from land and removal of structures) go to the Land and Titles Division, and Samoan custom and village rules may matter on communal land. Government housing has its own chapter and does not govern private rentals.

title: Severability in American Samoa
bodyText: The library's severability clause (`severability`) works in American Samoa as written, with two land-status cautions. American Samoa's rules on improper terms mostly strike or limit the offending term: under the Consumer Protection Act (if it reaches a lease, which is unsettled) a court may strike or limit an unconscionable clause, and the territory's own statutes are declared severable. Some rules reach the whole deal, and a severability clause cannot save it: a lease of communal (native) land has no validity until the Governor approves it in writing (`edu-communal-land-lease-approval-as`); an alienation of land in violation of the land chapter is void and can cost a non-native lessee the improvements made; and if a late fee or interest is treated as interest above the legal rate, the usury statute forfeits the whole debt on which it was charged, not just the excess (case law not searched on whether rent is a "debt or obligation" for this purpose). Keep fees and interest within the limits in the rent rows so no clause puts the rent itself at risk.

title: Tenant Portals and Electronic Dealings in American Samoa
bodyText: We found no American Samoa statute, regulation or court rule that addresses tenant portals or bars you from requiring rent, signatures or maintenance requests to go through one. The federal E-SIGN Act applies in American Samoa and sets the limits: no one is required to agree to electronic records or signatures, so get the tenant's agreement to sign and receive documents electronically (in the lease or a separate consent) and keep a paper route for a tenant who withdraws it. A portal can never carry the written demand for possession or any default, cure or eviction notice: serve those by hand, by delivery to a household member, or by registered mail (`edu-notice-delivery-methods-as`). If you require payment through a portal, also accept another method for a tenant without a bank account or card (see the payment-method rows), since United States currency is the territory's only legal tender for debts, and do not charge portal fees the lease does not state.

title: Tenant Records in American Samoa
bodyText: We found no American Samoa statute, regulation or court rule that requires a residential landlord to keep a rent ledger, give a receipt or statement of account on request, attach a ledger to a notice, or keep tenant files for a set time, and no general data-security or breach-notice law for private businesses. Good records still decide your cases: the written demand for nonpayment must state the amount due, and the court states the arrears in the judgment (less any rent excused by your breach), which is the amount the tenant may pay to stop the writ. Keep a running ledger of charges and payments for each tenancy and give a written receipt for every cash payment.
