One tax rule reaches some rentals: American Samoa's 5% hotel room tax covers lodging houses, rooming houses and apartment houses, and requires the owner to collect it, state it separately on the receipt, keep daily records and file quarterly returns; a tenant who holds a written lease of at least one month is exempt only for a quarter in which the tenant occupied, or had the right to occupy, the room for the whole quarter, the room was not also let short-stay, and the tenant did not sublet or assign it (`edu-rent-tax-as`). If you rent rooms or apartments for short stays or without written monthly leases, get tax advice. Protect applicants' Social Security numbers and bank details: keep them only as long as you need them and store them securely.

title: No Sunset on American Samoa Tenant Protections
bodyText: We found no American Samoa statute, regulation or court rule that puts a tenant-protection law on a repeal or expiration clock. The summary repossession chapter (with its retaliation defence and the post-judgment chance to pay), the interest limits, the Consumer Protection Act and the land-tenure rules carry no sunset date. The one time-limited rule is the price-gouging limit on month-to-month rents, which applies from a declared state of emergency until 30 days after the declaration, unless the Governor extends it in further 30-day periods; check whether an emergency has been declared before raising a month-to-month rent (`edu-no-term-change-notice-rule-as`). Watch for new public laws: the published Code compilation runs only to 2021, and later laws are issued separately.

title: Service and Assistance Animals in American Samoa Rentals
bodyText: American Samoa has no territorial law on service or assistance animals in housing; the federal Fair Housing Act applies here and governs. Treat a service or support animal that a tenant or occupant needs because of a disability as a reasonable accommodation, not a pet: waive no-pet, breed, size and weight rules for it, charge no pet deposit, pet rent or pet fee for it, and ask for reliable documentation only when the disability or the disability-related need is not obvious. You may refuse or withdraw the accommodation for a specific animal that is a direct threat to others' health or safety or would cause substantial physical damage that another accommodation cannot reduce, and the tenant remains responsible for damage it does. American Samoa uses the library's shared clause (`assistance-animal-accommodation`), which tracks the federal rules. Territorial animal laws still apply to an assistance animal: dogs must be licensed, and dogs and cats may be brought into American Samoa only from approved places on the Department of Agriculture's conditions.

title: Penalty for Refusing an Assistance Animal
bodyText: We found no American Samoa statute, regulation or court rule that makes it an offence, or sets a territorial penalty, to refuse housing to a person because of a service or assistance animal. The federal Fair Housing Act, which applies in American Samoa, does make refusing a reasonable accommodation for an assistance animal unlawful discrimination, and it is also unlawful to coerce, intimidate, threaten or interfere with a tenant who asks for one; the remedies are federal. Handle every request under `edu-assistance-animals-as` and the shared clause `assistance-animal-accommodation`, decide promptly, and keep a written record of the request and your answer.

title: No Penalty for Misrepresenting an Assistance Animal
bodyText: We found no American Samoa statute, regulation or court rule that makes it an offence to misrepresent a pet as a service or assistance animal, in housing or anywhere else. Your protection is the federal process: when the disability or the need for the animal is not obvious, you may ask for reliable documentation of the disability-related need, and you may decline an accommodation that is not supported or for an animal that is a direct threat or would cause substantial damage (`edu-assistance-animals-as`).

title: Pets in American Samoa Rentals
bodyText: American Samoa law lets you allow, limit or forbid pets by lease, and gives no group of tenants a right to keep one; assistance animals are different (`edu-assistance-animals-as`). Territorial animal laws apply at your rental: dogs must be licensed, and unlicensed dogs, and pigs, goats and other livestock allowed to run loose, may be impounded and destroyed; no owner or occupant may keep pigs, goats, sheep, horses or cattle within 50 feet of a building used for human habitation; and a vicious animal (one that, without provocation, has attacked or bitten a person or snarls, snaps, growls, claws or otherwise behaves so as to intimidate or frighten a person, including on its owner's command) may not be kept at all and is seized by the Department of Public Safety. Write those rules into your pet terms. Nothing gives you a right to enter and seize or remove a tenant's pet: entry must be permitted by law and peaceable, possession is recovered only through the court, and the library uses the pet clause without a removal power (`pet-policy-or`) for American Samoa; report a dangerous animal to the Department of Public Safety instead.

title: Pet Deposits and Pet Rent
bodyText: We found no American Samoa statute, regulation or court rule on pet deposits, pet fees or pet rent: none caps them, defines a pet deposit as a security deposit, or bars a non-refundable pet fee, and American Samoa has no security-deposit statute. The lease decides. State any pet rent as part of the rent and any pet deposit as money held to secure the tenant's obligations, refundable under the same terms as the security deposit, and state any one-time pet fee and what it covers. No pet charge may be made for an assistance animal under the federal Fair Housing Act (`edu-assistance-animals-as`). Keep pet charges tied to real costs, since the Consumer Protection Act may reach a lease (unsettled).

title: Pet Liability Insurance
bodyText: We found no American Samoa statute, regulation or court rule that bars or regulates a lease term requiring a tenant with a pet to carry liability insurance covering the pet or to name you as an interested party, so the shared clause (`pet-insurance-requirement`) works as written. The reason to use it: a person bitten or injured by a tenant's animal may sue, and American Samoa lets an injured person sue a liability insurer directly. Keeping a vicious animal is a crime here, and if it injures someone in an unprovoked attack the keeper commits a felony; a lease ban on such animals plus the insurance requirement protects you. The clause's exception for assistance animals follows the federal Fair Housing Act.

title: No Pet and Eviction Fact Sheet
bodyText: We found no American Samoa statute, regulation or court rule that requires you to give a tenant a fact sheet, notice or lease disclosure about pets and eviction, or to notify any agency when a tenant with a pet is evicted. Pet terms are a matter of the lease (`edu-pet-policy-as`). If a tenant leaves an animal behind, do not abandon or destroy it; contact the tenant and, for a dangerous or loose animal, the Department of Public Safety or the Department of Agriculture.

title: Caring for a Tenant's Animal
bodyText: We found no American Samoa statute, regulation or court rule that gives you a right to enter a rental to feed, check on or remove a tenant's animal, or that sets a procedure for an animal a tenant leaves behind. Entry into premises is lawful only if it is permitted by law, and then only peaceably. The safe course is the tenant's own advance consent: the optional animal-care clause (`animal-care-access-vi`) has the tenant list every animal and name a caretaker you may let in if the tenant is hospitalized, detained or otherwise absent and the animal is left without care. Without consent, contact the tenant and the authorities rather than entering yourself; a loose or dangerous animal is a matter for the Department of Public Safety or the Department of Agriculture.

title: Vehicle Rules at an American Samoa Rental
bodyText: American Samoa has no statute on vehicle rules at private rentals and no law authorizing or regulating private towing, so the library uses its own vehicle clause (`parking-vehicle-rules-as`) instead of the shared one. It keeps the shared rules (operable, licensed passenger vehicles only; no repairs or washing outside designated areas) and replaces towing with written notice to remove the vehicle and a lease breach if the tenant does not. One territorial law makes the ban on inoperable vehicles important: it is unlawful to possess a "junked" vehicle (one that cannot be licensed for the roads), and the people liable include the person on whose land it lies, so you can be fined for a tenant's derelict car; the Attorney General must give 10 days' written notice before prosecuting, and removal within that time ends the matter. Act on any junked vehicle at once: give the tenant written notice to remove it, and if it stays, treat it as a breach through the court rather than removing it yourself.

title: Towing and Junked Vehicles in American Samoa
bodyText: We found no American Samoa statute, regulation or court rule that authorizes or regulates towing from private rental property: there are no sign, written-authorization, rate-cap or kickback rules, nothing on towing for expired registration, and no procedure for a landowner to dispose of an abandoned vehicle. What the law does provide is the junked-vehicle chapter: possessing a vehicle that cannot be licensed for the roads is unlawful, the person on whose land it lies counts as a possessor, the fine is $10 to $500, and after a court filing and conviction each day counts as a separate violation; but no one may be prosecuted unless they were given 10 days' written notice and failed to remove the vehicle in that time. Because no statute lets you tow, and possession is recovered only through the court, do not tow, boot or remove a tenant's, occupant's or guest's vehicle yourself: give written notice to remove it (`parking-vehicle-rules-as`), enforce the lease through the court, and for a stranger's vehicle blocking access or a dangerous vehicle call the Department of Public Safety. Whether a landowner may tow a trespasser's car without a statute rests on common law (case law not searched).

title: Parking Terms in an American Samoa Lease
bodyText: We found no American Samoa statute, regulation or court rule that regulates parking terms in a residential lease, so where and how a tenant may park is a matter for the lease and your written rules. American Samoa uses the library's parking clause without a liability disclaimer (`parking-ks-oh-ca`): it says you do not provide security for the parking area but does not say you are not liable for your own negligence, in line with the library's cautious course for the territory. The zoning regulations require one off-street parking space per dwelling unit when a building is built, enlarged or converted, and require existing required spaces to be kept as long as the building stands, so do not take required spaces out of residential use. Keep fire lanes and hydrant areas clear (no parking within 15 feet of a hydrant), and treat a request for a closer or wider space by a tenant with a disability as a reasonable-accommodation request under the federal Fair Housing Act.

title: Assigned Parking
bodyText: We found no American Samoa statute, regulation or court rule on assigning a tenant a particular parking space, reassigning it, or changing parking rules during the term, so the shared clause (`assigned-parking-space`) works as written. Name the space clearly (describe its location if stalls are not marked), and reassign only to a space of comparable convenience on reasonable notice. Reassigning a space a tenant needs because of a disability may require a reasonable accommodation under the federal Fair Housing Act.

title: Parking Rules Notice
bodyText: We found no American Samoa statute, regulation or court rule that requires parking or towing rules to be delivered before the lease is signed, prescribes a heading for them, limits mid-term changes or the vehicle information you may ask for, or ties a parking permit to the lease term. Give tenants your parking rules in writing with the lease so they bind as lease terms; a change during the term binds only if the lease reserves the right to make reasonable rule changes on notice or the tenant agrees. Ask only for the vehicle information you need (make, model, colour, plate and registration).

title: Unbundled Parking
bodyText: We found no American Samoa statute, regulation or court rule that requires parking to be offered or priced separately from the rent, or forbids it. If you charge separately for parking, state the charge in the lease. The zoning regulations require one off-street parking space per dwelling unit when a residential building is built, enlarged or converted, and require required spaces to be kept while the building stands; that is a building rule, not a pricing rule, but it means you should not lease a building's required spaces away from its units.

title: Storage Space
bodyText: American Samoa has no self-service storage act, so no statutory lien-and-sale procedure applies to a storage locker or room that comes with a residential tenancy, and we found no American Samoa statute, regulation or court rule on storage space let with a dwelling. American Samoa uses the shared Storage clause without a liability disclaimer (`storage-space-ks-oh-ca`). Do not lock a tenant out of a storage space or remove or sell what is in it for unpaid rent: possession of any premises, which by statute include places used for storage, is recovered only through the court. Limit what may be stored (no hazardous, flammable or perishable materials) as the clause does.

title: EV Charging Right
bodyText: We found no American Samoa statute, regulation or court rule that gives a tenant a right to install or use an electric-vehicle charger, or requires you to provide one or allow one. Whether to allow a charger is your decision; a tenant's installation is an alteration that needs your written consent under the lease. If you agree, use the optional installation clause (`ev-charger-installation-hi`) and the rows on installation terms (`edu-no-ev-charging-requirements-as`).

title: EV Charger Installation Terms
bodyText: We found no American Samoa statute, regulation or court rule that sets conditions (insurance, licensed installers, registration, cost-sharing) for a tenant's electric-vehicle charger, so the optional installation clause (`ev-charger-installation-hi`) works as a contract. Two general rules fit its requirement of a licensed contractor and compliance with codes: electrical work is a specialty contractor licence class under the contractor-licensing rules, so use a licensed contractor, and the Power Authority makes all final connections to its lines, does not tolerate unauthorized connections, and must be told of any material change in the equipment connected to the wiring. In a building with several units each occupying customer has its own Authority meter, so put the charger on the tenant's own meter where you can; reselling power through your service is unlawful unless the Authority approves (`edu-electric-submetering-as`).

title: EV Charger at Move-Out
bodyText: We found no American Samoa statute, regulation or court rule that says who owns, removes or pays for a tenant-installed electric-vehicle charger when the tenancy ends. Settle it in the installation agreement before the charger goes in (`ev-charger-installation-hi`): whether the tenant must remove it and restore the wall and wiring, or may leave it, and at what price if you buy it. Otherwise the common law of fixtures decides (case law not searched). The shared end-of-tenancy clause rests on another state's statute and is not used here.

title: EV Charging in Shared Areas
bodyText: We found no American Samoa statute, regulation or court rule that gives tenants a right to install electric-vehicle chargers in shared parking areas, or sets rules for shared charging or for reserving and charging a fee for a charging space. Any shared-area charging is your decision; if you allow it, agree in writing on the space, any fee, electricity billing, insurance and removal, and use a licensed contractor. The shared shared-area clause rests on another state's statute and is not used here.

title: Cannabis in American Samoa Rentals
bodyText: Marijuana is illegal in American Samoa: it is a listed controlled substance, possessing any amount is a felony with mandatory fines or prison (no parole), and growing, producing or distributing it carries 5 to 20 years in prison or a fine of up to $20,000, or both. There is no medical-cannabis or adult-use law, so no tenant is protected as a patient or adult user and no lease term needs to accommodate cannabis. You may forbid all cannabis possession, use, smoking and cultivation at the property; the optional clause (`cannabis-restrictions-ak`) does this, and choosing all three options matches territorial law. Possession is recovered only through the court even when drugs are involved, so do not lock out or remove a tenant yourself; report suspected drug activity to the Department of Public Safety and rely on the lease's default sections.

title: Use of the Property and Common Areas
bodyText: We found no American Samoa statute, regulation or court rule giving a tenant a right that the library's use-of-property clause (`common-area-use`) would block: no protected right to a waterbed, clothesline, drying rack or solar device, and no statute protecting a tenant's display of flags, religious or cultural items or signs against a lease rule. The shared clause works as written, including its saving language for displays the law protects. Two notes: if any part of the building is a public place under the smoking law, the person in charge of the leased space must post smoking signs; and on communal land, village rules may limit uses of the property, which you should reflect in your rules.

title: Guests Displaced by a Disaster
bodyText: We found no American Samoa statute, regulation or court rule that lets a tenant house people displaced by a cyclone, tsunami or other disaster despite the lease's guest or occupancy limits, bars you from enforcing those limits, or says when a displaced person's stay becomes a tenancy; your guest and occupancy terms apply. During a declared disaster emergency the Governor's executive orders have the force of law and may control the occupancy of premises, provide temporary emergency housing, and even commandeer private property (with compensation), so check any order before enforcing occupancy limits or ending a tenancy. For 30 days after a declaration, and for any further 30-day periods the Governor adds, you may not raise a month-to-month rent more than 10% (`edu-rent-control-as`). Consider allowing displaced family members to stay for a stated period by written agreement; a written guest agreement helps show they are guests, not tenants.

title: Grills and Open Flames at an American Samoa Rental
bodyText: We found no American Samoa statute, regulation or court rule that sets a grill-distance or balcony-cooking rule for a private dwelling, or limits what a lease may say about grills, open flames or flammable materials, so the library's clause (`fire-safety-grilling`) works as written. The territory's air rules ban open burning generally but allow open fires for cooking food on non-commercial premises and for recreational or ceremonial purposes, so outdoor cooking is lawful in itself; the lease may still keep it 15 feet from buildings and off porches and balconies. During a declared disaster the Governor may suspend or limit the sale and transport of combustibles.

title: Firearms at an American Samoa Rental
bodyText: No American Samoa statute protects a tenant's right to keep a firearm in a rental, makes a lease rule on firearms unenforceable, or bars a rule about firearms kept in vehicles in your parking area, so a lease may set reasonable firearm rules or ban firearms at the property. American Samoa's weapons law is strict and binds your tenants directly: no one may possess any firearm or ammunition without a license from the Commissioner of Public Safety, licenses are issued only for certain shotguns and .22 caliber rifles, and carrying a concealed firearm is a crime unless the firearm is carried in a nonfunctioning state or is not readily accessible. It is unlawful to discharge any firearm, air gun or firework within 30 yards of a house, building or public road, which covers almost any residential lot. Use the American Samoa firearm clause (`firearm-rules-as`) rather than the shared Louisiana-based clause, whose promise not to restrict firearms locked in vehicles rests on a Louisiana statute American Samoa does not have. Apply any firearm rule the same way to every household. If a protection order bars a tenant or household member from possessing a firearm, the police enforce it; you need not police it, but report any firearm you know is unlicensed or misused.

title: Guests in an American Samoa Rental
bodyText: We found no American Samoa statute, regulation or court rule that sets or limits a private landlord's guest rules, so the lease may include reasonable ones; American Samoa uses the library's `guest-policy` clause as written. A few rules shape how you use it. Apply guest rules the same way to every household, because the federal Fair Housing Act applies in American Samoa, and allow reasonable exceptions a disabled tenant needs, such as a caregiver. If a tenant houses a cannery or call-center guest worker, the tenant becomes that worker's "host" under the guest-worker law (no one may host more than 5 at a time), and if you rent directly to a guest worker you need a business license and a written rent agreement filed with the host affidavit. Knowingly housing a person whose presence in American Samoa is unlawful is a crime, but don't screen guests by national origin or appearance. If your property is in a federally assisted program (for example Section 8 or a tax-credit property), VAWA bars evicting a tenant because a guest committed domestic violence against that tenant. Remove a guest who refuses to leave only through the courts: the summary possession law covers verbal licenses and trespassers, and no one may enter premises by force (case law not searched on when a long-staying guest becomes a tenant).

title: No Guest-Stay Limit in American Samoa Law
bodyText: We found no American Samoa statute, regulation or court rule that sets a maximum or minimum number of days a guest may stay, or a point at which a guest becomes a tenant or occupant, so the number of days in a guest clause is your choice; American Samoa uses the library's `guest-policy-day-limit` clause (14 consecutive days, or 14 days in any rolling 6-month period) as written. Put the limit in the lease and enforce it evenly. Extended-family visits are common in American Samoa; a day limit applied only to some households, or only to relatives of a particular national origin, risks a federal Fair Housing Act claim. A guest who stays past the limit is not removed by changing the locks: if they won't leave, you recover possession through the summary possession law, which covers verbal licenses as well as leases. See `edu-guest-policy-as` for guest-worker host rules.

title: No Guest Access Statute in American Samoa
bodyText: We found no American Samoa statute, regulation or court rule that gives a tenant's guests or service providers (caregivers, home-health aides, delivery or repair workers) a right of access to a residential building, bars a fee for guests, or makes guest access unwaivable. Guests come in under the tenant's right to occupy and the lease's guest terms (`guest-policy`). The federal Fair Housing Act, which applies in American Samoa, may require a reasonable accommodation such as access for a disabled tenant's caregiver or aide. In a federally assisted program, VAWA protects a tenant who is the victim of a guest's domestic violence (see `edu-guest-policy-as`).

title: No Key or Lock Rules in American Samoa Law
bodyText: We found no American Samoa statute, regulation or court rule on keys or locks in a rental: none requires you to supply particular locks, re-key between tenants, or give a key receipt, and none limits a charge for unreturned keys or bars a rule against copying keys. American Samoa uses the library's `keys` clause as written; keep any re-keying charge to your actual cost, since the Consumer Protection Act may reach a residential lease. Never use keys to recover possession: changing the locks on a tenant is a lock-out, and possession is recovered only through the courts. Two utility rules matter: the American Samoa Power Authority will not place an electric meter on a locked porch or anywhere it cannot readily reach, and the meter must stay accessible to it; and the water customer is liable for damage to the Authority's meter or other property caused by the customer "or his tenants", including broken locks on or near a meter. So don't lock tenants or the meter reader out of the meter area.

title: Police Calls, Crime-Free Leases and Cooperation in American Samoa
bodyText: We found no American Samoa statute, regulation or court rule that requires or regulates a crime-free lease addendum, requires you or your tenants to cooperate with police investigations, requires you to give police information about tenants, or bars a lease penalty for a tenant who calls the police or emergency help. A lease may require tenants and their guests to obey the law and may treat criminal activity at the property as a breach, but you still recover possession only through the courts. Two limits apply. A court will not enter a possession judgment if the termination "was intended primarily as retribution for a lawful act arising out of the tenancy", and a tenant's call for police or emergency help is likely such an act (case law not searched), so never end a tenancy or raise charges because a tenant called for help. A domestic-violence protection order may remove a household member from the home "regardless of ownership of the residence", and police may accompany a victim to recover the home; follow any such order. If your property is in a federally assisted program, VAWA bars evicting a victim because of violence committed against them. A few reporting duties bind anyone, landlords included: anyone with reasonable cause to suspect that a child died as a result of abuse or neglect must report it immediately to the Department, and anyone with reasonable cause to suspect that a child died as a result of human trafficking must report it immediately to the Department of Public Safety (A.S.C.A. §§ 45.2003, 46.5009). When a dead body is found, the village mayor (pulenuu) reports it to the Attorney General, and the body may not be moved until the Attorney General or the investigating officer arrives unless that is needed to prevent its loss or mutilation, so if a tenant is found dead, call the police and leave the body where it is (A.S.C.A. § 13.0520). If you run a boardinghouse or lodginghouse, you must immediately report to the Director of Health anyone in it you believe is sick with, or has died from, a contagious or other disease dangerous to public health (A.S.C.A. § 25.0403). Other child-abuse reporting duties fall on listed professionals, though anyone is urged to report (A.S.C.A. § 45.2002).

title: No Political Canvassing Access Rule in American Samoa
bodyText: We found no American Samoa statute, regulation or court rule that gives political candidates, campaign workers, petition circulators or voter-registration volunteers a right to enter a residential building or knock on tenants' doors, or that requires a voter-information area. Your lease and building rules decide who may come onto common areas, applied evenly. One election rule touches rentals near a polling place: on election day no one may carry on campaign activities, including posting signs or billboards, within the area around a polling place set aside for a neutral and quiet atmosphere, so a rental close to a polling place should keep campaign signage down that day. Village councils may have their own customs on campaigning in the village (not published; flagged only).

title: No Portable Cooling-Device Rule in American Samoa
bodyText: We found no American Samoa statute, regulation or court rule that gives a tenant a right to install a portable or window air conditioner or other cooling device, requires a lease that restricts them to say so, or requires you to provide air conditioning. Whether a tenant may add a unit is a lease matter: the library's alterations terms require your consent for changes to the unit, and you may set conditions such as safe mounting, no wiring changes and removal at move-out. If you install or replace a fixed cooling system as part of construction or renovation that needs plan approval, the territory's building energy-efficiency rules (ASHRAE standard 90-75) apply to the plans. Electricity in American Samoa is costly; if the tenant pays the power bill, say so in the lease so the tenant knows who pays to run a unit.

title: No Tenant Solar Device Right in American Samoa
bodyText: We found no American Samoa statute, regulation or court rule that gives a tenant a right to install a plug-in, balcony or portable solar device, limits a landlord's power to forbid or condition one, or voids lease or deed restrictions on solar energy systems. Whether a tenant may use one is up to the lease and your consent; you may refuse, or allow it on conditions such as safe mounting, no changes to the wiring, no connection that sends power into the building's service, and removal at move-out. The American Samoa Power Authority's rules do govern customer-owned generation: generators that could feed power back into its system need protective devices, parallel operation is allowed only if it does not harm the system, and the customer is liable for damage its generator causes. So any device that connects to the electric service must be cleared with the Power Authority first.

title: No Recycling Notice Rule in American Samoa
bodyText: We found no American Samoa statute, regulation or court rule that requires a landlord to tell tenants where or how to recycle, to provide recycling containers, or to post recycling instructions. What American Samoa does have is a set of garbage rules. Waste set out for collection must be in containers or bags meeting the solid waste official's specifications. The owner of a dwelling must prepare and place the household's solid waste for collection by a licensed collector, unless the owner and occupant agree that the occupant will do it and both sign a written notice to the collector (see `garbage-setout-as`). Every owner, lessee or occupant of an occupied building must keep garbage and rubbish from accumulating where it can harbor rodents. Commercial establishments must keep their own collection receptacles. A short note in the lease or house rules on where bins go and the collection day is good practice but not required.

title: Religious and Cultural Displays in American Samoa
bodyText: We found no American Samoa statute, regulation or court rule that gives a tenant a right to place religious or cultural items (a cross, a mezuzah, a devotional picture, holiday decorations) on a door, doorframe, porch or common area, or that limits a landlord's rules about them. Your lease rules decide, within one federal limit: the Fair Housing Act applies in American Samoa and bars discriminating in the terms or conditions of a rental because of religion, so a display rule must be neutral and applied the same way to every household, not aimed at one faith or culture. The shared `common-area-use` clause already lets a tenant make any display the law entitles them to make. Village councils may have customs about church observances and evening prayer curfews (not published; flagged only).

title: House Rules in American Samoa
bodyText: We found no American Samoa statute, regulation or court rule that sets conditions for a private landlord's house rules to be enforceable, limits rule changes during a tenancy, or binds a tenant only to rules in force at signing. Rules bind the tenant because the lease says so, so American Samoa uses the shared clause `rules-ia`, which requires rules to be reasonable, written, applied fairly and not a substantial change to the lease without the tenant's written agreement; attach the rules in force at signing. Whether a rule you add mid-term binds a tenant who never agreed rests on the common law of contracts (case law not searched), which is why the clause limits later rules. Two statutes matter when you enforce rules. A breach of a rule ends the tenancy only through the lease's termination power, a written demand that states "the time to take remedial action", and a court case. And a court will not enter judgment for possession if you "attempted to increase the defendant's obligations under the lease or contract as a penalty for a lawful act" and the tenant's failure to meet those new obligations was the main reason for the termination, so never add a rule to punish a tenant for complaining.

title: Smoke Drifting Between Units in American Samoa
bodyText: We found no American Samoa statute, regulation or court rule that addresses tobacco smoke drifting between units, requires a smoking-policy disclosure, or lets a lease make a tenant accept drifting smoke or give up claims over it. Don't use a drift waiver: the library doesn't draft terms that excuse a landlord's own responsibility because the common law on them was not searched. The Smoke Free Environment Act bans smoking in enclosed areas of public places (its list includes elevators, lobbies and waiting areas) and places of employment, but it excludes a private residence. Whether an apartment building's enclosed lobby, elevator or staffed hallway is a public place or place of employment under the Act is unsettled (case law not searched); the cautious course is to make enclosed common areas smoke-free and post signs at each entrance, as the Act requires owners or managers of covered premises to do. To control smoking inside units, use a clear no-smoking lease term applied to every household.

title: Snow Removal: Not Applicable in American Samoa
bodyText: Snow removal does not arise in American Samoa: the territory is tropical, and no American Samoa statute, regulation or court rule mentions snow. The shared Snow Removal clause is not used for American Samoa leases. What matters instead is cyclone and heavy-rain readiness: no statute assigns storm preparation between landlord and tenant, so say in the lease who secures shutters and loose items, who clears storm debris from yards and drains, and who keeps the grounds free of rubbish and standing water that breed rodents and mosquitoes.

title: Flags and Signs at American Samoa Rentals
bodyText: We found no American Samoa statute, regulation or court rule that gives a tenant a right to display a flag, a political sign or a religious item against your wishes, or that bars a landlord or association from restricting them, so the lease decides (`common-area-use`). Two rules matter. American Samoa's outdoor sign law makes it unlawful to put up an outdoor sign announcing or advertising a business, product, service or event unless the law allows it or a special permit is issued; light cloth or cardboard signs and banners are allowed for up to 72 hours. Whoever permits a sign on property they own or control is also responsible for it, so you share the risk of a tenant's unlawful outdoor sign. Whether a political or campaign sign is an "event" sign under that law is unsettled (case law not searched); a lease rule requiring your consent for outdoor signs and limiting temporary banners to 72 hours keeps you on the safe side. On election day, no campaign signs may go up in the area around a polling place. Apply display rules evenly; the federal Fair Housing Act bars rules that single out a religion or national origin.

title: Security Cameras and Video Doorbells at American Samoa Rentals
bodyText: We found no American Samoa statute, regulation or court rule that gives a tenant a right to install a security camera or video doorbell, regulates landlord or tenant cameras at rentals, or makes audio recording of a conversation a crime without everyone's consent; we found no territorial eavesdropping or voyeurism statute either. Installing a device is a lease matter: a device fixed to the doors or walls is an alteration that needs your consent, and you may allow battery or peel-and-stick doorbells on conditions (aim only at the tenant's own entry, never into another unit or a shared bathroom or laundry, remove at move-out and repair holes). Entering another person's unit or yard to watch or record them can be criminal trespass, and a case note under the trespass statute treats viewing an occupant for sexual purposes from under the eaves as entering the house (case law not searched). Federal criminal laws on intercepting communications may also apply (not searched here).

title: Barring Non-Tenants From the Property in American Samoa
bodyText: American Samoa's criminal trespass law lets you, as the person in control of common areas and grounds, bar a non-tenant from the property. A person commits trespass by knowingly entering or remaining unlawfully in a building or on real property, but for land (as opposed to a building) only if it is fenced or enclosed to keep intruders out, or notice against trespass has been given by telling the person directly or by posting it where intruders are likely to see it. A "keep off private property" sign needs no sign permit. If part of a building is open to the public (an office or lobby), a person there is licensed unless they defy a lawful order not to enter or remain given to them personally by the owner or another authorized person, so tell the person directly and keep a dated note of the warning. You may not bar a tenant's guests from the tenant's own unit, and a person who claims a right to live there (a former occupant, a guest who has moved in) is removed through the courts, which have a summary procedure for possession taken by trespass. Don't use force yourself; call the police.

title: Waterbeds in American Samoa Rentals
bodyText: We found no American Samoa statute, regulation or court rule on waterbeds or other water-filled furniture, so American Samoa neither protects a tenant's right to one nor sets conditions on it. The lease may forbid or allow them; the shared `common-area-use` clause requires your written consent. If you allow one, you may require the tenant to carry insurance covering water damage and to follow installation rules (frame, liner, floor-load limits), and the tenant is liable under the lease for damage it causes. Because no statute caps security deposits in American Samoa, any extra deposit for a waterbed is a lease term, but keep it reasonable and refund it under the lease's deposit terms.

title: No Association Disclosure Duty in American Samoa
bodyText: American Samoa has no condominium act and no statute governing homeowners or property owners' associations. We found no American Samoa statute, regulation or court rule that requires you to disclose an association's obligations or documents to a tenant, or to put your own statement about association rules in the lease. If your property is in a development with recorded covenants or an owners' group, its rules bind your tenant only through the lease, so attach or describe them and use the shared `hoa-compliance` clause. Many homes stand on communal (native) land or in villages, where the matai and the village council, not an association, set local rules (not published; flagged only).

title: Associations and Your Rental in American Samoa
bodyText: American Samoa has no condominium act and no statute governing homeowners associations. We found no American Samoa statute, regulation or court rule on association approval of leases, approval or application fees, association-held tenant deposits, association rent collection from tenants when an owner is delinquent, rental bans, or limits on the tenant information an association may demand. Any such terms come only from a development's recorded covenants or a private agreement and bind your tenant only through the lease. If the governing documents require the association to approve a lease, use the shared `association-approval-la` clause; otherwise leave it out. Rights over communal (native) land and village rules belong to the matai and village council rather than an association (flagged only); a lease of communal land needs the Governor's approval (`edu-communal-land-lease-approval-as`).

title: Tenants and Association Rules in American Samoa
bodyText: No American Samoa statute makes an association's rules binding on a tenant, requires you to deliver them at lease signing, caps association fines, or lets an association collect rent from a tenant; American Samoa has no condominium act. A lease term requiring the tenant to follow the association's rules is how they become the tenant's obligation, so American Samoa uses the shared `hoa-compliance` clause as written. Attach the rules to the lease so the tenant knows what they are, and pass through only fines actually charged for the tenant's own violations. We found no territorial rule on satellite dishes or antennas; a federal communications rule on over-the-air antennas may protect a tenant's dish in an area the tenant exclusively uses (not searched here).

title: No Bed Bug Disclosure Rule in American Samoa
bodyText: We found no American Samoa statute, regulation or court rule that requires you to tell an applicant or tenant about a unit's bed bug history, to give a bed bug information sheet, or to treat on a set timetable; the words "bed bug" appear nowhere in the territory's laws. The only pest statute is a rodent rule: every owner, lessee or occupant of an occupied building must take good-faith measures to get rid of rodents and keep the building and surroundings free of food and rubbish that harbor them. Treat any known bed bug infestation before a new tenant moves in and don't deny one if asked, since the Consumer Protection Act may reach a misleading statement in a residential lease. Say in the lease who arranges and pays for pest treatment.

title: No Pesticide Notice Rule in American Samoa
bodyText: We found no American Samoa statute, regulation or court rule that requires you to notify tenants before pesticides are applied in or around a rental, or to post a notice of pest-control treatment. The pesticide law lets the Director who administers it require notice to adjacent landowners by rule, but we found no such rule adopted. What the regulations do require is certification: a commercial applicator who uses or supervises restricted-use pesticides in or around human dwellings must be certified in the structural pest control category, so hire a certified operator for any restricted-use treatment. Give tenants reasonable advance written notice of any treatment inside the unit anyway, with any re-entry or ventilation instructions from the label, and enter only as the lease allows and never by force.

title: Certificates of Occupancy for American Samoa Rentals
bodyText: We found no American Samoa statute, regulation or court rule that requires you to give a tenant a copy of a certificate of occupancy, or to state in the lease that one exists. The building law matters anyway: every new building needs a building application, and on completion it must be inspected by the Department of Public Works to determine whether the plans were followed and whether it is safe for occupancy. American Samoa adopted the 1964 Uniform Building Code (Short Form) by reference; its text is not in the sources searched for this library, so check with the Department of Public Works whether your building's completion inspection was passed before you rent it. Keep the inspection record with your property file.

title: No Defective Drywall Disclosure Rule in American Samoa
bodyText: We found no American Samoa statute, regulation or court rule that requires a landlord to disclose defective or corrosive drywall, or sets any standard for it in rental housing; the only mention of gypsum is a contractor-licensing definition of plastering. If you know of a building defect that affects health or safety, fix it or tell the tenant before signing: no statute requires it, but the Consumer Protection Act may reach a misleading statement or a hidden known defect in a residential lease.

title: Outstanding Code Orders and Condemnation in American Samoa
bodyText: We found no American Samoa statute, regulation or court rule that requires you to tell an applicant or tenant about an outstanding inspection report, violation notice, nuisance order or unsafe-building order before signing a lease. American Samoa has no rental inspection or housing-code enforcement program, but government orders can still reach a rental: the Director of Health may inspect buildings and order a public health nuisance abated, keeping one after 10 days' written notice is a misdemeanor, and the Governor may order a dangerously dilapidated building torn down within 30 days (see `edu-substandard-property-orders-as`). The Zoning Board must notify both the owner and the occupant of a nonconforming use. Don't rent a unit under an order that affects its occupancy without telling the tenant: the Consumer Protection Act may reach a misleading omission, and a condition that stops the tenant using the home may excuse rent.

title: Electric Submetering in American Samoa
bodyText: We found no American Samoa statute, regulation or court rule that sets disclosures or billing rules for a landlord who submeters electricity. That is not permission: the American Samoa Power Authority's rules make it unlawful for a customer to resell any electric energy received from the Authority, or to supply any other person or premises through its service, except as the Authority approves, and in a building occupied by several customers each one becomes a customer of the Authority with its own meter. Whether billing tenants by submeter is "resale" is unsettled (case law not searched), so the cautious course is an Authority meter for each unit in the tenant's name, the Authority's written approval of any other arrangement, or electricity included in the rent. See `edu-utility-submetering-as` for the full utility-billing picture.

title: No Flood Disclosure Rule in American Samoa
bodyText: We found no American Samoa statute, regulation or court rule that requires you to tell a tenant that a rental is in a flood zone, has flooded before, or is exposed to tsunami or storm-surge hazards. American Samoa's flood rules govern development instead. The 1981 flood hazard executive order, now in the administrative code, designates the federal Flood Hazard Boundary Map as the official map of special flood hazard areas (Zone A, land with a 1% or greater chance of flooding in any year), requires new homes in Zone A to have the first floor raised, and has the Office of Development Planning keep floor-elevation records open to the public. Coastal rules normally deny new projects within 200 feet of the mean high-tide mark and in flood, landslide and erosion-prone areas. Telling a tenant that a home floods or sits in Zone A is good practice and avoids a misleading-omission claim under the Consumer Protection Act; also tell the tenant to insure their own belongings, and say in the lease who prepares the home for cyclones and tsunami warnings.

title: Shorelines and Public Access: No Lease Disclosure in American Samoa
bodyText: We found no American Samoa statute, regulation or court rule that requires a lease to disclose that a property is on or near the shoreline, that the public may use the beach, or that a public right of way crosses the land. Two rules matter for coastal rentals. Around Pago Pago Harbor, from Blunt's Point to Breaker's Point, a strip 15 feet wide inland from the high-water mark was taken for a public highway, and the Code asserts the government's and the public's rights in it, so tenants of harbor-front property may not fence or build on that strip. Coastal rules normally deny new projects within 200 feet of the mean high-tide mark and call for public access to and along the ocean to be kept and improved. Beach and reef areas in villages are often governed by village custom and the matai (not published; flagged only). If a path or public strip crosses your land, describe it in the lease and tell the tenant not to block it.

title: No Foreclosure Disclosure Rule in American Samoa
bodyText: We found no American Samoa statute, regulation or court rule that requires you to tell an applicant or tenant that the property is in foreclosure or that you have received a notice of default, or that protects a tenant when a lender forecloses. What the mortgage law does say: unless the mortgage says otherwise, the owner keeps the use and possession of mortgaged property until default; a lender foreclosing under a power of sale must publish notice three weeks running and post a copy of the notice on the premises at least 21 days before the sale, so your tenant may see it; and a mortgage does not attach to a recorded lease unless an instrument referring to that lease is recorded with the Territorial Registrar. If the property has a federally backed mortgage, the federal CARES Act notice rule may apply (see `edu-cares-act-notice-as`). Tell a tenant before signing if a foreclosure sale is scheduled: hiding it risks a misleading-omission claim under the Consumer Protection Act, and a buyer at the sale may not be bound by an unregistered lease (case law not searched).

title: No Good Cause Notice in American Samoa
bodyText: American Samoa has no good-cause eviction law and no rent regulation, so there is no notice to give a tenant about whether the unit is covered or exempt. We found no American Samoa statute, regulation or court rule requiring a pre-lease or renewal notice of that kind. Possession is still recovered only through the courts on the statutory grounds, and a court will not enter judgment if the termination was retaliation for a lawful act arising out of the tenancy; see `edu-for-cause-eviction-as`. From the declaration of a state of emergency until 30 days after it (longer if the Governor extends the period in further 30-day periods), the price-gouging law bars renting month-to-month housing for more than 10% above the rent charged just before the declaration, unless you can prove the increase is directly attributable to added costs, and even then only within the statute's cost-plus-markup limit.

title: No Contamination Disclosure Rule in American Samoa
bodyText: We found no American Samoa statute, regulation or court rule that requires a lease to disclose that the property is contaminated, is a cleanup site, or is subject to a recorded environmental use limitation, and no rule requiring such limitations to be written into leases. The territory's environmental rules put duties on owners and operators instead (for example, underground storage tank owners must notify the environmental agency and keep records of releases and cleanup), and the Department of Health may order a property that endangers health decontaminated, closed or evacuated. If you know of contamination that could affect a tenant's health, such as a leaking fuel tank, fix it or tell the tenant before signing: the Consumer Protection Act may reach a misleading omission, and a public health nuisance on property you own or occupy is unlawful.

title: Lead-Based Paint Disclosure in American Samoa
bodyText: The federal lead-based paint disclosure rule applies in American Samoa: neither the federal statute nor the EPA and HUD regulations exempt the territories. Before a tenant is bound by a lease of housing built before 1978, you must give the EPA pamphlet Protect Your Family From Lead in Your Home, disclose any lead-based paint or lead hazards you know of, hand over any lead reports or records you have (including for common areas), and attach the Lead Warning Statement and signed acknowledgments to the lease (`lead-based-paint`). Keep a copy for at least three years. The rule does not apply to leases of 100 days or less with no renewal, to housing for the elderly or disabled where no child under six lives (unless a child is expected), to zero-bedroom units, or to housing a certified inspector has found lead-based paint free. A knowing violation exposes you to federal penalties and to triple the tenant's damages. We found no American Samoa statute or regulation that adds a territorial lead-paint notice or duty.

title: No Lead-Safe Certificate Rule in American Samoa
bodyText: We found no American Samoa statute, regulation or court rule that requires a lead-safe or lead-free certificate, an inspection report or a clearance test to be attached to a lease, or that requires a lead inspection before renting. The only lead rules for rentals are federal: the pre-1978 disclosure (see `edu-lead-based-paint-as`). Under that federal rule, a lease of housing that a certified inspector has found free of lead-based paint is exempt from the disclosure, so if you have such a finding, keep the inspector's report with the lease file.

title: No American Samoa Lead Notices Beyond the Federal Disclosure
bodyText: We found no American Samoa statute, regulation or court rule that requires a territorial lead notice, rights form, inspection certificate or information packet with a lease, beyond the federal pre-1978 disclosure (see `edu-lead-based-paint-as`). The one territorial lead rule concerns drinking water: American Samoa's safe drinking water regulations adopt by reference the federal rule on lead pipes, solder and flux (its text is not in the sources searched for this library), so use only lead-free materials and a licensed plumber when you repair or replace plumbing that carries drinking water. No notice to tenants is required.

title: No Landlord Insurance Mandate in American Samoa
bodyText: We found no American Samoa statute, regulation or court rule that requires a residential landlord to carry liability insurance, to register a policy, or to tell tenants whether you are insured. American Samoa's compulsory insurance laws cover motor vehicles, commercial vehicles and passenger vessels, not rental property. Carrying liability insurance is still wise, and if you do, a person injured at your property may sue your insurer directly in American Samoa, within the policy's terms and limits, even if the policy forbids direct action. Don't put a clause in the lease excusing you from your own negligence; the library leaves such terms out for American Samoa.

title: No Meter Conservation Charge Rule in American Samoa
bodyText: American Samoa has no energy-efficiency or conservation charge attached to a utility meter that a later occupant must pay, and no property-assessed energy financing program, so there is no notice to give a new tenant and no rent deduction rule. We found no American Samoa statute, regulation or court rule on the subject. For who pays electricity and how it is metered, see `edu-electric-submetering-as`.

title: No Drug-Lab Disclosure Rule in American Samoa
bodyText: We found no American Samoa statute, regulation or court rule that requires you to disclose that a rental was used to make methamphetamine or other drugs, to report a suspected drug lab, to have a former lab cleaned to a standard, or bars renting a contaminated unit. General rules still apply: creating or allowing a public health nuisance (anything that endangers life or health or contaminates the environment) is unlawful, and the Department of Health may order the property decontaminated, closed or evacuated at the owner's expense. If you know a unit was used as a drug lab, have it professionally cleaned before renting and tell the tenant; hiding it risks a misleading-omission claim under the Consumer Protection Act.

title: No Military Zone Disclosure Rule in American Samoa
bodyText: We found no American Samoa statute, regulation or court rule that requires a lease to disclose that a rental is near a military installation, in an aircraft noise or accident-potential zone, or in a military impact area, and none giving a tenant a right to end the lease on that ground. If a rental is close to Pago Pago International Airport or a military facility and noise is significant, telling the tenant before signing is good practice.

title: No Mold Disclosure Rule in American Samoa
bodyText: We found no American Samoa statute, regulation or court rule that requires you to disclose mold to a tenant, give a mold information sheet, or meet a mold standard; the words "mold" and "mildew" do not appear in the territory's housing or health laws. In American Samoa's humid climate mold is common, so inspect and clean before each tenancy, say in the lease how the tenant should ventilate and report moisture, and respond to reports promptly. Mold bad enough to endanger health could be a public health nuisance the Department of Health may order corrected, and hiding a known serious mold problem risks a misleading-omission claim under the Consumer Protection Act.

title: No Ordnance, Demolition or Shared-Meter Disclosure in American Samoa
bodyText: American Samoa law has none of these three pre-signing disclosures. We found no American Samoa statute, regulation or court rule requiring you to tell a tenant about a former military ordnance site nearby, about a planned demolition of the building, or that the tenant's utility meter also serves other areas. Related rules: the Governor may order a dangerously dilapidated building torn down within 30 days, so tell any tenant at once if you receive such an order. The Power Authority installs an electric meter for each customer in a building occupied by several customers, so a shared electric meter should not arise (see `edu-electric-submetering-as`), but a multi-dwelling building is on one water meter unless you ask for a meter per unit, so say in the lease how water is paid for.

title: No Owner Identity Disclosure Rule in American Samoa
bodyText: We found no American Samoa statute, regulation or court rule that requires you to give a tenant the name and address of the owner or of a manager or agent authorized to receive notices, and none that bars a possession case for failing to do so. Two rules make identity matter anyway. Any demand for possession or payment must be dated and signed by the person entitled to possession or by that person's attorney or agent, and a court case for possession needs a copy of that demand and of any written lease. A lease of communal land is made with the native proprietors, must state its terms in full, and has no validity until the Governor approves it in writing. Put your name, the owner's name if different, and an address for notices in every lease.

title: No Private Well Testing Rule in American Samoa
bodyText: We found no American Samoa statute, regulation or court rule that requires a landlord to test a private well or give test results to tenants. The territory's safe drinking water regulations apply to public water systems, which they define by adopting the federal definitions; a well that serves enough connections or people to be a public water system brings monitoring and public-notice duties, so check with the territorial environmental agency before supplying several rentals from one well. The Power Authority's rules prohibit drilling a private well and let only the Authority authorize the use of an existing one, so get its authorization before tenants rely on a well. If tenants drink well or catchment water, test it and share the results.

title: No Chemical-Exposure Warning Rule in American Samoa
bodyText: California's Proposition 65 warnings do not apply in American Samoa, and we found no American Samoa statute, regulation or court rule that requires a landlord to warn tenants about chemicals known to cause cancer or reproductive harm, or to post such warnings at rental property. Federal rules still apply where they reach the territory, such as the lead-based paint disclosure for pre-1978 housing (`edu-lead-based-paint-as`).

title: Property Tax Portion of Rent: Not Applicable in American Samoa
bodyText: American Samoa does not tax real property, so there is no property-tax portion of rent to state and no annual statement to give. We found no American Samoa statute, regulation or court rule imposing a real property tax or requiring a rent disclosure tied to one. A different tax can reach some rentals: a 5% tax on renting hotel rooms, which by definition can include rooming houses and apartment houses, with an exemption for a tenant holding a written lease of at least one month; see `edu-rent-tax-as`.

title: No Radon Disclosure Rule in American Samoa
bodyText: We found no American Samoa statute, regulation or court rule that requires a landlord to test for radon, disclose radon levels or give a radon information sheet, and none requiring radon-resistant construction; the word "radon" does not appear in the territory's laws. No disclosure is required.

title: Required Lease Disclosures in American Samoa
bodyText: American Samoa has no residential landlord-tenant act and no statute listing disclosures a private residential lease must contain; we found no territorial disclosure form, first-page notice or coverage statement. What you must do comes from a few specific rules. Federal lead-based paint: for housing built before 1978, give the pamphlet, disclose known lead hazards and attach the signed Lead Warning Statement (`edu-lead-based-paint-as`). Communal (native) land: a lease has no validity until the Governor approves it in writing (`edu-communal-land-lease-approval-as`). Guest workers: if you rent to a cannery or call-center guest worker for a charge, you need a business license and a written rent agreement stating the term, the monthly rent and the facilities provided, filed with the host affidavit. Government land: a lease longer than 4 years needs an inflation-adjustment clause (this binds the Government as landlord). For lease content generally, see `edu-lease-content-requirements-as`.

title: No Tenant Rights Guide Requirement in American Samoa
bodyText: We found no American Samoa statute, regulation or court rule that requires you to give tenants a government-published rights and responsibilities guide, a tenant handbook or a statutory summary at signing or renewal, and the territory publishes none for private rentals. The library's American Samoa education rows are the nearest thing; the main points to share with a tenant are that possession is recovered only through the courts after a written demand, and how and where rent is paid.

title: No Sanitary Code Variance Notice in American Samoa
bodyText: American Samoa has no housing sanitary code with variances for rentals, so there is no variance to give tenants or attach to a lease. We found no American Samoa statute, regulation or court rule requiring one. Two variance rules exist elsewhere: a public water system operating under a drinking-water variance must notify the regulators and local media, and the Zoning Board may grant a zoning variance after notice to neighboring owners, tenants or matai. If your rental's water comes from a system under a variance, pass on what you learn to tenants.

title: Sex Offender Registry and Rentals in American Samoa
bodyText: We found no American Samoa statute, regulation or court rule that requires you to tell tenants about registered sex offenders nearby, to put a registry notice in the lease, or that bars a registered offender from living near schools or other places. The Attorney General's Office runs a public sex offender registry website that lists each registered offender's residential address and lets anyone ask for e-mail alerts when an offender moves into a zip code or area; tenants can check it themselves. Don't use registry information to harass anyone; the website itself warns against it. Knowingly harboring a registered sex offender who is in violation of the registration law is a misdemeanor, so if you learn a tenant or occupant is avoiding registration, don't help hide them. If you screen applicants using the registry, apply the same rule to everyone.

title: No Single-Family Occupancy Notice in American Samoa
bodyText: We found no American Samoa statute, regulation or court rule that requires a single-family home lease to carry an occupancy notice, presumes an occupant has no right to be there unless the lease has some formality, or sets a font size, bold type or first-page placement for any lease disclosure. American Samoa leases may be in English or Samoan (both are official languages); give the tenant a copy in a language the tenant reads. A person who comes into possession by trespass is removed through the courts' summary possession procedure.

title: No Special District Lease Statement in American Samoa
bodyText: We found no American Samoa statute, regulation or court rule that requires a lease to state that a property is in a special district or that the tenant knows of district charges or plans. American Samoa has no special assessment or improvement districts for housing; the government's industrial park has its own commission rules for its commercial lessees, which do not reach private residential leases.

title: No Fire Sprinkler Disclosure in American Samoa
bodyText: We found no American Samoa statute, regulation or court rule that requires you to tell a tenant or applicant whether the building has fire sprinklers, or to describe a sprinkler system in the lease. The only sprinkler provisions we found are an insurance definition and a backflow rule for public water systems. American Samoa adopted the 1964 Uniform Building Code (Short Form) for buildings, but the code book itself is not in the sources we searched, so we could not check whether it requires sprinklers in any residential building (`edu-no-fire-sprinkler-duty-as`). If your building has sprinklers, you may describe them in the lease and tell the tenant not to tamper with them or hang things from the heads; if it has none, don't say or suggest that it does, since the Consumer Protection Act may reach a residential lease.

title: Deaths, Crimes, HIV and Offenders: What to Disclose in American Samoa
bodyText: We found no American Samoa statute, regulation or court rule that says whether you must, or need not, tell a prospective tenant that a death, suicide, homicide or other crime happened at the property or that it is reputed to be haunted, and no statutory safe harbour for staying silent; American Samoa also has no real estate licensing law with its own disclosure duties. What you say is governed by the common law of misrepresentation (case law not searched) and possibly the Consumer Protection Act, so answer a direct question truthfully and don't hide a known physical problem. Two territorial rules apply. A person who tests HIV positive may not be denied housing because of it, so never refuse a tenant, or disclose or ask about anyone's HIV status, on that ground. And the Attorney General keeps a public sex offender registry website showing registered offenders' residential addresses; you need not check it or disclose it, but you may point an applicant who asks to it.

title: Renting to Students in American Samoa
bodyText: We found no American Samoa statute, regulation or court rule that creates a student-housing regime: no licence, inspection, lease certification or special lease terms for renting to college or other students. Students rent like anyone else, and a minor student's capacity to contract rests on the common law (case law not searched), so have a parent or guardian sign too if a tenant is under 18. One tax rule may matter if you rent rooms: the hotel room tax covers lodging houses, rooming houses and apartment houses, and its definition leaves out only dormitory rooms a religious organization, school, college or university runs for its students, faculty or staff, so a private landlord renting rooms to students is not within that exclusion (`hotel-occupancy-tax-as`); a student with a written lease of a month or more may still qualify for the permanent-resident exemption quarter by quarter (`edu-rent-tax-as`).

title: No Tenant Rights Statement in American Samoa
bodyText: We found no American Samoa statute, regulation or court rule that requires you to give tenants a government statement or summary of tenant rights, attach one to the lease or a renewal, have tenants sign each page, or provide one before you may sue. The one document a possession case does require is your written demand, and the court rules make a copy of it, and of any written lease, part of the complaint (`edu-self-help-eviction-as`). Give tenants a full signed copy of the lease, since it is your evidence of the terms.

title: No Exemption Notice Needed in American Samoa
bodyText: Some places require a lease statement telling tenants that a property is exempt from a rent cap, a just-cause eviction rule or a tenant's right to buy. American Samoa has none of those laws, so there is nothing to be exempt from and no exemption notice to give: we found no American Samoa statute, regulation or court rule capping ordinary rent increases, requiring a cause to end a tenancy (`edu-for-cause-eviction-as`), or giving tenants a right to buy (`edu-no-tpa-notice-as`). The one rent limit is the price-gouging law, which applies to month-to-month housing from the declaration of a state of emergency until 30 days after the declaration (longer if the Governor extends it in further 30-day periods), and it has no exemption notice.

title: No Tenant Right to Buy in American Samoa
bodyText: We found no American Samoa statute, regulation or court rule that gives a tenant of a private landlord a right of first refusal or an opportunity to buy the property when you sell it, or that requires you to notify tenants of a sale or of any purchase right. No notice about one belongs in your lease. Land law limits who may buy instead: land other than freehold land may not be sold or otherwise alienated to a person with less than one-half Samoan blood, and a matai may not alienate communal family land without the Governor's written approval, so many tenants could not lawfully buy the land even if offered (`edu-foreign-ownership-as`). Whether a sale ends an existing lease or binds the buyer rests on the lease, registration and the common law (case law not searched); registering a written lease gives notice of it to anyone who later deals with the land (`edu-lease-registration-as`).

title: No Truth-in-Renting Act in American Samoa
bodyText: American Samoa has no truth-in-renting act: we found no American Samoa statute, regulation or court rule that requires you to give tenants a government statement of their rights with the lease, to print a notice that some clauses may be unenforceable, or that penalizes you simply for offering a lease containing a term the law forbids. American Samoa also has no list of prohibited lease terms (`edu-prohibited-lease-terms-as`). What does reach lease terms: the possession statute's tenant defences, which no statute lets a lease waive; the 15% interest ceiling and the usury forfeiture; and the Consumer Protection Act, which may reach a residential lease and lets a court strike unconscionable clauses. Keep the lease to terms you can enforce.

title: Who May Grant a Lease in American Samoa
bodyText: Usufruct is a civil-law interest that American Samoa's law does not use, and we found no American Samoa statute, regulation or court rule on leases granted by a usufructuary, a life tenant or anyone else holding less than full ownership. What matters instead is the land's status and who controls it. For communal (native) land, a lease needs the Governor's written approval and may run up to 55 years (`edu-communal-land-lease-approval-as`); under Samoan custom, which the Code preserves where it does not conflict with law, control (pule) over family land rests with the senior matai, so a lease signed by a family member who is not the matai, or without the family's support, may be challenged (case law not searched). For individually owned or freehold land, the person granting the lease should hold title, ideally registered; whether a lease outlasts a lessor with a limited interest rests on the common law (case law not searched). Before you sign as tenant or take over as landlord, check the title at the Territorial Registrar.

title: No Utility Disclosure Attachment in American Samoa
bodyText: We found no American Samoa statute, regulation or court rule that requires a utility disclosure attached to the lease: no form explaining how a shared bill is split, no submeter statement and no fee table. The Power Authority's rules matter more. For water, it provides one delivery point per building, a building with several tenants is on one meter unless the owner asks, at its own expense, for a meter per unit, and any tenant meters are grouped at one central point. For electricity, when a building is occupied by several customers each becomes a customer with its own meter; reselling electricity is unlawful, and a customer may not supply another person or premises through its service without the Power Authority's approval. A landlord must also co-sign the tenant's application or account transfer and answers for the tenant's past-due bills. So say in the lease which utilities you pay and which the tenant pays and in whose name each account is (`edu-utility-submetering-as`).

title: Second Units and Zoning in American Samoa
bodyText: We found no American Samoa statute, regulation or court rule on accessory dwelling units: nothing allows a second unit by right, limits a zoning rule against one, or requires the owner to live on the lot. The territorial zoning law decides it. In a single dwelling (R1) zone the permitted homes are one-family dwellings, plus uses customarily accessory to them such as home occupations and private garages; two-family and multiple dwellings are permitted in multiple dwelling (R2) zones, and the agricultural and watershed conservation zones allow any R1 or R2 use. On Tutuila, land not otherwise zoned is in the watershed conservation zone. So before you rent out a second unit, check the zoning map: a separate rental unit on an R1 lot is not a listed use, and whether it could count as an accessory use is unsettled, so ask the Zoning Board or seek a variance. Building it also needs a building application and a completion inspection, and work that may affect coastal resources needs a land use permit.

title: Charging for Alarm Tampering in American Samoa
bodyText: We found no American Samoa statute, regulation or court rule that sets or limits a fee a lease may charge a tenant for removing, disabling or tampering with a smoke or carbon monoxide alarm, and none that requires landlords to install alarms in the first place (`edu-no-alarm-duty-as`). So a lease term on alarm care is a matter of contract. American Samoa uses the library's optional detector clause (`detector-care-la`), which bars the tenant from removing or disabling a detector and makes the tenant pay the reasonable cost of repairing or replacing one the tenant's side damages. Charge only that real cost rather than a fixed penalty, since a penalty may not be enforced at common law (case law not searched) and the Consumer Protection Act may reach a residential lease.

title: Asbestos in American Samoa Rentals
bodyText: We found no American Samoa statute, regulation or court rule that requires you to inspect a rental for asbestos or to tell a tenant about it. The territory's hazardous materials rules do reach asbestos, though: anyone who handles, uses, stores or disposes of a hazardous substance must follow them, materials containing asbestos must be used and maintained under a hazardous materials management plan that records where the friable asbestos is, areas containing asbestos must carry a bilingual English and Samoan caution label, asbestos-abatement work must meet the federal worker-protection standards the rules adopt, and small quantities of asbestos may be buried only in leak-proof, labelled bags apart from other waste. Whether a landlord whose building simply contains asbestos material is covered is unsettled; the cautious course is not to disturb suspect material (older cement sheeting, pipe lagging, floor tiles), to use a qualified contractor for any removal, and to tell the tenant about known asbestos in the home.

title: No Balcony Inspection Rule in American Samoa
bodyText: We found no American Samoa statute, regulation or court rule that requires a landlord to inspect balconies, decks, stairways or other exterior elevated elements, or to report on them. Two building rules still apply: a new building must pass a completion inspection for whether it is safe for occupancy, and the Governor may order the owner to tear down a building so dilapidated as to be unsafe and dangerous. The 1964 Uniform Building Code the territory adopted is not in the sources we searched, so we could not check its railing or balcony standards. The cautious course is to inspect balconies, railings and stairs at each turnover and after storms, repair rot and rust promptly, and keep a record, since liability for a fall rests on the common law (case law not searched).

title: Casualty and Re-Renting Terms in American Samoa Leases
bodyText: Some places set statutory rules on fire or storm damage and on a landlord's duty to re-rent after a tenant leaves early, and say whether a lease may change them. American Samoa has neither: we found no statute, regulation or court rule giving either side casualty rights (`edu-casualty-termination-as`) or imposing a duty to mitigate by re-renting (`edu-landlord-remedies-termination-as`), so there is no statutory right for a lease to waive and both questions are left to the lease and the common law (case law not searched). Three limits still apply whatever the lease says. No statute lets the lease remove the tenant's defence that your breach excused the rent, so treat it as beyond the lease's reach (case law not searched). Accelerated future rent is not "rent due" for a nonpayment possession case, so a clause making all remaining rent due on default does not let you evict for it. And if the Consumer Protection Act reaches residential leases, a court could strike a grossly one-sided term. The cautious course is the library's casualty clause (`casualty-termination-as`) and claiming future rent only as damages after you have tried to re-let.

title: Children in the Household
bodyText: We found no American Samoa statute, regulation or court rule that requires a lease to address occupancy by children or that limits how many children may live in a rental, but the federal Fair Housing Act reaches American Samoa and governs. You may not refuse to rent to a household, set different terms or rules, or advertise a preference because the household includes children under 18, someone who is pregnant, or someone getting custody of a child. The Act's narrow small-owner exemptions (`edu-fair-housing-as`) can lift the refusal and different-terms rules for a few landlords, but never the ban on discriminatory statements and advertisements.
