The Act does not limit reasonable government restrictions on the maximum number of occupants; a limit you set yourself is not covered by that wording, so keep it reasonable for the home's size and apply it to every household (federal guidance and case law not searched); the territory amended the 1964 Uniform Building Code's occupant table to 100 square feet per occupant for dwellings, but the code book is not in our sources, so we could not confirm how that figure applies (`edu-permitted-occupants-as`). Housing for older persons that meets the federal definition is exempt from the familial-status rule. List every occupant, including children, in the lease (`permitted-occupants`) and write pool, balcony and noise rules the same for every household.

title: Confession of Judgment Clauses in American Samoa
bodyText: We found no American Samoa statute, regulation or court rule that authorizes, or expressly bans, a lease clause in which the tenant confesses judgment or authorizes someone to enter judgment against the tenant without a lawsuit. Don't use one. Under the court rules a civil action begins only when a complaint is filed, a default judgment needs written notice of the application, in English and in Samoan, at least 10 days before the hearing, and possession is recovered through a court case: the summary possession procedure starts with a written demand, and after a judgment for nonpayment the tenant has a statutory right to stop the writ by paying the judgment amount and costs, which no lease term can remove. A confessed judgment would bypass all of those protections, and if the Consumer Protection Act reaches residential leases a court could treat it as unconscionable.

title: The Consumer Protection Act and Your Lease
bodyText: American Samoa's Consumer Protection Act bars deceptive and unconscionable practices by a supplier in a consumer transaction, and a "supplier" includes a lessor. The Act must be construed liberally to protect consumers, but whether it reaches a residential lease is unsettled: a consumer transaction is a sale, lease or other disposition of goods, a service or an intangible for personal, family or household purposes, and real property is not named (case law not searched). Treat it as applying. The Act's list of deceptive practices includes misrepresenting what is offered, saying something is needed when it is not, and any other misleading or false promise; a court weighing unconscionability looks at, among other things, a price grossly above the market, taking advantage of a consumer who cannot understand the language of the agreement, and terms excessively one-sided in the supplier's favour. The Act does not list leaving blanks at signing or failing to give a copy of the contract. A consumer may sue for actual damages or $100, whichever is greater, and the Bureau of Consumer Protection may seek injunctions, restitution, civil penalties of up to $10,000 per wilful violation, and orders striking unconscionable clauses. So describe the home and its terms accurately, explain the lease in Samoan where the tenant needs it, and keep terms balanced (`edu-unconscionability-as`).

title: Keeping Domestic Violence Information Confidential
bodyText: We found no American Samoa statute, regulation or court rule that requires a private landlord to keep confidential what a tenant tells you about domestic or family violence, or that creates an address-confidentiality program. Territorial confidentiality rules we found protect information held by government (human-trafficking victims) or by the health department (HIV records), not landlords. If your rental is assisted under a covered federal housing program (for example Section 8 assistance or the low-income housing tax credit), the federal Violence Against Women Act applies by its own terms: anything a tenant or applicant gives you to show they are a victim, including the fact that they are a victim, must be kept confidential, not put in a shared database, and disclosed only with their written consent, for an eviction case under that Act, or as other law requires. In any rental, the cautious course is to follow the same practice: keep such information in a separate locked or protected file, share it only with staff who need it, and never tell other tenants or the abuser (`edu-dv-eviction-protection-as`).

title: Tenants' Calls for Police or Emergency Help
bodyText: We found no American Samoa statute, regulation or court rule that gives tenants a specific right to call police or emergency services that a lease cannot waive, or that limits penalizing a tenant or household for such calls; we also found no nuisance rule that penalizes a property for repeated police calls. Don't put any lease term in that discourages a tenant from calling for help. Three rules point the same way. The territorial domestic violence law requires police responding to a domestic violence call to protect the victim and tell the victim of the right to ask for protection. Ending a tenancy primarily as retribution for a lawful act arising out of the tenancy is a defence to possession, and summoning help can be such an act (case law not searched). And in housing under a covered federal program, the Violence Against Women Act says an incident of domestic violence is not a serious lease violation or good cause to end the victim's tenancy.

title: Eviction Penalty Clauses in American Samoa
bodyText: We found no American Samoa statute, regulation or court rule that specifically voids, or specifically allows, a lease clause charging the tenant a fee or penalty because you served a demand, filed a possession case or won one. Other rules reach most such clauses. Raising a tenant's obligations as a penalty for a lawful act, and then ending the tenancy because the tenant did not meet them, is a defence to possession. A charge added to overdue rent may count as interest or a fee under the usury law, which forfeits the whole debt if the legal rate is exceeded (unsettled; case law not searched). Court costs follow the judgment, and attorney's fees rest on the lease and common law (`edu-attorney-fees-as`). A penalty unrelated to your real loss may not be enforced at common law (case law not searched), and the Consumer Protection Act may reach a one-sided term. So don't add an eviction or demand fee: claim your actual damages, court costs and any reasonable, mutual attorney's fees in the possession case.

title: Liability Disclaimers in American Samoa Leases
bodyText: We found no American Samoa statute, regulation or court rule that voids, or expressly allows, a residential lease term saying the landlord is not liable for injury or damage, or making the tenant hold the landlord harmless. The only liability limits in the law are for the Power Authority and other utilities in their own service rules. Whether a lease may exempt you from your own negligence rests on the common law that American Samoa adopts, and possibly on the Consumer Protection Act's unconscionability rule if that Act reaches residential leases (case law not searched). The cautious course: don't rely on a disclaimer of your own negligence. American Samoa uses the library's clauses that allocate risk without one, such as tenant property insurance (`tenants-property-insurance-ks-oh-ca`), parking (`parking-ks-oh-ca`), storage (`storage-space-ks-oh-ca`) and services and utilities (`services-utilities-provided-ks-oh`); keep the property safe and carry your own liability insurance instead.

title: Fair Housing in American Samoa
bodyText: The federal Fair Housing Act reaches American Samoa and is the main fair housing law there. You may not refuse to rent, set different terms, misstate availability or make any statement or advertisement showing a preference because of race, color, religion, sex, disability, familial status (children under 18 or pregnancy) or national origin, and you may not threaten or interfere with anyone exercising those rights. Its exemptions are narrow: an owner of no more than three single-family houses renting one without a broker or agent, and rooms or units in an owner-occupied building for no more than four families, neither of which covers the ban on discriminatory statements and advertisements; dwellings a religious organization (or a nonprofit it operates, supervises or controls) owns or runs other than for a commercial purpose, which it may limit to or prefer for persons of the same religion unless membership in that religion is restricted by race, color or national origin; lodgings that a private club not in fact open to the public owns or operates and provides as an incident to its primary purpose, other than for a commercial purpose, which it may limit to or prefer for its members; and, for the familial-status rule only, qualifying housing for older persons. American Samoa adds one territorial rule: no person who tests HIV positive may be denied housing because of it, and that rule has no stated exemption. We found no other territorial housing-discrimination statute (for example on marital status, age or source of income), no territorial fair housing agency, and no real estate licensing law; the territorial constitution has no equal protection clause, according to a case note (case law not searched). A complaint under the federal Act can be filed with HUD; the Act's lawsuit provisions are not in our sources, so take advice on where a court case may be brought. Apply the same screening criteria, terms and rules to every applicant and tenant, and keep your advertising neutral.

title: Hunting on Leased Land in American Samoa
bodyText: We found no American Samoa statute, regulation or court rule on whether a tenant of farm or other leased land may hunt or fish on it, or that requires the owner's written permission. Hunting itself is closely regulated: everyone who hunts needs a hunting licence, the Department's annual proclamation sets seasons, hunting areas, fees and bag limits, any taking of wildlife not allowed by the proclamation or other law is prohibited, and commercial hunting of flying foxes is banned. If you lease land and want to allow or forbid hunting, trapping or fishing, say so in the lease; a permission in the lease does not replace the tenant's licence. Firearm rules are strict as well (`edu-firearms-as`).

title: Building and Fire Code Standard in American Samoa
bodyText: American Samoa has no fire code for residential buildings: we found no adopted fire code, life-safety code or housing code in its statutes, regulations or court rules. The building standard is the Uniform Building Code, Short Form, 1964 Edition, adopted by statute with territorial amendments, and administered by the Department of Public Works' building official; new buildings need a written building application and a completion inspection for whether the building is safe for occupancy, and the Zoning Board hears appeals from building-code decisions. The 1964 code book itself is not in the sources we searched, so we cannot tell you what it requires for exits, alarms, railings or fire separation, and we did not guess. The Power Authority's rules require service grounding to the most current National Electrical Code, and it will not serve a building the government has not inspected and certified. The code has not been moved or replaced: its last amendment was in 1969, and none of the uncompiled laws through 2025 changes it. Ask the Department of Public Works which standards it applies to your building, and keep your completion inspection record.

title: No Fire Sprinkler Requirement Found for American Samoa Rentals
bodyText: We found no American Samoa statute, regulation or court rule that requires fire sprinklers in residential rentals, or a sprinkler retrofit in existing buildings; the territory has no fire code. The 1964 Uniform Building Code (Short Form) adopted by statute governs construction, but its text is not in the sources we searched, so we could not check whether it required sprinklers in any type of residential building built under it; ask the Department of Public Works when you build or substantially alter. If your building has sprinklers, keep them maintained: the Power Authority's fire-protection water rates cover only hydrant use by the fire and police departments, a customer must test and maintain any private hydrant under its control, and the water-system backflow rules can require a backflow device on the connection in some cases (Class 1 and Class 2 sprinkler systems are exempt from the AS-EPA rule). Nothing requires you to tell tenants (`edu-no-sprinkler-disclosure-as`).

title: Land Ownership Limits and Leasing in American Samoa
bodyText: American Samoa has no foreign-adversary or alien land law of the kind some states have, but its land law restricts ownership by ancestry and by corporations, and those rules reach leasing. Land other than freehold land may not be sold, given or otherwise alienated to a person with less than one-half Samoan blood, and communal (native) land may be alienated by a matai only with the Governor's written approval; an alienation in breach is void, and a nonnative who breaks the chapter forfeits the improvements he made to the landowner. Leasing is treated differently: communal land may, with the Governor's approval, be leased "to any person" for up to 55 years (`edu-communal-land-lease-approval-as`), so an approved lease is lawful whatever the tenant's ancestry. Whether a lease of individually owned land to a person of less than one-half Samoan blood is an "alienation" is unsettled (case law not searched); take advice before a long lease of such land to such a tenant. Corporations are a separate trap: no corporation, local or foreign, may acquire any interest in land unless the Governor approves the transaction in writing and the Territorial Registrar records it, and until then it has no effect. A lease is an interest in land, so a lease to a company tenant (for example an employer renting staff housing) should go to the Governor for approval and be recorded. A foreign investor permit gives no right to own land.

title: Which Code Edition Applies in American Samoa
bodyText: American Samoa's building standards are frozen at named editions, and no statute adopts later editions automatically; the exceptions are in the Power Authority's service rules, which require service grounding to the most current National Electrical Code, let the Authority refuse service for noncompliance with the most current National Electrical Safety Code or National Electrical Code, and, where the Authority requires plumbing changes to prevent backflow, require the latest edition of the plumbing code they name, so ask the Power Authority which editions it applies. The statute adopts the Uniform Building Code, Short Form, 1964 Edition, with territorial amendments, last changed in 1969. A 1979 regulation adds the ASHRAE 90-75 energy standard, applied to the design and construction of new public buildings and treated as part of the building code. The hazardous materials rules incorporate a named federal asbestos worker-protection regulation by reference. We found no residential housing or fire code at all. So the edition that applies to a private rental's construction is the 1964 code, unless the Department of Public Works applies something else in practice; its text is not in our sources, so ask the Department what it enforces before you build or renovate.

title: Waiving Habitability in an American Samoa Lease
bodyText: American Samoa has no statutory habitability standard for private rentals, so there is no statutory habitability requirement for a written agreement to remove, and no rule letting a tenant accept named conditions for a rent reduction (`edu-no-habitability-waiver-rule-as`). Whether the common law implies a habitability warranty, and whether a lease can exclude it, is not settled by any statute (case law not searched). Public-law duties bind you whatever the lease says, such as the rodent and sanitation duties on every owner, lessee or occupant of a building and the unsafe-building rule, and the tenant's defence that your breach of the lease excused the rent comes from statute, which does not let a lease waive it, so treat it as beyond the lease's reach (case law not searched). If you and the tenant agree that a known defect will not be repaired in return for lower rent, describe the condition and the reduction in writing, keep it to items that do not affect health or safety, and remember that a court may strike a grossly one-sided term if the Consumer Protection Act reaches the lease.

title: Immigration Status and Renting in American Samoa
bodyText: American Samoa runs its own immigration system, and we found no American Samoa statute, regulation or court rule that bars a landlord from asking about immigration status, that protects immigrant tenants as a class, or that makes it a crime to rent to someone without lawful status. Three sets of rules matter. Guest workers: a guest worker permit for cannery or call-center work needs a host who certifies that they will house the worker; a host who charges rent must give the Attorney General a copy of the host's business licence and a written rent agreement stating the term, monthly rent and facilities; no one may host more than 5 guest workers at a time; and a host may not coerce a worker into paying more than the agreed rent (a felony). The worker's employer-sponsor must make provision for the worker's debts, including utilities, and must make sure the worker leaves American Samoa as soon as the job ends, so tie the lease term to the permit and keep the sponsor's details on file. Other sponsored residents: a sponsor answers for the alien's public debts, not private rent, and a sponsored person generally may remain up to 20 days after sponsorship ends (up to 45 days where a court has specifically found domestic or family violence by the sponsor or the sponsor's household or family members, and until judgment in any case the person has pending against the sponsor). Finally, the federal Fair Housing Act bars treating applicants differently because of national origin, so if you ask about status or identity, ask every applicant the same way.

title: Jury Waivers: No Civil Jury in American Samoa
bodyText: Don't put a jury-waiver clause in an American Samoa lease: there is no civil jury for it to waive. The Code provides jury trial in the High Court's Trial Division only for a person charged with an offense punishable by more than 6 months in prison (and in the District Court for offenses of 6 months to a year), and the civil procedure rules on demanding a jury are omitted, so landlord-tenant cases are decided by the judges. We found no statute treating jury or class-action waivers in standard-form contracts as unconscionable. If you use a multi-state lease, delete or leave untagged any jury-waiver paragraph.

title: No Penalty for Using a Prohibited Lease Term in American Samoa
bodyText: We found no American Samoa statute, regulation or court rule that imposes a money penalty on a landlord for knowingly using a lease that contains a prohibited term; American Samoa has no list of prohibited lease terms to trigger one (`edu-prohibited-lease-terms-as`). Two penalties can still follow from what a lease charges or how it is used. The usury law makes anyone who extends credit and takes interest, fees or minimum charges above the legal rate guilty of a misdemeanour and forfeits the whole debt to the debtor, which could reach an interest or fee term on overdue rent (unsettled; case law not searched). And if the Consumer Protection Act reaches residential leases, a tenant harmed by a deceptive or unconscionable practice may recover actual damages or $100, whichever is greater, and the Bureau may seek civil penalties of up to $10,000 per wilful violation. Keep any interest at or below 15% a year in a signed lease, and leave out terms you could not enforce.

title: Rights an American Samoa Lease Should Not Try to Waive
bodyText: American Samoa has no residential landlord-tenant act, so there is no single list of tenant rights a lease may not waive; we found no statute, regulation or court rule declaring lease waivers of tenant rights void. The rights that come from statute should still be treated as beyond the lease's reach, because no statute allows them to be waived: the written demand and its service before a possession case; the court process itself (no lock-outs, utility shut-offs or removal of belongings, and entry only if permitted by law and never with force); the retaliation and rent-excusing-breach defences; and, after a nonpayment judgment, the tenant's right to stop the writ by paying the judgment amount and costs within the time allowed. A case note under the demand section suggests a party may waive the demand rules that protect it (a lead only; case law not searched), but don't rely on a lease waiver of them. Federal rights that reach the territory, such as fair housing and servicemember protections, apply whatever the lease says; the federal servicemember law has its own rules on written waivers, which are not in our sources, so don't put a waiver of those rights in the lease. Write the lease so these protections stand.

title: Plain Language and Samoan in American Samoa Leases
bodyText: We found no American Samoa plain-language or consumer-contract statute that reaches residential leases: nothing sets a readability test, requires the lease to be divided and captioned by sections, or requires a front-page statement of landlord-protective terms. Samoan and English are both official languages, and many notices the law requires must be in both, including the court summons in a possession case and notice of a default-judgment application, but no statute requires a private lease to be in Samoan. The Consumer Protection Act, if it reaches residential leases, treats taking advantage of a consumer's inability to understand the language of an agreement as a sign of unconscionability. So use plain, short sentences, and if your tenant reads Samoan more easily than English, give a Samoan translation or explain the lease in Samoan and note in the lease that you did.

title: No Required Consumer Statement in American Samoa Leases
bodyText: We found no American Samoa statute, regulation or court rule that requires a residential lease to carry a statement of consumer restrictions listing every waiver or landlord-protective term, to pass a readability test, or that offers Attorney General pre-approval of a lease form; there is no dollar threshold to check because there is no such law (`edu-plain-language-as`). The closest rules are bilingual notice duties in other fields, such as the English-and-Samoan statement auto repair shops must print for customers. You need not add a consumer statement, but a short plain-language summary of the main tenant obligations, in English and Samoan where useful, helps show the tenant understood the terms if the Consumer Protection Act is ever raised.

title: Pool Safety Rules for American Samoa Rentals
bodyText: We found no American Samoa statute, regulation or court rule that requires a residential landlord to fence a pool, install barriers or alarms, post safety rules or give tenants a pool safety notice, and no health regulation on pools at apartments or rental homes. The Director of Health has authority to make regulations on bathing and swimming places and on the health conditions of buildings and pools, but we found none adopted. If your rental has a pool, the cautious course is a self-closing, self-latching gate and a fence around it, posted rules (no lifeguard, no diving where shallow, children supervised), regular water treatment, and rules applied the same way to every household so that adults-only pool hours don't treat families with children unequally under the federal Fair Housing Act. Liability for a drowning or injury rests on the common law (case law not searched). Taking a large quantity of water to fill a pool needs arrangements with the water utility first.

title: Lease Terms American Samoa Law Limits
bodyText: American Samoa has no list of prohibited residential lease terms; we found no statute, regulation or court rule that voids confession-of-judgment, exculpation, indemnity or fee-shifting clauses as such, penalizes knowingly using a forbidden term, bars passing home-warranty or repair charges to tenants, or voids a lease because of when it was handed over. Specific laws still limit what a lease can do. Possession comes only through the court after a written demand, so no lock-out, utility shut-off or self-help removal clause works (`edu-self-help-eviction-as`). The retaliation and rent-excusing-breach defences, and the tenant's right to stop a nonpayment writ by paying the judgment and costs, come from statute and no statute lets the lease waive them (`edu-nonwaivable-rights-as`). Accelerated rent is not "rent due" for a nonpayment case. Interest above 6% a year needs the tenant's signature and may never exceed 15%, and charging interest or fees above the legal rate forfeits the whole debt. A jury waiver has nothing to act on (`edu-no-jury-waiver-as`). Leases of communal land need the Governor's approval and a lease to a corporation needs approval and recording (`edu-foreign-ownership-as`). And the Consumer Protection Act, if it reaches residential leases, lets a court strike unconscionable clauses (`edu-unconscionability-as`); disclaimers of your own negligence are the riskiest (`edu-exculpatory-clauses-as`), and a confessed judgment should never be used (`edu-no-confession-of-judgment-as`).

title: Questions You Should Not Ask Applicants
bodyText: We found no American Samoa statute, regulation or court rule that separately bans asking applicants about, or keeping records of, protected characteristics. The federal Fair Housing Act, which reaches American Samoa, makes it unlawful to make any statement in connection with renting a dwelling that indicates a preference, limitation or discrimination based on race, color, religion, sex, disability, familial status or national origin, and a question on an application form or at a showing can be such a statement. Territorially, no one who tests HIV positive may be denied housing because of it. So don't ask about race, religion, national origin, pregnancy or plans for children, disability or medical conditions, or HIV status; ask every applicant the same questions about income, rental history and identity; and keep any information you do learn out of your decision.

title: Registered Sex Offenders as Tenants in American Samoa
bodyText: We found no American Samoa statute, regulation or court rule that restricts where a registered sex offender may live (no distance limit from schools or parks), limits offenders living together, or makes it a crime to lease to an offender; nor any lease-statement safe harbour. American Samoa's registry law works through registration instead: a registered offender must appear in person at the Attorney General's Office immediately to update a change of residence, and the public registry website shows offenders' residential addresses, with a warning that the information must not be used to harass anyone named or living at a reported address. One crime can reach a landlord: knowingly harbouring, or helping to harbour, a sex offender who is in violation of the registration law. If you learn a tenant has not registered the address, don't hide them; you may tell the Attorney General's Office. Treat screening for sex offences the same way for every applicant (`edu-tenant-screening-as`).

title: Renting Homes in Single Dwelling Zones
bodyText: We found no American Samoa statute, regulation or court rule that limits renting out a home in a single dwelling zone, or requires the owner to live on the lot, and no short-term rental rule. The territorial zoning law regulates the use, not who occupies it: a one-family dwelling is a permitted use in a single dwelling (R1) zone whether the owner or a tenant lives there. Two limits follow from the zoning definitions. A one-family dwelling contains only one dwelling unit, so dividing an R1 house into separate rental units is not a listed R1 use (`edu-accessory-dwelling-unit-as`). And a building rented to transient guests for sleeping is defined as a hotel, so renting a house for short stays may be treated as a hotel use rather than a dwelling (unsettled; case law not searched) and may bring in the hotel room tax (`hotel-occupancy-tax-as`). Village councils may have their own rules, which are not published (`edu-usufructuary-lessor-as`).

title: Housing Vouchers and Source of Income in American Samoa
bodyText: We found no American Samoa statute, regulation or court rule that bars refusing a tenant because of the source of their income or because they would pay with a housing voucher or other rent subsidy, or that requires you to accept vouchers or to state a policy in the lease; the federal Fair Housing Act does not list source of income either. We also found no territorial housing-voucher program in the corpus; federal housing programs operate through their own contracts. If you join a federal assistance program, its contract and federal rules govern, and the Violence Against Women Act protections apply to that tenancy. Whatever your policy, apply it to every applicant: a voucher or income rule used only against some groups can still be a federal fair housing violation, and an income test should look at the tenant's share of the rent consistently.

title: Steam Radiator Covers: Not Applicable in American Samoa
bodyText: Not applicable in American Samoa. The territory has a tropical climate with no heating season and no heating requirement for dwellings (`edu-heating-na-as`), and we found no American Samoa statute, regulation or court rule on steam heat, radiators or radiator covers in homes; the only boiler and steam rules are the Board of Marine Inspectors' inspection of vessels and of boilers and pressure vessels generally, air permits and contractor licensing. No radiator-cover rider belongs in an American Samoa lease.

title: Voucher Program Inspections in American Samoa
bodyText: We found no American Samoa statute, regulation or court rule that addresses refusing to rent because a housing-assistance program will inspect the unit, or that sets a deadline for program approval. Because American Samoa also has no source-of-income protection (`edu-no-source-of-income-protection-as`), declining to join a program, or to allow its inspection, is not itself unlawful under territorial law. If you do take an assisted tenant, the program's contract governs inspections and the federal Violence Against Women Act applies to the tenancy. Apply any program policy the same way to every applicant, so that it can't be challenged as a cover for discrimination under the federal Fair Housing Act.

title: Keeping Tenants' Information Private in American Samoa
bodyText: We found no American Samoa statute, regulation or court rule that bars a private landlord from disclosing a tenant's or applicant's personal information, requires written consent before you share it, or sets data-security or breach-notice duties for private businesses (`edu-tenant-records-as`). The territorial privacy rules we found bind government bodies (health information, HIV records, crime victims). Two federal duties can reach you: in housing under a covered federal program, information showing a tenant is a victim of domestic violence must be kept confidential (`edu-dv-confidentiality-as`), and federal consumer-reporting law (not in our sources) governs how you obtain and use a credit report. The cautious course is to collect only what you need, keep Social Security numbers and bank details locked or encrypted, share tenant information only with your staff, lawyers or a court as needed, and get the tenant's written consent before giving references or information to anyone else.

title: Housing Employees in American Samoa
bodyText: We found no American Samoa statute, regulation or court rule that requires a private employer-landlord to give an employee-occupant a signed statement of occupancy and vacating conditions, or to offer a rental agreement when the job ends. The rules that exist: Government housing, under its own chapter, is limited to government contract specialists and certain local hires, ends 30 days after the contract ends or after notice, and is recovered by the Attorney General in the District Court; that chapter governs only the Government as landlord. For a private employer, the possession statute's "lease" includes a written or verbal licence to use premises, so an employee who stays after the right to occupy ends can be removed through the summary possession procedure after a written demand, never by self-help. The minimum-wage law lets the Wage and Hour Board count the reasonable cost of lodging an employer customarily furnishes as part of wages and regulate charges to employees for lodging, so check the Board's rules before deducting rent from pay. Guest-worker hosts who charge rent must submit a business licence and a written rent agreement with the worker's permit application, and a sponsor must ensure a guest worker leaves when the job ends (`edu-immigration-status-as`). Put the occupancy terms, the rent or wage credit, and what happens when employment ends in a signed writing.

title: Tenant Organizing in American Samoa
bodyText: We found no American Samoa statute, regulation or court rule that protects tenants' right to form or join a tenant association, to meet in common areas, or to distribute information, or that bars a landlord from interfering with organizing. The territorial constitution protects the right of the people peaceably to assemble against government action, not private landlords. One statutory protection reaches it indirectly: a court may not give you possession if you ended the tenancy primarily as retribution for a lawful act arising out of the tenancy, and joining with other tenants to raise repair or rent concerns is likely such an act (case law not searched). Don't end or refuse to renew a tenancy, or raise rent, because a tenant organized or complained.

title: Screening Applicants in American Samoa
bodyText: We found no American Samoa statute, regulation or court rule that regulates tenant screening as such: no limit on criminal-history checks or look-back periods, no rule that criminal history may be checked only after a conditional offer, no cap on minimum-income tests, no screening-criteria notice and no negligence shield for renting to someone with a record (`edu-no-application-fee-rule-as`). The limits that apply: the federal Fair Housing Act bars screening that treats applicants differently, or uses criteria or questions that show a preference, because of race, color, religion, sex, disability, familial status or national origin; American Samoa bars denying housing to someone because they test HIV positive; and a person whose juvenile record has been sealed may lawfully say no record exists. Federal consumer-reporting law governs credit reports but is not in our sources. Write your criteria down (income, rental history, references, any criminal-history rule tied to safety), apply them to every applicant, and keep the reasons for each decision.

title: Unconscionable Lease Terms in American Samoa
bodyText: American Samoa's only unconscionability statute is in the Consumer Protection Act, which must be construed liberally to protect consumers: an unconscionable act or practice by a supplier in a consumer transaction violates the Act, unconscionability is a question of law for the court, and the court may strike or limit unconscionable contract clauses. Whether a residential lease is a consumer transaction is unsettled (case law not searched), so assume the Act applies. The court looks at things such as taking advantage of a consumer who could not protect their interests because of infirmity, ignorance, illiteracy or inability to understand the language of the agreement, a price grossly above what similar housing costs, and terms excessively one-sided in your favour. Outside the Act, unconscionability is a common-law contract defence (case law not searched). We found no statute that lets a court revise or end a lease for unforeseen hardship, and none declaring any particular lease clause enforceable notwithstanding unconscionability. The price-gouging law separately caps rent increases on month-to-month housing at 10% from a declared emergency until 30 days after it (longer if the Governor extends it), unless you can prove a larger increase comes directly from added costs, within the statute's cost-plus-markup limit, and bars offering anything for rent at an unconscionable price around and during the emergency (`edu-rent-control-as`).

title: No Landlord Incentive for Renting to Veterans in American Samoa
bodyText: We found no American Samoa statute, regulation or court rule that gives private landlords a tax credit, payment, deposit guarantee or other incentive for renting to veterans, or that requires a preference for veterans in private housing. Territorial veterans' rules we found concern government employment: preference points in civil-service examinations and related personnel rules. Federal programs that help veterans with rent run under their own contracts and are not in our sources. Federal servicemember protections, such as the right of active-duty tenants to end a lease on qualifying orders, are a separate matter covered in the library's military lease-termination rows.

title: Water Heater Temperature in American Samoa Rentals
bodyText: We found no American Samoa statute, regulation or court rule that requires a landlord to set a water heater to a maximum temperature, at each new tenancy or at any time, and no energy or building rule on individual water heaters in dwellings; American Samoa has no heating or hot-water requirement for rentals (`edu-heating-na-as`). The only water-heater rule we found is the water utility's: every residential customer must install a dual-check backflow device at the meter, and where check valves or similar devices are used the customer must install and maintain a pressure relief valve between them and the water heater. The cautious course is to set any water heater you supply at about 120°F (49°C) before each tenant moves in, keep its pressure relief valve working, and list it in the lease (`appliances-included`).

title: No Window Guard Requirement in American Samoa
bodyText: We found no American Samoa statute, regulation or court rule that requires window guards or window stops in rentals where children live, or a window-guard notice or lease rider. The building law adopted by statute, the 1964 Uniform Building Code (Short Form), is not in the sources we searched, so we could not check its window or sill-height standards; a building application must show the number, locations and dimensions of windows. If young children will live in an upper-floor unit, the cautious course is to offer window stops or guards that still allow emergency exit, and to apply that offer to every family the same way. Liability for a fall rests on the common law (case law not searched).

title: Checks Marked 'Paid in Full'
bodyText: American Samoa has not adopted the Uniform Commercial Code. Its negotiable-instruments law is the older Uniform Negotiable Instruments Law (A.S.C.A. § 27.2503), which has no rule on checks marked 'paid in full', so whether cashing one settles a disputed claim is a common-law question; under the traditional rule, cashing a check offered in full satisfaction of a genuinely disputed claim can settle it. No American Samoa case has been reviewed, and the Code text read is the Bar Association's, current to August 2021. The cautious course: don't cash a check for less than you claim that is marked as payment in full of a disputed amount; return it uncashed.

title: Duty of Good Faith
bodyText: American Samoa's landlord-tenant statutes impose no general duty of good faith of the kind in the Uniform Residential Landlord and Tenant Act (American Samoa's summary-possession chapter (it has no residential landlord-tenant act) searched); good faith appears only in specific rules. Courts in many states read a covenant of good faith and fair dealing into every contract, a lease included; whether and how American Samoa's courts do is case law this library has not reviewed, so act as if the duty applies. In practice: give notices, enter, handle the deposit, enforce lease terms and end a tenancy honestly and for the purpose the law or the lease gives you the right, not as a pretext.
